news.Title: Billionaire Ray Dalio Is Going All-In on AI and Chip Stocks: Top 5 Holdings
news.Content:
Speaking at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on October 7, Ray Dalio was of the opinion that the AI boom had entered a "classic bubble," and that there was a distinction between "how terrific a technology is and how terrific an investment is." Gain insight into the AI sector through our list of the AI Stocks Dominating List of Biggest Winners .

He further told the Forbes event that the changing circumstances and rising rates had not yet resulted in "a negative effect on other things", but that, at the same time, it does not elevate the pressure for interest rates to balloon even further. He said the AI bubble could begin to burst once higher borrowing costs started having an impact, adding that he believed markets were approaching that point.

READ ALSO: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller's New AI Warning and Top 10 Stock Picks

Dalio has been developing this argument throughout 2026. In January, he warned that the AI boom was in the early stages of a bubble, after a prolonged rally in technology stocks. His broader concerns extended to the uncertainty surrounding Fed policy and productivity growth, adding that he believed the newly appointed Fed chair and FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) at the time were likely to be biased to push nominal and real interest rates down. This, according to him, could be supportive of prices and inflate bubbles. For more insight, read our recently published article on the top 10 stocks to buy according to billionaire Ken Fisher .

But Dalio is far from dismissing AI's economic promise. In a September discussion published by the World Economic Forum, he argued that both the optimists and pessimists could be right. He believes that AI is following the same path as other transformative technologies throughout history, ranging from railroads to the internet, as they all tend to produce bubbles. AI is no different from them, according to Ray, and how the technology is managed by societies would eventually help determine how the advantages and disadvantages are shared.

So, what are the best AI and chip stocks billionaire Ray Dalio is going all-in on? We provided the expanded list of the top 10 holdings here . The top 5 stocks are provided below.

Our Methodology

For this list, we shortlisted stocks owned by Ray Dalio's Bridgewater Associates. We prioritized well-known companies that are also popular among hedge funds and analysts. The stocks are ranked in ascending order of their analyst upside potential.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Story Continues

Recently, we created a video looking at the 10 stocks billionaires Dalio and Laffont love. You can click below to see these stocks in our video on YouTube:

Billionaire Ray Dalio Is Going All-In on AI and Chip Stocks: Top 10 Holdings

5. NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA )

Analyst Upside: 59.27%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 280

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) remains one of the most direct ways for investors to gain exposure to the expansion of AI computing infrastructure. Its accelerated computing platforms support the training and deployment of sophisticated AI models, while its networking technologies and software contribute to the broader systems used in data centers.

The company's November 17, 2026 earnings release revealed the extraordinary scale of demand. Third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue reached $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, while Data Center revenue rose 110% to $107.6 billion. NVIDIA also reported that its Vera Rubin NVL72 computing platform had begun shipping.

READ MORE: 10 Stocks Defying Tech Market Turmoil

The larger investment opportunity extends beyond supplying individual processors. NVIDIA's strategy encompasses integrated computing systems designed to address the demanding performance requirements of increasingly complex AI applications. For investors, NVIDIA's ability to maintain its technological advantage and generate attractive margins will matter just as much as the overall growth of the AI infrastructure market.

4. Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMAT )

Analyst Upside: 69.65%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 129

Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) is positioned to benefit from the increasing sophistication of semiconductor manufacturing. Its equipment and technologies support the production of advanced chips, making it an important supplier as manufacturers invest in more capable processors and memory.

The company's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results demonstrated strong demand for its technologies. Revenue increased 53% year over year to $10.41 billion, while fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $34.45 billion, up 21% year over year. Its quarterly GAAP gross margin stood at 50.4%. Applied Materials also generated $8.87 billion in operating cash flow during the fiscal year, giving investors another measure of the financial performance supporting its semiconductor equipment operations.

READ ALSO: 10 High P/E Stocks Under the 200-Day SMA

The company's strength lies in the range of manufacturing processes its products address. Rather than depending on a single chip architecture, Applied Materials supplies technologies used across different stages of semiconductor production, and this creates exposure to increasingly complex manufacturing requirements, although it does not eliminate the industry's cyclicality.

Capital investment by semiconductor manufacturers remains an important determinant of equipment demand. The central issue for shareholders is whether technology-driven spending can sustain profitable growth beyond periods of especially strong equipment investment.

3. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX )

Analyst Upside: 74.29%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 122

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) supplies semiconductor manufacturing equipment used in processes such as deposition and etching. Its technologies are important to producing increasingly complex chips, including the advanced logic and memory devices used in AI computing systems.

Lam's September-quarter 2026 results demonstrated substantial operating momentum, with revenue increasing to $8.22 billion, up 22% from the preceding quarter. Lam's opportunity is not limited to an increase in the number of chips manufactured. As semiconductor technology becomes more complex, production can require increasingly demanding manufacturing processes, creating opportunities for specialized equipment suppliers.

DON'T MISS: 10 Best Healthcare and Insurance Stocks To Buy Following the 2026 Democratic Midterm Sweep

Lam's exposure to memory manufacturing also connects its business to the investment required to produce more sophisticated memory devices. Nevertheless, semiconductor equipment spending remains cyclical, and changes in manufacturers' capacity plans can affect orders even when the long-term demand for computing continues to expand.

For investors, Lam's ability to support advanced manufacturing requirements while preserving operating profitability will be central to the company's longer-term investment case.

2. ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ: ASML )

Analyst Upside: 76.41%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 125

ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ:ASML) occupies an important position in the semiconductor supply chain because its extreme ultraviolet lithography systems enable the production of advanced chips. As demand for increasingly powerful AI processors grows, the technical complexity of chip manufacturing makes ASML's equipment particularly significant.

The company's third-quarter 2026 results reflected strong demand. In its October 2026 earnings release, ASML said customer demand was exceeding its planned supply capacity for both 2027 and 2028. Management is consequently exploring additional capacity increases to meet demand. Total net sales for the quarter reached €11.7 billion, with a gross margin of 57.5%. The company now expects full-year 2026 total net sales to be in the €44 billion to €45 billion range, with a gross margin around 56%.

READ ALSO: 10 Unrivaled Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade

ASML's competitive advantage lies in the advanced technology and specialized expertise required to manufacture its lithography systems. Its business also benefits from servicing and upgrading equipment already installed at customer facilities, providing a revenue opportunity beyond new system sales.

However, ASML is exposed to semiconductor manufacturers' capital spending decisions. The important factor for investors to consider is whether the increasingly demanding manufacturing requirements of advanced semiconductors can sustain equipment demand through the industry's cyclical fluctuations.

1. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU )

Analyst Upside: 128.12%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 169

Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) offers exposure to an essential part of AI computing that receives less attention than processors: memory. High-performance computing systems require substantial memory capacity and bandwidth, making advanced memory technologies important to the operation of AI infrastructure.

The company's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results showed revenue increasing to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, while operating cash flow reached $43.97 billion. Management highlighted AI-related demand and its plans to increase investment in technology, products, and manufacturing capacity. These investments are intended to support the evolving requirements of customers developing advanced computing platforms.

The company's advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory products place it within an important part of the AI supply chain. Reuters reported in September that Micron has increased commitments under its long-term supply agreements to $32 billion, which highlights the demand for AI memory chips. Micron's ability to manage capacity investment while meeting demand for more advanced memory products will be important to sustaining its financial performance.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MU as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Content:

Talen Energy（TLN.US）： 成交價363.74美元，上漲9.26%，開盤360.61美元，盤中高點365.52美元，盤中低點353.95美元，均價361.02美元，成交量7.01萬股。

Talen Energy與一名具投資等級評級的PJM客戶簽下七年期容量合約，將在2029/2030至2035/2036各交付年度銷售750MW容量，預期每年帶來約1億美元收入，主要由Guernsey Power Station提供750MW認可容量。這筆新約的重要性，在於公司把原本受電力市場波動影響較大的獲利來源，進一步轉成可預測的長約現金流。加上先前與AWS的協議，Talen到2036年的已簽約毛利率已提高至40%，未來十年合計約有10億美元容量收入能見度。公司也另外鎖定Guernsey剩餘588MW於2029/2030年度，以及Waterford Energy Center自2029/2030至2031/2032三年共702MW容量，使2029/2030規劃年度總簽約容量超過2GW。

Littelfuse（LFUS.US）： 成交價388.07美元，上漲8.53%，開盤381.11美元，盤中高點392.22美元，盤中低點378.95美元，均價385.37美元，成交量1.72萬股。

Littelfuse最近連續推出兩條新產品線，方向都指向車用電子與空間受限的工業設備。較具代表性的是TP7.0SMD-XC車規級TVS二極體，採用Foldback技術，在小型表面貼裝封裝中提供最高7000W峰值脈衝功率，並維持24V低且平坦的箝位電壓，鎖定ADAS、區域控制單元等低耐壓敏感晶片保護需求，同時通過AEC-Q101認證並支援PPAP流程。另一項更新是C&K SDE系列薄型SMT DIP開關，主打可端對端並排擴充，最高提供12位配置，應用鎖定工業控制面板、保全消防與物聯網裝置。相較只看整體景氣，這兩項新品更直接顯示Littelfuse正把產品重心往高可靠度、車規化與小型化設計深化。

Terex（TEX.US）： 成交價54.33美元，上漲8.13%，開盤51.67美元，盤中高點54.8美元，盤中低點52.1美元，均價53.79美元，成交量9.14萬股。

Terex近期沒有新的財報、併購或重大接單公告，現有資料顯示市場判讀仍圍繞公司轉型是否能落實到獲利結構改善。較具體的觀察點，是Terex是否能達成2026年調整後EBITDA9.65億美元目標，以及把營收結構由波動較大的設備銷售，逐步轉向更穩定的業務來源。現階段外界主要檢視三件事，包括既有訂單能否持續轉成營收、併購後成本協同是否如期發揮，以及高毛利、低波動業務占比能否提高。也就是說，Terex當前最值得追蹤的變化，不是單一新消息，而是轉型進度能否把原本偏週期性的工業設備公司，推向獲利品質更穩的結構。

news.Title: Why Kulicke & Soffa (KLIC) Stock Is Jumping Today: Chip Rally Follows Nvidia CEO News

news.Title: Should You Buy Marvell Technology Stock Before Dec. 1?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) reports its latest earnings numbers at the start of December, and they could be pivotal for a stock that's been volatile in recent weeks. While it's still sitting on some strong gains north of 60% this year, there has been a bit of a pullback of late as the market reacted negatively to news of its planned acquisition of Lumentum Holdings .

A good earnings report and outlook could, however, convince investors that the tech stock is on the right path forward. Should investors buy Marvell's stock before its earnings come out on Dec. 1?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The market may be expecting much more than just a strong quarter

Back in August, when Marvell reported its most recent numbers, its growth rate was 37%, with the company posting record revenue of more than $2.7 billion. For the current quarter, which ended on Oct. 31, Marvell forecasted around $3.2 billion in net revenue, which would translate into a year-over-year growth rate of over 50%.

Effectively, this means that type of growth is already priced into the tech stock . Unless Marvell does better than that, which may not be easy to achieve, the stock may not necessarily get much, if any, boost. Crucially, investors may be looking ahead to the guidance and how strong demand is expected to be for the next quarter.

The challenge these days is that with interest rates on the rise, there may be a bit more of a pullback in tech-related spending in the future, which, in turn, may hurt Marvell's near-term growth prospects. Investors may be looking for confidence that won't be the case. Plus, they may be looking for reasons for management to justify its all-stock deal for Lumentum, which places a massive $115 billion enterprise value on the business.

Thus far, Marvell's management hasn't appeared to have done enough to convince investors that the deal will pay off. There will likely be questions relating to the deal on the earnings call, which may have a big impact on the stock afterward.

Is Marvell's stock worth buying today?

For investors looking to buy Marvell's stock, it may be a good idea to wait until after earnings. As well as what the company does in the upcoming quarter and as rosy as its guidance may be, there's also the Fed meeting that happens a week later. An interest rate hike is widely expected, and it may be even 50 basis points. That could trigger a sharp sell-off in the tech sector, at which point Marvell may be an even more attractive buy.

Story Continues

Currently, it's trading at around 50 times its trailing earnings, which may be justifiable under ideal growth conditions. However, given the state of the economy and the possibility of a pullback in tech spending, investors may want to demand a lower price for Marvell stock before buying it. And the stock's valuation could indeed fall lower in the coming weeks; there's no rush to buy right now.

news.Title: Anthropic stock whipsaws as Monday's tech rally takes off
news.Content:
Just two days after its public debut, the stock market's newest AI giant, Anthropic ( ANT ), looks to be missing out on Monday's major tech rally.

The stock of the Claude model maker fell as much as 2% on Monday, trading below $88 as of 12:20 p.m. ET after earlier whipsawing. Meanwhile, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other AI-linked stocks, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ), soared amid the broader tech rebound that followed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.

The move comes after Anthropic's stock sank 9% on Friday following a 17% gain on its IPO day last Thursday. At Monday's current price, the stock is up about 5% from its $83 IPO price.

The choppy performance might reflect ordinary post IPO profit-taking and broader skepticism about Anthropic's valuation. Needham analysts said in a Sunday note that the most common concern they hear from investors is whether the company can sustain its enormous revenue growth next year. The company's fully diluted IPO valuation of about $1.5 trillion is roughly 40 times trailing sales.

The stock also has a potential supply overhang. As much as 315 million shares held by insiders, roughly one-third of the stock the company issued in its IPO, became eligible for sale almost immediately, according to Anthropic's IPO paperwork.

Needham added that given Anthropic's staggered schedule for permitting insider share sales could bring more shares to market in the first six months.

Another key question hanging over the company is how credit markets will absorb the AI firm's massive spending needs. Anthropic has committed to spending about $900 billion on its computing and infrastructure needs for the next two decades , including $70 billion due over the next 12 months.

The AI boom's ravenous capital needs have flooded the bond market this year, becoming a looming concern for investors.

Investors expect the major rating agencies to assign a high-yield, or junk, rating to the company's debt, according to a Wall Street Journal report . No rating has yet been announced.

Anthropic's credit rating is key for the wider AI ecosystem. Getting the higher investment-grade rating would help offer some relief to chip makers, including Nvidia and Broadcom ( AVGO ), that have guaranteed billions of dollars worth of microchips to customers that lease compute power to major model makers like Anthropic and rival OpenAI. ( OPAI.PVT )

The high-yield bond market also comes with constraints, including smaller capacity and higher borrowing rates, for the newly public giant.

news.Title: Situational Awareness Stock Portfolio: Top 10 Picks
news.Content:
Leopold Aschenbrenner was a university valedictorian at 19, a fired AI researcher at 22, and by 25 the manager of a hedge fund that reportedly peaked near $45 billion.

The Germany-born investor joined the safety team at OpenAI in 2023 and lost the job in April 2024 over an alleged leak of a brainstorming document, which he disputes. Two months later he published a 165-page essay arguing that artificial general intelligence could arrive within a few years and that the race to build it had begun.

How a Viral Essay Became a Hedge Fund

He named his fund, Situational Awareness LP , after the essay and launched it in 2024 with backing from investors including Patrick and John Collison, Daniel Gross, and Nat Friedman. Its core idea was that the bottlenecks of the AI boom would be electricity and computing capacity, not the models themselves.

The bets paid off. By the end of 2025 the fund reported about $5.5 billion in U.S. stock exposure across nearly 30 holdings, and it gained 439% in the first half of 2026. Its assets reportedly swelled to about $45 billion, much of it built on borrowed money. Readers following the theme can find more names in our list of AI infrastructure stocks for the long term .

The Margin Calls That Erased Most of the Fund

Then the AI trade turned. In July 2026, semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks fell, a bet against software stocks went wrong, and lenders demanded more collateral. The fund lost 67% in July, CNBC reported. Before markets opened on July 30, it sold most of a roughly $16 billion public stock book to Citadel , the hedge fund run by billionaire Ken Griffin, at about a 10% discount.

Assets dropped to about $10 billion, mostly private stakes, and Aschenbrenner told investors the fund would stop borrowing against its public holdings. A November 16 filing showed its U.S.-listed holdings had shrunk 92%, to $1.58 billion on September 30 from $20.24 billion at the end of June.

He did not stay out for long. The same filing showed a rebuilt book of AI-linked stocks and call options, which then fell hard in October. Our ranking of the cheapest AI data center stocks according to billionaires shows how other big investors hold the group. On November 18, the Financial Times reported that he was discussing a "Situational Awareness 2.0" with brokers and investors, with a chief risk officer, outside money and possibly leverage again.

Our Methodology

For this article, we reviewed the Q3 2026 13F filing of Situational Awareness LP, the hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, and ranked its holdings by stake value in ascending order. Anthropic, the fund's largest position, was private at quarter-end and is absent from the filing, so we used the stake value reported in the press.

Story Continues

At Insider Monkey, we are obsessed with what hedge funds do. The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Situational Awareness Stock Portfolio: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Picks 10 to 6

10. Fermi (NASDAQ:FRMI)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $11,248,691

Situational Awareness LP owned 2,671,898 shares of Fermi as of September 30, a new position that makes up 0.71% of its portfolio. The stake was valued at $11,248,691.

Fermi is a Dallas-based developer building Project Matador, a power and data center campus in Texas. It sells power and ready-to-build land to AI companies, and it has no revenue yet, so its story rests on tenants.

On November 12, Fermi said an undisclosed investment-grade hyperscaler had agreed to advance 600 megawatts of power capacity beginning in 2027, with more than $200 million committed up front. Chief Executive Officer Lee McIntire said hyperscalers want sites with permitted power, and he called Fermi's head start in getting power a key reason the customer signed.

The report also carried bad news. Fermi lost $141.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 and ended it with about $316 million in cash and restricted cash. A previously announced lease with TensorWave will not move forward, which leaves the new customer as the main commercial win so far. For a skeptic's view, see what Jim Cramer said about Fermi going public .

9. Bitdeer (NASDAQ:BTDR)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $20,294,143

Bitdeer is a Singapore-based company that mines bitcoin and now rents out computing power and data center space for AI. Mining still brought in most of its revenue in the third quarter of 2026, according to the company's report.

Situational Awareness LP held 1,934,618 shares of Bitdeer at the end of September, which is 1.29% of its portfolio. The stake was valued at $20,294,143, and the fund had cut the position by 44% since the end of June.

Bulls like how quickly the AI side is signing contracts. Revenue hit a record $320.7 million, up 89%, adjusted EBITDA rose 173% to $69.6 million, and the AI cloud backlog reached about $2.9 billion. A 16-year, $4.7 billion lease with Volta covers its Tydal site in Norway.

Bears point to a net loss that widened to $125.5 million from $30.1 million. They also point to a new U.S. licensing requirement for advanced chips bound for Malaysia, announced in mid-November, where Bitdeer runs all of its existing AI cloud capacity. Our piece on whether signed demand at its Malaysian site can turn into profit goes deeper.

8. IREN (NASDAQ:IREN)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $21,579,080

IREN runs data centers powered by renewable energy and rents out AI computing capacity from them. It also still mines bitcoin, though that revenue is shrinking fast.

Situational Awareness LP owned 527,864 shares of IREN at the end of September, or 1.37% of its portfolio, after selling most of the position during the third quarter. The stake was valued at $21,579,080.

Bulls got plenty to like in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended September 30. Revenue rose 66% from the previous quarter to $228 million, and AI cloud revenue jumped 182% to $200 million. The net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million. IREN reported a revenue backlog of $20.3 billion, about two-thirds of it from investment-grade customers.

The sour note was timing. IREN moved its target of more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue to January 2027, and possibly February, after a customer-requested design change and supplier delays. It also plans about $15 billion of capital spending in fiscal 2027, and the shares fell 41% in October. For the funding side, see our analysis of IREN's Microsoft contract and its financing .

7. CleanSpark (NASDAQ:CLSK)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $38,885,094

CleanSpark made up 2.47% of Situational Awareness LP's portfolio at the end of September, when the fund held 3,019,029 shares. The stake was valued at $38,885,094, and the fund had cut it by 76% since the end of June.

CleanSpark began as a bitcoin miner and now calls itself a data center developer. It owns sites and power contracts in Georgia, Tennessee, Mississippi, Wyoming and Texas, and it wants to lease them to AI companies.

Bulls point to the lease. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended June 30, CleanSpark signed a 20-year, $6.6 billion triple-net lease at Sandersville, Georgia, with a high investment-grade tenant, and it said the equity portion of the project was fully funded. The catch is that mining revenue is shrinking in the meantime: quarterly revenue fell 30.5% to $138.0 million.

CleanSpark is expected to report its next quarterly results on November 24, and analysts expect a loss of $0.35 per share. Investors will look for news on leasing its other sites. Our look at whether CleanSpark's AI pivot can pay off covers that question.

6. Roundhill Memory ETF (CBOE:DRAM)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $140,337,000

Roundhill launched the fund on April 2, 2026, as the first ETF built around memory and storage makers. It is actively managed and holds companies such as Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, Sandisk and Seagate, partly through swaps. The fund lists 27 holdings in all.

Situational Awareness LP held call options on 2,325,000 shares of the Roundhill Memory ETF at the end of September, a new position that makes up 8.9% of its portfolio. The options were valued at $140,337,000, based on the shares they cover.

The position tells a story about the fund's summer. At the end of June, it owned 4,828,786 Micron shares and 2,495,344 Sandisk shares, which together made up 56% of its portfolio. Both stocks were gone from the September filing, sold in the July fire sale.

The position is a smaller, option-based bet on the same theme, so the fund went from owning memory makers outright to holding calls on a basket of them. Roundhill's fund charges 0.65% a year and can change its holdings at any time. Sandisk, one of its listed holdings, fell 16% on November 20.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of DRAM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq surge as Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia sparks stunning rally
news.Content:
Stocks soared on Monday as investors cheered Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. It marked a major rebound on Monday as buyers stepped back in for the holiday-shortened week after a bruising sell-off.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 4.8% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) jumped more than 1,400 points to recover by 3% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rallied 6.6%.

Nvidia stock soared more than 30% Monday morning after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said.

Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO >

The move came after President Trump renewed his call to reinstate the chipmaker's founder, Jensen Huang, as CEO amid a series of controversies.

Sentiment was exuberant after a volatile week last week that saw the AI trade unravel and the S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory. Despite Monday's tech rally, Anthropic ( ANT ) shares slipped Monday after whipsawing earlier in the morning.

Elsewhere on the calendar for Monday, Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) and Zoom Communications ( ZM ) report results as the Q3 earnings season wraps up.

"AI and Equities are 'Too Big To Fail'," wrote McElligott. Still, the strategist warns investors not to mistake a forced short-covering rally for an all-clear signal on the economy.

"It's naïve to believe that a one-day 'Up Shock' absolves the market of underlying concerns surrounding the multiple spinning plates," he wrote. "This 'Mechanical Bounce' guarantees us nothing."

McElligott added that a single-day surge does not erase broader structural headwinds—including stubborn inflation, rising borrowing costs, and cooling expectations around corporate AI spending. If those pressures persist, he noted, investors could abandon their decade-long playbook of buying every stock market dip and shift money into cash and bonds instead.

news.Title: Why Did Cerebras Stock Soar Today?
news.Content:
Cerebras (NASDAQ:CBRS) stock bounced back in a big way Monday, soaring 19.2% through 10:45 a.m. ET. And why?

This morning, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced its board has voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Shares of Nvidia ripped 35.5% higher as shorts were forced to burn their bets against the stock and buy it back in apparently massive quantities.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director

With the future of AI looking suddenly surer, other AI stocks -- Cerebras included -- are soaring.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

And yet...

And yet, I cannot help but wonder if this rally -- in Cerebras stock -- makes sense. On the one hand, yes, Nvidia has been described (by detractors) as creating a "circular economy" -- but also (by fans) as turning Nvidia into the "Central Bank of AI." To that extent, when Nvidia's business stumbles, you could argue this is bad news for most AI companies.

But I'm not so sure it would be bad news for Cerebras in particular. Recall that Cerebras's whole business model is built around replacing Nvidia chips with newer, faster, wafer-scale chips that have the added benefit of building their own memory into the wafer. In that regard, Cerebras is really a direct competitor to Nvidia -- not a dependent.

What it means for Cerebras

For this reason, I actually think a revival at Nvidia is bad news for Cerebras, because it un-hobbles a Cerebras competitor. With Jensen Huang now back in the saddle at Nvidia, I'd be more inclined to buy Nvidia stock at 8.4x trailing sales than Cerebras stock at more than 20x sales.

Investors buying Cerebras today may actually be making a huge mistake.

news.Title: Nvidia stock soars 30% after brutal selloff
news.Content: Nvidia (NVDA) has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, reversing a decision that shook the artificial intelligence industry and sent the chipmaker's shares plunging. The company announced Monday, Nov. 23, that Huang would return immediately as president, CEO and a member of the board, just 11 days after his resignation. Nvidia shares surged roughly 30% in morning trading following the announcement. Last Friday, Nvidia stock went into free fall, plunging 14% as concerns over AI spending and the departure of Huang weighed on investor sentiment. The decline brought its weekly loss to 23%. Nvidia board voted to bring Huang back after a series of meetings with him. The company said directors were satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. The decision also followed discussions with senior U.S. government officials, whose input helped convince the board that Huang's return has no national security risk. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement . Huang welcomed the decision. "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," he said. "I can't wait to get back to work." U.S. President Donald Trump has been saying he supports Jensen Huang's return. He just posted on Truth Social that the Nvidia board "has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO." "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Trump said. Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia faces federal scrutiny Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by U.S. authorities of being a Chinese spy. Beijing has denied the espionage allegations. His departure ended more than three decades of leadership at the company he co-founded in 1993. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and began searching for a permanent replacement. Related: CoreWeave stock sinks nearly 7% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns As recently as Nov. 17, Jones told investors that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang. But pressure to bring him back continued to grow. Trump publicly supported Huang's return, writing Sunday that rehiring him would be the best outcome for both Nvidia and the United States. Story Continues Elon Musk and several technology executives also backed a petition calling for Huang's reinstatement. The reversal comes as Nvidia faces questions from Washington over its compliance with restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that the administration was still seeking answers about Nvidia's compliance practices. "We do need answers," Bessent said during an interview with CBS News . Bessent said officials were examining whether potential violations reflected problems at lower levels of the company or reached senior leadership. Despite Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia said its independent investigation into the reported foreign intelligence effort would continue. The company has also established a National Security and Export Control Committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the business. Nvidia said it would continue cooperating with government investigations. Huang is still expected to face questions from House lawmakers in December over the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies. He has also agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee. news.Title: Intel landed Microsoft, but now it needs something it can't make
news.Content:
Intel Corp. (INTC) has landed Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) as the first company to announce the use of its EMIB chip packaging, according to Intel's announcement . Microsoft will use the technology for its own Azure chips under a long-term agreement announced on Nov. 18.

The deal also confirms a multi-year Xeon server chip supply, including next-generation chips code-named Diamond Rapids. For a foundry business still trying to prove itself, few customer names carry more weight.

Wedbush saw good news with a catch. Analyst Matt Bryson called the win a " positive step " but said its financial importance is unclear, according to Seeking Alpha . In his view, the real question is how Intel's packaging efforts ramp up "amidst ABF constraints."

Also read: Intel announces more layoffs as workforce shrinks by 7,300

ABF stands for Ajinomoto Build-up Film. It comes from Ajinomoto Co., the Japanese company best known for MSG seasoning, and Intel does not make it.

Intel's highest-profile packaging win now depends partly on a food company's factory output.

What Microsoft and Intel each get from the deal

Advanced packaging joins pieces of silicon into one working chip. EMIB is a tiny bridge buried in the chip's base that links those pieces.

Microsoft designs its own chips for Azure, but it needs a partner to package them at scale. The companies said the work is designed to give Microsoft customers a more "predictable, scalable and resilient" foundation, according to Intel's release .

Adding Intel gives Microsoft another place to build when capacity gets tight.

The Xeon supply commitment may matter even more. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Intel's " immediate priority " is unlocking supply to meet " extraordinary demand " for Xeon chips, according to its third-quarter earnings release . With multi-year supply confirmed, Microsoft has effectively secured its place in line.

For Intel, the win is about credibility. Intel Foundry, which is courting outside customers, needs big names to justify its heavy spending. Bryson said it is clear that Intel has "several large EMIB deals . "

Winning deals is one job. Delivering them depends on a supplier in Japan.

An MSG maker matters to Intel's plans

ABF substrates are the insulating, wired bases that connect tiny silicon chips to the circuit boards below them, according to Tom's Hardware . Practically every advanced chip Intel makes today depends on them, the outlet reported.

EMIB bridges sit inside that base, so more packaging orders mean more demand for the film.

Ajinomoto controls a reported 95% or more of the global ABF market. That puts a company better known for seasoning at the base of high-end chip packaging.

Story Continues

The supply is already stretched. Ajinomoto's film capacity was running at full load in the second quarter of 2026, Tom's Hardware reported. In May, the company told substrate makers it would raise ABF prices by about 30%.

Bryson's note suggests the squeeze is reaching Intel. Intel's packaging growth depends partly on a queue it does not control.

What the deal could mean for Intel stock

Much of the bull case for Intel rests on its foundry, and investors aren't paying up for promises yet. Shares slipped about 1% the day the deal was announced.

The bigger damage came earlier. Intel shares fell nearly 29% on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, the day after its third-quarter report. The drop followed a fourth-quarter revenue forecast of $15 billion to $16 billion, below third-quarter sales of $16.5 billion, according to Intel's earnings release .

The stock now trades far below its 52-week high of $142.35. It is still up about 46% over 52 weeks, so most of the past year's rally has unwound.

Intel carries a consensus Hold rating from 49 analysts, according to Stock Analysis . Their average 12-month price target of $90.65 implies room for a recovery.

The most recent rating in Stock Analysis data came from Bank of America's Vivek Arya , who reiterated a Hold on Nov. 12. Arya also cut his price target to $80 from $100, the data show.

Earlier in November, Citi's Atif Malik kept a Buy rating but lowered his target to $100 from $130, according to the same data.

The message from analysts reads as hold, not buy. Both firms kept their ratings but cut targets, which suggests patience rather than conviction. Without disclosed terms, the Microsoft deal is hard to build into earnings forecasts yet.

More Intel:

Intel stock collapses; shareholders say they were misled

Bank of America pulls its Buy on Intel as the comeback slips

Intel CEO reveals a PC problem as Goldman cuts stock target

Chip supply now hinges on the smallest parts

Deals like this one show how far chipmaking pressure has spread beyond factories and designs. A film from one dominant supplier can now shape how fast a chipmaker turns new orders into revenue.

Investors should watch two things: what Intel's next quarterly report says about packaging customers and ABF supply, and whether Microsoft names the chips headed to Intel. Either would show more about the deal's real size.

The Microsoft deal proves Intel can win the order. The harder test is whether Ajinomoto's film lets Intel fill it.

news.Title: Stock Market Midday, Nov. 23: Nasdaq Surges Nearly 7% as Jensen Huang's Return Sparks Historic AI Rebound
news.Content:
Wall Street staged a strong rebound on Monday, November 23, as investors returned to equities following last week's steep sell-off. Renewed enthusiasm for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, fueled by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO, helped propel major indexes sharply higher, reversing some of the losses suffered during the recent market downturn.

As of 11:31 a.m. ET, the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) had surged 6.79% to 24,152, while the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) jumped 5.00% to 7,256. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) gained 3.26% to 49,715, reflecting a broad recovery in investor sentiment.

The rebound extended beyond equities, with gold climbing 4.40% to $3,670. Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield declined 12 basis points to 4.92%, providing some relief to investors concerned about elevated borrowing costs.

Today's biggest moves

Nvidia l ed Monday's gains, surging 32.05% following the board's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The announcement fueled a broader rally across AI-related stocks, with Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) climbing 19.50% amid renewed investor enthusiasm for semiconductor companies.

Meanwhile, Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS) jumped 14.62% following the announcement that CrowdStrike Holdings (NASDAQ:CRWD) had agreed to acquire the cybersecurity company in a $43.9 billion deal. However, CrowdStrike shares declined 11.00% as investors weighed the financial implications of the acquisition.

What this means for investors

Monday's sharp rebound provides some relief following last week's sell-off, but investors should distinguish between a recovery driven by improving fundamentals and one fueled by the reversal of excessive pessimism. Jensen Huang's reinstatement removes a significant source of uncertainty for Nvidia, although the broader semiconductor industry still faces questions surrounding AI valuations, regulatory restrictions, and the sustainability of infrastructure spending.

Looking ahead, Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation report could prove particularly influential. With the 10-year Treasury yield still near 5%, persistently elevated inflation could reinforce expectations that interest rates will remain restrictive, putting renewed pressure on equity valuations. For Monday's rally to develop into a more sustainable recovery, investors should look for broader market participation, stabilizing earnings expectations, and continued improvement in financial conditions.

news.Title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
news.Content:
By Ragini Mathur, Avinash P and Niket Nishant

Nov 23 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes rallied sharply on Monday, led by a nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks after Nvidia said it had reinstated ‌Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after ‌an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump's call for Huang's return.

Huang resigned as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged ​Chinese spy.

The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

"Huang's return marks one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive," said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.

"Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn't ‌like what it saw."

The Nasdaq-100 was on track to ⁠add more than $2 trillion in market value on Monday.

The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Trump paused his "Liberation Day" tariff package in April 2025.

Chip stocks ⁠gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

The rally was broad-based in the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure ​earlier following ​Huang's abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius ​advanced 23.4%.

The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% ‌and led the gains in the benchmark index.

Other sectors also climbed, with energy being the only group in negative territory.

The rebound follows a bruising few weeks for equities, as investors grew concerned about the heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns. Fears of political scrutiny for the sector also mounted after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

The selloff had pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory, while the Nasdaq came close to entering a bear market before Monday's rebound.

At 12:02 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial ‌Average rose 1,470.00 points, or 3.05%, to 49,617.33, the S&P 500 gained 335.07 points, ​or 4.85%, to 7,245.46 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1,509.70 points, or 6.69%, to ​24,131.42.

Story Continues

INFLATION DATA WILL TAKE THE SPOTLIGHT

Investors will now focus on ​Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could offer fresh direction on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

Traders are pricing ‌in a nearly 98% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike ​at the Fed's December meeting, according ​to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

New York Fed President John Williams is scheduled to speak later on Monday.

Elsewhere, Zscaler jumped 15.3% after CrowdStrike said on Monday it would buy the cybersecurity provider in an all-stock deal that values Zscaler at about $43.9 billion.

CrowdStrike shares fell ​10.5%.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 4.44-to-1 ratio on ‌the NYSE and by a 3.91-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 1 new 52-week high and 6 new ​lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 15 new highs and 207 new lows.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Purvi Agarwal, Ragini Mathur ​and Avinash P in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich and Maju Samuel)

news.Title: Situational Awareness Stock Portfolio: Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Top 5 Picks
news.Content:
Leopold Aschenbrenner was a university valedictorian at 19, a fired AI researcher at 22, and by 25 the manager of a hedge fund that reportedly peaked near $45 billion.

The Germany-born investor joined the safety team at OpenAI in 2023 and lost the job in April 2024 over an alleged leak of a brainstorming document, which he disputes. Two months later he published a 165-page essay arguing that artificial general intelligence could arrive within a few years and that the race to build it had begun.

How a Viral Essay Became a Hedge Fund

He named his fund, Situational Awareness LP , after the essay and launched it in 2024 with backing from investors including Patrick and John Collison, Daniel Gross, and Nat Friedman. Its core idea was that the bottlenecks of the AI boom would be electricity and computing capacity, not the models themselves.

The bets paid off. By the end of 2025 the fund reported about $5.5 billion in U.S. stock exposure across nearly 30 holdings, and it gained 439% in the first half of 2026. Its assets reportedly swelled to about $45 billion, much of it built on borrowed money. Readers following the theme can find more names in our list of AI infrastructure stocks for the long term .

The Margin Calls That Erased Most of the Fund

Then the AI trade turned. In July 2026, semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks fell, a bet against software stocks went wrong, and lenders demanded more collateral. The fund lost 67% in July, CNBC reported. Before markets opened on July 30, it sold most of a roughly $16 billion public stock book to Citadel , the hedge fund run by billionaire Ken Griffin, at about a 10% discount.

Assets dropped to about $10 billion, mostly private stakes, and Aschenbrenner told investors the fund would stop borrowing against its public holdings. A November 16 filing showed its U.S.-listed holdings had shrunk 92%, to $1.58 billion on September 30 from $20.24 billion at the end of June.

He did not stay out for long. The same filing showed a rebuilt book of AI-linked stocks and call options, which then fell hard in October. Our ranking of the cheapest AI data center stocks according to billionaires shows how other big investors hold the group. On November 18, the Financial Times reported that he was discussing a "Situational Awareness 2.0" with brokers and investors, with a chief risk officer, outside money and possibly leverage again.

We shared the expanded list of Situational Awareness Stock Portfolio: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Top 10 Picks . Click the image below to watch our video covering the top 5 stocks.

Story Continues

Our Methodology

For this article, we reviewed the Q3 2026 13F filing of Situational Awareness LP, the hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, and ranked its holdings by stake value in ascending order. Anthropic, the fund's largest position, was private at quarter-end and is absent from the filing, so we used the stake value reported in the press.

At Insider Monkey, we are obsessed with what hedge funds do. The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Situational Awareness Stock Portfolio: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Top 5 Picks

5. Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $182,688,450

Sandisk makes flash memory storage for phones, laptops and data centers, and it was spun off from Western Digital in early 2025.

Situational Awareness LP held call options on Sandisk valued at $182,688,450 at the end of September, a new position that makes up 11.58% of its portfolio. The value is based on the shares the options cover. The fund owned 2,495,344 shares at the end of June and sold them in July.

The company has kept delivering. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended October 2, revenue hit $11.0 billion, up 23% from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and up 378% from a year earlier. Data center revenue reached $4.80 billion. Sandisk guided second-quarter revenue to $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and announced an eight-for-one stock split, which took effect on November 19. Chief Executive Officer David Goeckeler said data center growth outpaced the rest of the business.

Gross margin was 85.0%, up from 84.6% in the fourth quarter. Shares fell 16% to $79.24 on November 20, the first full session after the split. Our analysis of whether Sandisk at six times forward earnings has a peak priced in takes up that question.

4. Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $332,590,800

Nebius made up 21.08% of Situational Awareness LP's portfolio at the end of September, a new position of call options on 1,410,000 shares. The options were valued at $332,590,800, based on the shares they cover.

Nebius is a technology company that provides infrastructure and services to AI builders worldwide, including large GPU clusters and cloud tools.

Bulls point to the third quarter of 2026. Revenue rose 571% to $980.8 million, and the net loss from continuing operations shrank to $37.5 million. Customers committed more than $12 billion in contracts since the start of the third quarter, and Nebius expects 2027 revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion.

Bears focused on the forecast. On November 12, Nebius narrowed its 2026 revenue outlook to $3.0 billion to $3.2 billion because third-party capacity, including a New Jersey site, came online later than planned. It also expects about $27 billion in capital spending this year. The shares lost 35% in October and closed at $81.31 on November 20, 72% below their June record. Our piece on whether Nebius has pricing power its earnings do not yet show looks at the upside case.

3. Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $389,156,900

Bloom Energy makes solid oxide fuel cell systems that turn natural gas or biogas into electricity on site, without burning it.

Situational Awareness LP held call options on 1,405,000 shares of Bloom at the end of September, which is 24.67% of its portfolio. The options were valued at $389,156,900, based on the shares they cover, and the position grew 864% since the end of June.

In the third quarter of 2026, revenue rose 138.1% to a record $1,235.8 million. Bloom raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion, its third increase of the year. The caution is delivery timing: Bloom said a few year-end deliveries could decide where full-year revenue lands within that range.

BMO Capital Markets upgraded Bloom to Outperform from Market Perform on November 19 and cut its target to $230 from $260. Analyst Ameet Thakkar said the pullback improved the risk-reward. He cited contract protections, milestone-based customer payments and large projects such as Nebius. Our look at whether Bloom's premium can survive its scale-up now that it is profitable covers the valuation question.

2. SharonAI (NASDAQ:SHAZ)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: $440,673,870

Situational Awareness LP owned 8,070,950 shares of SharonAI at the end of September, which is 27.94% of its portfolio. The stake was valued at $440,673,870, and the fund had raised it by 50% since the end of June.

SharonAI is an Australian "neocloud" that rents out Nvidia GPU computing power to businesses and AI labs in Australia and the Asia-Pacific region. It listed on Nasdaq in February 2026.

The company reported third-quarter 2026 results on November 16. Revenue rose to $9.9 million, while the net loss widened to $43.8 million. Bulls look past those numbers to the contract book: total contract value of about $9.6 billion over 5.5 years, including $2.5 billion signed since the second quarter, and a five-year take-or-pay deal with a global AI lab.

SharonAI said annual recurring revenue was $50 million in the third quarter and should climb to $400 million to $450 million in January 2027 as capacity comes online. That gap between signed and billed is the risk. The shares fell 58% in October. Our analysis of whether SharonAI is a trapdoor or a masterpiece weighs both sides.

1. Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT)

Situational Awareness LP's Stake Value: About $5 billion (press estimate)

Situational Awareness LP's stake in Anthropic was valued at about $5 billion, according to press reports. It does not appear in the fund's 13F because Anthropic was private on September 30. The fund kept the stake when it sold its public stock book on July 30, and it held about $10 billion in assets afterward, mostly private.

Anthropic builds the Claude family of AI models and sells them to businesses and consumers. It priced its IPO at $83 on November 18, above the $70 to $78 range it had marketed, selling 980 million shares to raise about $81.3 billion, which valued the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Trading opened on November 19 at $111.50, then faded to a first-day close of $97.17, which was 17% above the IPO price. Needham analyst Scott Berg started coverage that day with a Buy rating and a $150 price target, and he expects growth above 150% in fiscal 2027 and operating margins above 35%. Wolfe Research also began coverage on November 19, with an Outperform rating and a $135 target.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of ANT as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Europe's STOXX logs strongest day in over six months on tech boost
news.Content:
By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair, Purvi Agarwal and Johann M Cherian

Nov 23 (Reuters) - European shares logged their strongest gains in more than six months on Monday, boosted by technology stocks after US-based ‌Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

The development temporarily halted a leadership crisis at the AI ‌chip giant and soothed broader concerns that had sparked a global selloff, given Huang's crucial role in shaping a myriad of deals within the technology ​sector.

However, Huang and Nvidia still face regulatory scrutiny in Washington over dealings with an alleged Chinese spy at a time when the Democrats are set to take charge of Congress.

"Today's stock market rebound represents a massive sigh of relief by investors. However, one cannot rule out a more conservative approach by Huang going forward," said Dan Coatsworth, head ‌of markets at AJ Bell.

"It's plausible that ⁠investors will be more critical of the pace and scale of financing deals and start to ask more questions about financial payback."

The STOXX 600 closed 1.9% higher at ⁠637.84 points, marking its biggest daily jump since early May. Europe's technology index led sectoral gains with a 4.7% rise, recovering from its sharpest weekly fall since March 2020 on Friday.

Among chip-linked stocks, AT&S shot up 13%, Aixtron surged 8.9% and BE ​Semiconductor ​jumped 9.2%. AI equipment makers Schneider Electric and Siemens Energy ​gained 4.1% and 7%, respectively.

The sector had ‌taken a beating in recent weeks as investors were vexed over the timeline for returns on the billions invested by companies to develop the technology. Despite Monday's gains, Europe's tech index is down nearly 13% this quarter.

Losses in US-based Anthropic since its strong debut broadly reflected those concerns.

Most other sectors in Europe were also higher, with defence, industrials and miners up more than 3% each.

Among others, Abivax advanced 4.7% after rejecting as misleading a short-seller report that ‌questioned the safety of its experimental bowel-disease drug obefazimod, while ​British power generator Drax rallied more than 5% after it forecast annual core ​profit above consensus.

Julius Baer slipped 1.7%, despite reporting a ​17% rise in 10-month adjusted pretax profit, with investors weighing slower net inflows as ‌the bank continues to exit higher-risk client relationships.

Nemetschek ​shares dropped 5.7% to the ​bottom of the STOXX 600 after J.P. Morgan downgraded the software firm to "underweight" from "overweight".

Story Continues

French President Emmanuel Macron suggested on Monday reviving a 2011 proposal for a constitutional "golden rule" to impose limits on public finances ​in an attempt to reassure investors.

The ‌country's rising debt burden has drawn increasing scrutiny ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Fresh data ​pointed to a deeper downturn in Europe's second-largest economy.

(Reporting by Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair in Bengaluru; ​Editing by Nivedita Bhattacharjee, Joyjeet Das and Alex Richardson)

news.Title: Lucid Needs More Buyers. This Strategy Could Help It Reach Them.
news.Content:
Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID) has spent plenty of time convincing investors its vehicles deserve attention. But building an impressive electric vehicle (EV) is one thing. Convincing people to pull the trigger on a big-ticket purchase can prove more challenging.

A customer might love the range, performance, and design, then wonder where they'll get it serviced in a pinch. Admiring a car online is easy, but signing the paperwork when support feels far away, combined with Lucid's financial uncertainty? That's a tougher sell, especially for a young EV maker such as Lucid.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Lucid is introducing another twist within its European strategy, and it's possible the move could help Lucid convince more buyers to jump on board without needing to operate more locations itself.

Borrowing some local muscle

In August, Lucid named Munsterhuis Autobedrijven its first retail partner in the Netherlands. The partnership calls for a dedicated Lucid sales location in the city of Hengelo, with authorized after-sales and service at the same site. Essentially, it complements Lucid's existing Studio and Service Center in Hilversum.

This continues a hybrid retail strategy that already included a partnership with Germany's Wackenhut. Lucid is adding independent partners alongside its own locations. The upside is worth noting for investors because an established retailer brings local relationships and experience selling and servicing cars. Lucid brings the vehicles and enjoys its expanding reach.

For buyers, nearby sales and service could remove a reason to hesitate before making the big-ticket purchase. For shareholders, partners could provide a way to expand customer access while sharing the work of building a retail presence. All in all, it's really an underrated move by Lucid if it can expand on the idea and execute.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lucid has company

Lucid's strategic twist isn't completely unheard of before. Chinese EV maker Nio is pursuing a related approach. In June 2025, it announced European expansion through local distribution partners, including Hedin Mobility Group for Belgium and Luxembourg.

The agreements aren't exactly identical, but the logic and strategy are similar: An automaker doesn't have to build every part of its overseas sales network from scratch. Of course, the middleman needs to make money, too. Sharing the economics with a retail partner could leave Lucid keeping less from each sale.

Story Continues

But reaching more buyers while committing less capital to its own retail network could be a worthwhile trade-off for a company trying to conserve cash.

More doors need to lead to more buyers

The question facing investors is whether better access produces additional sales without an equally large increase in Lucid's own spending. Investors should cheer more partner appointments, broader service coverage, and evidence that the expanded network attracts customers. That said, a longer location list alone won't guarantee a spike in deliveries, demand, or revenue.

This won't fix Lucid's business overnight , and to be fair, the young automaker has a number of problems to address. However, making its vehicles easier to buy and maintain for more potential consumers could help turn product credibility into more sales.

Lucid doesn't need to own every showroom. It needs more customers walking into one – and driving home in its cars.

news.Title: The Nasdaq Just Had 1 of Its 10 Worst Weeks in the Past 45 Years. Here's What History Says Comes Next.
news.Content:
The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) fell 10% in the week ending Nov. 20, bringing its overall loss since its October high to more than 18%.

Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) current drama and the Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) IPO are getting most of the attention. But the damage in the sector is widespread.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Investors who went overweight in tech and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks may be wondering if the worst is over or if it's yet to come. History gives us some guidance, although it may not be as comforting as they're hoping for.

Image source: Getty Images.

Every 10% down week since 1971 came during a bear market

Before this week, the Nasdaq had dropped 10% or more in a single week exactly 10 times since 1971. The list, unfortunately, reads like a history of stock market crisis periods: Black Monday, the 2000 tech bubble, the 2008-09 Great Recession, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the "Liberation Day" tariff sell-off.

Each one happened during what became a bear market. The Nasdaq Composite is essentially there right now, so the current correction fits right in. The question is where the decline stops.

The typical outcome is positive, but the range of outcomes is wide

Here's what the index did following those past instances of 10%-plus weekly declines:

At a high level, the results seem encouraging. The median return over the following one-month, three-month, six-month, and 12-month periods are all positive and modestly above the stock market's long-term averages.

But the real story, I think, is the volatility.

Story Continues

Across the data set, individual returns vary widely. Even in a relatively short one-month forward return, the Nasdaq Composite was down more than 11% twice but up more than 15% three times. That doesn't do much for predictability.

Even within the same crisis period, returns were very volatile.

In April 2000, the index was up 28% three months later but down 40% after 12 months.

In September 2001, it was up 30% after six months but down 14% after 12 months.

In October 2008, the index was flat after six months but up nearly 30% after 12 months.

The key takeaway isn't that this is a consistent buy-the-dip opportunity. It's that this could be just the beginning of an extended period of above-average market volatility. And volatility tends to mean a higher risk of further declines.

The bottom usually comes later

No matter what forward-looking time frame you consider, the 10% single-week decline rarely marked a low for the Nasdaq Composite. In many cases, additional declines of 10% or more were still in store.

Plus, big drops also tended to cluster together. In seven of the 10 instances, the index suffered another weekly loss of 7% or more within the following 13 weeks. That's consistent with other studies that have shown sharp up and down moves often happen in close proximity to each other.

In the three cases where the 10% down week occurred in close proximity to the market's bottom (September 2001, April 2000, and April 2025), the Nasdaq had already declined sharply in the lead-up.

In 2026, the Nasdaq was already about 8% to 10% below its all-time high prior to last week's 10% decline. That's not nearly as large of a correction as the market saw before the three instances mentioned above. But last week's huge decline didn't come out of the blue either.

What investors should do now

Prepare for more volatility. History shows that a 10% single-week decline usually isn't a one-off, and that additional whipsaws in stock prices can last for months.

For long-term investors with 10-plus years yet to go before initiating any drawdowns, I think this is a good opportunity to either stay the course you already have planned and/or use the current drawdown to opportunistically buy the dip if you have cash for this purpose. Try to avoid making major changes to your asset allocation based on the past six weeks.

But if you've found that the current correction has you losing sleep at night, consider adjusting to a more conservative allocation. It'll likely yield better long-term results than trying to time in and out of the market. It's best to avoid investing beyond your risk tolerance.

news.Title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week
news.Content: Nvidia's board needed 12 days to hit "undo" on Jensen Huang. Three years ago this week, OpenAI needed less than five to do the same with Sam Altman. Almost nobody saw the Huang news coming. Minutes before Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced his return Monday morning, bettors on Polymarket gave him about a 3% chance of getting his job back this month. Five minutes later, the odds were 99%. The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, and Colette Kress goes back to being CFO. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA," Chair Harvey Jones said. Nvidia stock rose more than 30% Monday, on track for its best day since 2003 and adding nearly $1 trillion in market value, most of what it lost while Huang was gone. Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO > Huang's exile was expensive Nvidia lost about $1.2 trillion in market value from the Nov. 11 close, when the board accepted Huang's resignation, through Friday, a stretch that included the stock's worst week ever . Silicon Valley has seen this movie before. OpenAI fired Altman on a Friday afternoon in November 2023. Microsoft ( MSFT ) hired him that Sunday, and more than 700 of OpenAI's roughly 770 employees threatened to follow him. By Tuesday night, he was back. "I love OpenAI, and everything I've done over the past few days has been in service of keeping this team and its mission together," Altman wrote on X. Huang had his own campaign, though not one he ran. A "Stand with Jensen" petition drew more than 100,000 signatures, Elon Musk's among them, including more than 5,000 from people who said they work at Nvidia. It called for "due process, not mob justice." OpenAI's kingmaker was Microsoft. Nvidia's was the White House. The board said input from senior levels of the US government led it to conclude that Huang poses no national security risk. President Trump had pushed for Huang to get a second chance. Huang's undoing is different from Altman's in one way. Altman came back to a new board. Huang comes back to the same chair, plus a new national security and export control committee, a search for a chief compliance officer, and an independent investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. More about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO: Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington. Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, stock rockets Trump celebrates Jensen Huang's return after pushing Nvidia for his reinstatement Apple's comeback took 12 years Steve Jobs resigned from Apple ( AAPL ) in September 1985 and was named interim CEO in September 1997. Apple stock rose 2% on his first day back and beat the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) by 65 percentage points over the next year. Story Continues Most famous comebacks start with a cheer from the Wall Street bleachers, but the year after has been a coin flip. Nvidia's jump Monday is on track to be more than triple the biggest first-day pop in the chart below. Academic research is tougher on boomerangs A study of 167 returning CEOs at S&P 500 companies from 1992 to 2017 found that their stocks performed about 10% worse per year than under first-time CEOs, and even worse in fast-changing industries, according to MIT Sloan Management Review . Founders made up 4% of all the CEOs studied but 44% of the boomerangs. Huang's calendar is still full. He faces a closed-door House interview Dec. 1 and has agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee. Jobs came to see his exile as a gift. "I didn't see it then, but it turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me," Jobs said in his 2005 Stanford commencement speech. news.Title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia’s CEO. Is Nvidia Stock in the Clear or Do Risks Remain?
news.Content:
Nvidia's (NASDAQ:NVDA) board of directors shocked the world this morning by reinstating Jensen Huang as the company's CEO, president, and a member of the board.

As many know, Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 following media reports that alleged Huang had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman named Alice Huang (no relation), who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In a statement, Nvidia's board said they felt "confident" that Huang "poses no national security risk."

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."

In the statement, Huang said he is "honored" to return and retakes his post "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

As of 11:50 a.m. ET, Nvidia stock traded nearly 31% higher. Is the stock in the clear, or do risks remain?

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

What Huang's reinstatement could signal

Huang is clearly a fantastic CEO from an operational perspective. He founded Nvidia 33 years ago and clearly had the foresight to see artificial intelligence coming decades before it went mainstream.

But Huang's return may be lifting Nvidia stock for other reasons. The board stated that Huang's return poses no national security risk. Investors could interpret this to mean that Nvidia did not bypass export restrictions and sell chips that may have illegally reached China.

Reports suggest that Alice Huang had set up a network to purchase chips through shell companies or companies established outside China, which then shipped them to China. If this is the case and the U.S. imposes further restrictions to prevent it, this would threaten Nvidia's future revenue and earnings, which would certainly impact the stock and the company's total value.

The big question is how many of Nvidia's chips have been making their way to China illegally. From the outside, it's hard to believe the board would reinstate Huang if they were concerned that the company, under his direction, had knowingly bypassed export restrictions.

Story Continues

The reinstatement follows an interview on Nov. 22 with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who seemed to dial back some of his previous rhetoric directed at the company and even left the door open for Huang's return.

Do risks remain?

The short answer is yes.

In its statement, Nvidia's board said that the independent investigation it launched into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion." The board has also created a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

That feels a bit counterintuitive for the board to say it feels confident that Huang poses no national security concern, yet to continue the independent investigation. Another question is why this national security committee is only being set up now.

Furthermore, the board said on Nvidia's recent earnings call it had no intention of reinstating Huang, so its hands may have been forced for another reason. For instance, there was strong support for Huang's reinstatement. It's possible a significant number of employees threatened to leave the company if Huang was not reinstated. If this is the case, Nvidia's board could be acting hastily.

Huang is also set to testify before Congress. Additionally, the U.S. Commerce Department recently imposed a rule that will prevent Chinese companies from using advanced U.S. chips that are remotely stored in data centers outside China.

The Commerce Department will also require companies in Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, or Thailand to obtain licenses to export or transfer chips.

If it turns out that a material number of Nvidia's chips were purchased to be provided to Chinese companies for remote access or direct shipment, that could lead Wall Street analysts to cut their revenue and earnings projections for future years.

The reinstatement of Huang certainly caught me by surprise, as I didn't think it could happen so soon. I still see risks for the stock, and after the big move, the easy money has been made.

Nvidia isn't necessarily expensive at these levels, but I would still tread cautiously and would continue to keep future Nvidia stock purchases smaller and more speculative. I don't think this story is over.

news.Content:

International Paper（IP.US）： 成交價29.28美元，下跌3.56%，開盤31美元，盤中高點31.03美元，盤中低點29.1美元，均價29.65美元，成交量65.31萬股。

International Paper最近較具體的變化，是外部評等已轉向反映公司獲利面臨多重壓力。Argus近日將其評等降至持有，理由不是單一短期雜音，而是較高投入成本、關稅不確定性與需求疲軟已開始打擊獲利，代表包裝與紙業景氣修復速度不如原先預期。

這項訊號的重要性在於，公司雖被認為具備不錯的產業紀錄，但目前討論焦點已從經營基礎是否穩健，轉為成本能否順利轉嫁、需求何時止弱，以及關稅變數會不會繼續壓縮營運彈性。就現有資訊來看，International Paper近期最值得追蹤的不是擴張或新產品，而是獲利承壓的環境是否延續。

Tyson Foods（TSN.US）： 成交價62.81美元，下跌3.55%，開盤64.42美元，盤中高點64.68美元，盤中低點62.78美元，均價63.35美元，成交量21.74萬股。

Tyson Foods已把牛肉業務重整拉到營運核心，並明確把資本與投資優先轉向雞肉與加工食品。公司2026財年牛肉部門營收約213億美元，卻虧損約6.54億美元，第四季還認列8000萬美元活牛存貨非現金減損，反映牛隻供應緊縮仍是最大壓力來源。

相較之下，雞肉全年營業利益達18.6億美元，第四季銷量再增2%，已連續第八季量增；加工食品全年營業利益13.3億美元，第四季零售據點增加4.4%，單季營業利益升至3.21億美元。公司已與Allied Beef建立長期合作，並規劃在2027年夏恢復Amarillo第二班次全產能，同時預期2027財年整體營收將下滑3.5%至5.5%、調整後營業利益落在17億至21.5億美元，顯示下一階段重點是修復牛肉結構，而非單純追求營收放大。

Texas Pacific Land（TPL.US）： 成交價258.89美元，下跌3.2%，開盤280.34美元，盤中高點282.65美元，盤中低點250.93美元，均價260.65美元，成交量17.76萬股。

Texas Pacific Land近14日內未見新的重大公司公告，現有資料也沒有新增資產交易、土地開發、權利金變化或資本回饋政策調整。以這類資產型公司來看，真正能改變營運方向的通常是土地相關收入、資源開發活動，或回購與配息等資本配置動作，但近期公開資訊並未出現這類新催化。

因此，Texas Pacific Land目前較像處在消息空窗期，市場暫時仍只能依既有資產價值與現金流預期評估公司，而不是根據新策略重新定價。後續若公司公布新的授權、處分、回購或配息安排，才較可能成為下一個可辨識的營運主線；在此之前，尚看不出近期有足以改變成長方向的公司特定事件。

LyondellBasell（LYB.US）： 成交價54.36美元，下跌2.65%，開盤56.18美元，盤中高點56.69美元，盤中低點54.04美元，均價54.71美元，成交量32.51萬股。

LyondellBasell已同意出售前休士頓煉油廠用地及相關資產給Valero旗下子公司，交易總值3.205億美元，預計於2026年第四季完成。這筆交易代表公司持續推進資產組合轉型，把資源從非核心資產抽離，轉向更符合長期策略、且更有價值創造潛力的業務。

公司表示，Valero將承擔該用地後續營運、環境責任、退休金成本與相關員工義務，等於LyondellBasell不只變現土地，也一併移出後續負擔。管理層先前已決定停止煉油業務，這次出售則讓這項方向更具體，顯示公司正把資本配置能力留給核心化學品與其他更符合策略的資產，而不是繼續保留已退出經營的煉油設施。

Elevance Health（ELV.US）： 成交價385美元，下跌2.4%，開盤386.03美元，盤中高點395.39美元，盤中低點379.75美元，均價385.22美元，成交量15.22萬股。

Elevance Health在企業雇主健保市場的競爭位置近期明顯強化。瑞銀針對166位企業福利經理人的年度調查中，Elevance以5分制4.34分拿下全美健康保險公司最高評價，並在客戶服務與醫療網兩項領先，顯示它在大型雇主採購決策中的相對優勢正在提升。

更關鍵的是，77%受訪者表示計畫在2027年為核心醫療福利尋求新提案，明顯高於去年的53%與前年的41%，代表大型企業合約重談潮正在升溫，Elevance有機會在新一輪招標中爭取更多業務。不過，這波機會也伴隨成本壓力，雇主預期2027年自籌資金計畫總醫療成本將增加7.9%，高於今年預估的7%，其中GLP-1減重藥被列為主要推手，後續仍要看公司定價與理賠管理能力。

ConocoPhillips（COP.US）： 成交價133.46美元，下跌1.95%，開盤134.61美元，盤中高點135.79美元，盤中低點132.94美元，均價134.31美元，成交量50.33萬股。

ConocoPhillips已與Vår Energi簽署最終協議，出售挪威業務以及英國Teesside原油終端40.25%持股與營運權，原始總對價44.25億美元，調整後約39億美元。這不是單純處分邊角資產，而是把一整組成熟北海資產變現，進一步收斂版圖並強化資本配置彈性。

被出售資產在2025年平均日產約12萬桶油當量，截至2025年底相關已證實儲量約2.21億桶油當量，規模並不小。公司預期扣除約14億美元的2026年剩餘稅負後，淨現金入帳約25億美元，交易預計於2027年第一季底前完成，並將把資金用於一般公司用途與2027年的彈性庫藏股回購。這也呼應ConocoPhillips先前強調的資本回饋政策，以及把資產與現金流轉向更高報酬用途的方向。
