news.Title: Meta Platforms Stocks Rebound 6.13% After 12.6% Weekly Slide on Class C Lawsuit
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) shares rebounded 6.13% to $595.20 at 10:40 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 23, clawing back part of a 12.6% weekly drop that ended Friday at $560.84. Wisevoter tied last week's slide to Delaware shareholder suits over the planned Class C shares and to a Reuters investigation into its Muse AI agent, which Meta said involved mostly hallucinations that were already addressed. Meta also told the court it will not issue new Class C shares while the litigation continues.

That pause hits a plan Meta unveiled with its third-quarter results: a one-time dividend of one non-voting Class C share per existing share, with the amended charter set to take effect on January 19, 2027. The quarter itself was strong underneath a $9.89 billion legal charge. Revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and diluted EPS of $3.83 would have been $7.40 without the charge. Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion and narrowed 2026 capex guidance to $135 billion to $145 billion.

Even after Monday's bounce, the shares sit about 24% below their 52-week high of $779.82. news.Title: Micron Stocks Jump 13.73% After Selloff Left Shares Near 5 Times Annualized Earnings
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU ) shares rallied 13.73% to $676.16 at 9:55 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 23, recovering part of a roughly 23.6% slide last week that included a drop of nearly 14% on Friday. Investing.com tied that slump to TrendForce's call for lower NAND contract prices from early 2027 and to the wider AI rout. On Monday, Citi pushed back, arguing that capex fears are overblown for DRAM demand, according to the same report.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with MU.

Is MU fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Micron's own books explain why buyers came back so fast. In fiscal Q4 2026, which ended September 3, the company reported revenue of $54.23 billion against $11.32 billion a year earlier, a gain of about 379%. Non-GAAP gross margin hit 87.0%, non-GAAP EPS reached $33.42, and operating cash flow came in at $43.97 billion. CEO Sanjay Mehrotra pointed to strategic customer agreements as support for how long these results can last.

Annualize that quarter's $33.42 and the shares trade near 5 times earnings even after Monday's jump. A multiple that low says the market treats fiscal Q4 as a peak, not a run rate. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 96/100, pairing top-tier profitability with a strong balance sheet, while momentum sits in the middle after last week's damage. The GF Value of $860.51 puts the price 21.4% below GuruFocus's estimate, a "Modestly Undervalued" label that only holds if pricing does not roll over. news.Title: California attorney general says Huang reinstatement changes nothing
news.Content:
By Jody Godoy

Nov 23 (Reuters) - California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office said on Monday ‌that Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's chief ‌executive officer does not diminish the need for a probe ​into what Nvidia told investors about its China ties.

Bonta started investigating the company last week after Huang's resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one ‌with a woman ⁠alleged to have spied for China. Nvidia reinstated Huang on Monday after ⁠US President Donald Trump called for his return.

"The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the ​fact that ​the American people ​deserve to know what ‌happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public," a spokesperson for Bonta's office said on Monday

The office's probe into whether confidential information or advanced chips went to China, and whether ‌the company misled investors, remains ongoing, ​the spokesperson added.

Nvidia said its ​board voted unanimously ​on Monday to reinstate Huang ‌after concluding that it was ​satisfied with ​his candor and leadership ability. The board said that, after receiving input from senior US ​government officials, ‌it saw no national security risk from ​his return.

(Reporting by Jody Godoy in New ​YorkEditing by Nick Zieminski)

news.Title: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO;  Trump says he 'convinced' board
news.Content: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board on Monday announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO." Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "The US government [now has] tools at hand to drastically restrict US-based AI technology access by China, with Nvidia no longer lobbying for a US-based AI ecosystem in that geography, while reinstating Mr. Huang so Nvidia remains Nvidia," Gerra wrote. "The combination of these two actions probably represents the worst-case scenario for China." According to Gerra, Nvidia may need to accelerate its open model strategy just in case the government puts restrictions on the use of Chinese open models. 33 mins ago Jared Blikre Nasdaq futures tripped a circuit breaker built for market crashes as Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia The Nasdaq spent last week careening downhill. news.Title: Jensen Huang is back atop Nvidia. He has a long road ahead in Washington.
news.Content: Returning Jensen Huang to Nvidia's top job was hailed in Silicon Valley as essential to the future of the AI trade, and on Monday his supporters got their wish. But the embattled CEO's road back to the job may prove easier than the one awaiting him in Washington. Huang's reinstatement comes less than two weeks after revelations of his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative forced his resignation, setting off a political firestorm over Nvidia's dealings with China and its influence within the Trump administration. Now back at the helm of the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, Huang faces a growing list of congressional inquiries, federal and state scrutiny, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle demanding answers about whether his relationship compromised American national security. "All the questions that people have been raising in the press and in social media, all those questions are still out there," Martijn Rasser, vice president of technology leadership at the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP), told Yahoo Finance. "That aspect of the story is still very much in play," said Rasser, a former officer at the Central Intelligence Agency and former director of the technology and national security program at the Center for a New American Security. Nvidia's board of directors said on Monday that the decision to reinstate Huang came after they "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump, who has pushed for Huang's reinstatement since his ouster on Nov. 12, confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally lobby for Huang, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security. The president noted in a Truth Social post that the US government "has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," and that "the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct." Lawmakers, including prominent members from the president's own party, have disputed those assertions. Republican Senator John Cornyn, who sits on the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote shortly after the news, "No national security risk? Based on what?" Story Continues Republican Representatives Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter last week requesting Huang's testimony before their respective House committees, saying that "recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." Democrats have made similar calls since Huang's reinstatement, following on prior statements condemning potential national security violations at Nvidia. "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers," Senator Elizabeth Warren (Ma.), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, wrote on Monday after the news. "Huang's return only increases the urgency to pass bipartisan export control bills and make sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." Republicans have also pushed on wider questions surrounding the US government's involvement with Nvidia, including coming congressional interrogations of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Huang has called "the person I talk to most in the administration." "If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, perhaps he should have responded to my many letters warning about these Chinese communist front companies and, more importantly, taking the threats of communist China more seriously," Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton said in an interview with The Wall Street Journal. Nvidia has said in multiple quarterly reports that it projects no compute revenue from China in forward-looking estimates, stating in its fiscal second quarter report, "Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for wide distribution in China's data center market with the approval from both the USG and the Chinese government." Huang's first major test will come next week on Dec. 1, when he is scheduled to appear before three House committees investigating his ties to the suspected Chinese operative, Alice Huang, and the potential diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is also set to face questioning alongside senior Commerce Department officials responsible for enforcing restrictions on chip exports. An inquiry by the Commerce Department into Singapore-based Megaspeed — the company that Alice Huang was once associated with — over alleged violations of US semiconductor export controls was transferred to the Justice Department after Teter asked the Commerce Department for information on the investigation, The New York Times reported. Huang has separately agreed to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee, setting up an appearance alongside Lutnick, who has also agreed to testify and who is facing scrutiny over reports he slowed investigations into companies suspected of funneling controlled semiconductors into China. The controversy has also drawn investigators beyond Capitol Hill. California's attorney general has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation connected to Huang's affair. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over accounting violations , per Reuters. Proposed national legislation could also present further complications for Nvidia's business. The so-called AI Overwatch Act would tighten export controls on shipments of advanced dual-use AI chips to foreign nations such as China, while the Chip Security Act would impose new verification measures on the locations of chips exported abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would impose more restrictive export controls on the equipment needed to make advanced AI chips. "I think the news of the past few weeks has underscored in the mind of many legislators on Capitol Hill that not enough is being done to ensure that critical US technologies stay out of the hands of our adversaries," SCSP's Rasser told Yahoo Finance. As Huang prepares to appear before Congress, he will have an important ally in Trump, who has repeatedly referred to Huang as a close associate. The president said on Monday that he personally weighed in on the Nvidia board's decision to reinstate Huang and believes his intervention was "very important" to the decision to reinstate Huang, telling CNBC, "I convinced them." "If I thought he did something wrong, I wouldn't be recommending to his board to hire him," Trump said. Follow Jake Conley on X @byjakeconley or email him at jake.conley@yahooinc.com . news.Title: Wall Street analysts cheer Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — but they still have concerns
news.Content:
Bernstein analysts were quick to upgrade Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Monday after the board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO of the AI chipmaker, though Wall Street sees ongoing investigations as a lingering overhang on the company.

The stock surged as much as 32% following Huang's reinstatement. President Trump said he spoke to the board and "convinced" them to reinstate Huang.

Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon and his team, which had downgraded the stock to Neutral just 11 days ago, rerated the stock as a Buy again as soon as the board announced Huang's return.

"As we remain positive on AI buildout fundamentals, and with Jensen back in the seat, we upgrade today back to [Outperform] (as his exit was the primary reason for the downgrade)," Rasgon wrote.

The analyst maintained a $200 price target, highlighting questions that will likely leave some overhang in place, including ongoing investigations which may limit NVDA's multiple for now.

"While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again-off-again response from the board is, frankly, clown-like," the analysts added, questioning what this says about how the board goes about making other decisions.

Yorkville's Dan Ives, which has maintained a Buy rating on the stock, said on Monday that the firm believes Nvidia stock should be valued at $300 with Jensen Huang back. However, the analysts kept $225 as the price target for the stock, saying they're looking for a resolution of the board's investigation.

The path to closing the price gap "runs through the committee's conclusion, a clean read on the export probe, and a 4Q print delivered by a CEO whose tenure is no longer a topic on the earnings call," Ives wrote.

KeyBank analyst John Vinh stated that while Jensen Huang's reinstatement is a "significantly positive development," the firm retains a Sector Weight, or Neutral, rating and awaits further clarification on the board's ongoing investigation and the SEC accounting inquiry before revisiting its rating,

Stifel analyst Ruben Roy, meanwhile, reiterated a Buy rating and maintained a $225 price target, noting that while Huang's return removes key-person risk, the ongoing investigations remain a potential overhang on the shares.

Several other analysts echoed the sentiment that a major overhang has been cleared, even as governance questions remain. In other words,

"In our view, the reinstatement removes the key overhang created by the CEO transition," Citi analyst Atif Malik wrote, issuing a Buy rating and raising the firm's price target to $240.

Story Continues

Malik noted that while Huang's reinstatement "restores continuity across NVDA's product roadmap," uncertainty remains around the scrutiny into Huang's relationships. "That said, we would view clean resolutions of these concerns as a further catalyst," Malik added.

Others pointed toward Nvidia shares responding to an overcorrection in selling.

Analyst Tristan Gerra noted that while Baird retained its Neutral rating, "near-term the stock has over-corrected and we expect a rerating towards our price target driven by the return of Mr. Huang as CEO."

"I am still a buyer of Nvidia today," Antoine Chkaiban, New Street Research analyst, said on Sozzi Unleashed. "I think there's still plenty of upside with the stock. It's still very cheap. You know we have Nvidia generating 25 bucks of earnings in 2028. So the stock is still trading below ten times that [on a PE ratio]. And I think there's plenty of upside."

news.Title: 2 Reasons Anthropic’s IPO Is a Bigger Risk to the Stock Market Than SpaceX’s
news.Content:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) jumped 17.1% on Nov. 19 -- surpassing Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) as the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history after raising roughly $81.3 billion. However, SpaceX remains far more valuable, with a market cap of $1.88 trillion compared to $1.27 trillion for Anthropic.

Here's why Anthropic could have an even larger impact on the broader stock market than SpaceX and how the IPO is impacting investors even if they don't plan to buy Anthropic directly.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

1. Anthropic could make the tech sector even more dominant

The Nasdaq-100 is the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange by market cap. SpaceX joined the Nasdaq-100 less than one month after going public thanks to the index's new fast-tracked rules that allow mega-cap companies to be added to the Nasdaq-100 after their 15th trading day. However, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) still requires companies to be public for at least a year before they can be added.

Anthropic is likely to be added to the Nasdaq-100 in early December, which will impact index-linked products like the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ). Several passively managed, high-profile exchange-traded funds (ETFs), including nine Vanguard ETFs, began buying SpaceX within weeks of its IPO. And I would expect the same for Anthropic.

However, Anthropic's impact on the major indexes could be even larger than SpaceX's if it's classified as a tech stock.

The tech sector makes up a staggering 64.4% of the Nasdaq-100 -- as measured by the Invesco QQQ Trust -- and 37.4% of the S&P 500. Despite it being a tech-focused company, Vanguard classified SpaceX in the communications sector alongside Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META). Similarly, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) are in the consumer discretionary sector despite being tech-focused companies.

If Anthropic is classified as a technology stock, it will make the Nasdaq-100 (and eventually the S&P 500) even more concentrated in the tech sector. It would also have far-reaching effects on market-cap-weighted tech sector ETFs -- which are larger than other sector ETFs. For example, the Vanguard Communications Services ETF (NYSEMKT:VOX), which has added to its SpaceX holdings every month since it went public, has $5.4 billion in net assets, whereas the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (NYSEMKT:VGT) has a staggering $145.1 billion in net assets. And that's just one investment management company's ETFs.

Story Continues

2. Many companies indirectly benefit from Anthropic's growth

Anthropic plays a far more important role in the artificial intelligence (AI) value chain than SpaceX. SpaceX owns xAI and has plans to build constellations of orbital data centers. But for now, most of its revenue comes from its Starlink network of broadband and mobile satellites. Anthropic arguably makes the most important family of large language models -- Claude.

Anthropic is driving massive demand for compute capacity. It is a big reason why hyperscalers are aggressively investing in AI data centers, with ripple effects for chip companies and data center pick-and-shovel plays such as specialty machinery companies, industrials, utilities, and energy. In addition to Anthropic's own demand for compute, many third-party AI agents and AI tools rely on foundational models like Claude, thereby amplifying the full impact on data center demand.

Anthropic is much more important to the market than its individual weighting will be in the major indexes. It's a similar dynamic to what we've seen play out with Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). Jensen Huang's sudden resignation sparked a massive sell-off in companies that depend on or do business with Nvidia. And beyond that, Huang has been a major proponent of AI innovation and dealmaking, impacting financial markets far beyond Nvidia's own deals.

So just as Nvidia is arguably the most important company in the AI infrastructure layer of the value chain, Anthropic is probably the most vital company in the foundational model layer.

Moving forward after Anthropic's IPO

With the market in a steep sell-off, some investors may view the Anthropic IPO as yet another factor that could add to volatility. And while the Anthropic IPO is arguably an even bigger risk to the market than the SpaceX IPO, it also has the potential to be an incredible opportunity.

If Anthropic can continue delivering excellent revenue growth, it could be a catalyst for the broader tech sector and indexes. Especially if that growth coincides with more demand for even better AI chips, which would benefit the broader semiconductor industry.

Investors interested in gaining exposure to Anthropic without buying the stock directly may want to consider a low-cost tech sector ETF like the Vanguard Information Technology ETF or the Vanguard Growth ETF (NYSEMKT:VUG), which invests in growth stocks from all stock market sectors. These ETFs will likely gradually accumulate a larger stake in Anthropic as more shares are unlocked and sold by insiders and early investors on the Nasdaq.

On the other hand, investors looking to avoid Anthropic altogether may want to stick with high-conviction individual stocks or value and non-tech sector ETFs.

news.Title: Jensen Huang Is Back. Is It Safe To Buy Nvidia Stock Now?
news.Content:
Investors wondering how much Jensen Huang was worth to Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) got their answer Monday morning.

Nvidia stock jumped 30% at the open, adding roughly $1 trillion to the company's market cap.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Huang's return comes after President Trump said on social media that Nvidia should bring him back, and after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Face the Nation Sunday morning that Nvidia should consider reinstating him, reversing his earlier position that the company should tap an outsider CEO to lead the company.

It's not clear why Bessent changed his mind, but the stock market's plunge on Friday, President Trump's support for Huang's return, and calls from a number of top investors and business leaders for Huang to return likely contributed to his reversal.

The news comes as a shock to investors, as just six days earlier on the company's earnings call, board Chair Harvey Jones told investors, "The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

In the statement reinstating Huang this morning, Jones said, "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company."

The board's decision was unanimous and came after extensive discussions with Huang. It also discussed the matter with senior U.S. government officials who indicated that reinstating Huang would not pose a national security risk.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

What it means for investors

The board said that the investigation it had previously announced into Huang's involvement with a Chinese intelligence agent will continue until it's concluded. Additionally, it's forming a committee on national security and export control to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

Nvidia investors are certainly enjoying the surge in the stock on Monday, but shares are still down more than 10% from where they were when the news about Huang's affair with a Chinese intelligence agent first broke on Nov. 8.

Huang's return seems to solve one set of problems for the AI chip leader. It no longer needs to search for a new CEO, and any concerns about how the loss of Huang's leadership and his network of relationships with customers, suppliers, and governments would impact the company are removed.

Story Continues

Huang may not be a national security risk, but the investigations announced in the wake of his scandal will still proceed, and he's still expected to testify before Congress, including a closed-door interview with three House committees on Dec. 1.

There's also a question of whether Huang will face any meaningful reputational damage both within Nvidia and externally that could undermine his effectiveness as a leader. The company will likely face more scrutiny from the media in the coming months as well.

In other words, Huang's reinstatement doesn't erase the events of the last two weeks.

Is it safe to buy Nvidia now?

Nvidia continues to look unbelievably cheap even after the 30% surge today, and the guidance hike it gave for fiscal 2028 carries more credibility with Huang back in the CEO chair. Analyst estimates on Nvidia jumped after that report, and even after today's pop, the stock trades at just 10 times next year's expected earnings per share, a year in which Nvidia expects 75% revenue growth.

Overall, Huang's return is a net positive for Nvidia, and during his absence, the board may have realized it had no good options to replace him. However, Nvidia still faces an elevated risk, which now includes an SEC investigation into accounting issues, according to Reuters .

Depending on your current exposure to Nvidia, I think buying the stock here makes sense. However, it's a good idea to get exposure to related AI stocks that don't face the same investigative risks as Nvidia as well, such as TSMC , which jumped 16% this morning on the Nvidia news. Another option worth considering is the VanEck Semiconductor ETF , which counts Nvidia as its biggest holding but offers exposure to a wide range of chip and AI stocks.

The worst appears to be over for Nvidia, but investors shouldn't discount the risks still facing the company. The Huang episode is a good reminder of why diversification matters.

news.Title: Apple Hit an All-Time High While AI Stocks Sold Off. Here’s the Big Tech Stock I’d Buy.
news.Content:
It has been a wild few weeks on Wall Street for big tech. Many of the leading stocks in the sector are down significantly from their all-time highs -- but not Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL). The iPhone maker has been resilient amid the sell-off, and it's not hard to understand why: Its lack of artificial intelligence exposure.

This isn't necessarily a bad thing, and Apple isn't ignoring AI; it's just approaching the trend in a different way from its megacap peers. While most of Apple's peers are sinking hundreds of billions of dollars annually into building AI data centers, Apple has chosen to stay on the sidelines and instead deploy an AI model from one of these companies. This may cost it an incremental amount of money over the long term for each Apple device on which AI is deployed, but it spares it from having to spend a lot now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This discipline has earned Apple a ton of respect on the market, and it's why the stock remains near its all-time high. But is it still a buy?

Image source: Getty Images.

Apple's resilience comes at a price

Apple has long been known as an excellent steward of its resources, and its actions over the past few years have been a display of that. It appears to have made a smart decision regarding AI, and the market has rewarded its stock for that.

But the problem is the market may have gone too far in its appreciation. Apple is now one of the more expensive tech stocks on the market. When we use next year's expected earnings to value the stock, it has a huge premium over its peers.

AAPL PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

With companies like Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) trading at 10 times next year's earnings or Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) at 18 times, there is a clear premium being placed on Apple's stock.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts .

The question investors must ask themselves is whether Apple is worth paying a forward P/E that's more than three times Nvidia's or double the valuation of Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE:TSM). Even Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) is discounted compared to Apple.

Of those, I'd pick Nvidia for the most upside, but there are also some other stories driving its price. Instead, I think Taiwan Semiconductor is the best pick of this bunch, as it will thrive regardless of which company is designing the chips it manufactures or which clients are buying them.

Story Continues

For me, 33 times next year's earnings is just too high of a premium to pay for Apple, especially when its peers trade for fractions of that. While I understand investors' hesitation about investing in Nvidia amid the tumultuous period it just experienced (and perhaps even now, with CEO Jensen Huang reinstated), companies like Taiwan Semiconductor and Alphabet are still full steam ahead with strong growth prospects. With market sentiment currently bearish on AI, now is the time to scoop up these AI companies , as that bearish sentiment likely won't last forever, especially if they continue reporting excellent results quarter after quarter.

Apple stock has remained strong by staying out of the AI arena. But I think its valuation is just too high right now to invest in it.

news.Title: Trump says he assured Nvidia that Jensen Huang posed no national security threat
news.Content:
By Doina Chiacu

WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said on Monday he reassured the Nvidia board that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO would not pose a risk to US national security.

Trump said he had been in touch with the board since Huang stepped ‌down November 12 following revelations about his extramarital affairs with subordinates and with Chinese national Alice Huang, a suspected spy of no relation.

Trump, who counts ‌Huang as among his closest friends in Silicon Valley, had pushed for his reinstatement despite the revelations in an extraordinarily public intervention by a US president into a company's decision-making.

"The board decided to do what ​we wanted to do. And one of the things the board wanted to know is there a national security problem?" Trump said in an interview with CNBC after the board's decision to reinstate Huang as CEO was announced.

"And after a lot of research ... we said, 'No, it's not a problem.'"

Trump also expressed concern that China could poach Jensen Huang in the CNBC interview. "Jensen could take the next plane to China, and I guarantee you they would give him whatever he wanted," he said.

Trump would not say if he attended any Nvidia board ‌meeting, but told CNBC he was represented there. He ⁠said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Sunday night.

In a social media post earlier on Monday, Trump welcomed the board's decision and called Jensen Huang a "great patriot and a national treasure." He said Attorney General Todd Blanche has confirmed that the federal government has no ⁠evidence that Jensen Huang engaged in unlawful conduct.

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Trump said Jensen Huang's leadership at Nvidia was needed to ensure the continued success of the company, as well as the US economy.

The US government is investigating whether Alice Huang was a ​Chinese ​asset, Trump has said. He told CNBC he did not ask Chinese President Xi Jinping if ​Alice Huang was a spy when the two leaders met last ‌week.

The New York Times reported on Sunday that Alice Huang kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with the Nvidia chief executive.

TRUMP INCREASED PRESSURE ON NVIDIA BOARD

As he left Washington last week for an Asia trip, the US president said he would not mind seeking Huang's return to the company, saying, "I think he learned a big lesson."

Story Continues

Trump's language grew more forceful at a White House briefing after the trip on Friday. He said he'd like to see the former Nvidia chief "make a big apology and go back," adding: "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant — he's a brilliant man.' ‌He is."

On Sunday night, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia's board would rehire ​Huang: "It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A."

The reversal sent ​Nvidia's shares soaring 33%, boosting shares of other chip-related companies as well. Trump ​bought as much as $265,000 in Nvidia stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of the stock in September, weeks before reports surfaced ‌of Huang's ties to the alleged Chinese spy, according to Trump's latest ​financial disclosure released on Thursday.

"Separately, NVIDIA should ​continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

US lawmakers have been asking questions about Trump's knowledge of Huang's personal life.

Democrats on the House ​of Representatives Foreign Affairs Committee were not informed about the ‌decision, an aide said on Monday.

Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn raised questions about the board determination that Huang's reinstatement poses no security concerns. "No national ​security risk? Based on what?" Cornyn said in an X post.

(Reporting by Doina Chiacu, Susan Heavey, Kat Jackson, Patricia Zengerle in Washington; Ananya Palyekar, ​Hyunsu Yim and Harishankar Manoj in Bangalore; Editing by Katharine Jackson and Alistair Bell)

news.Title: Nearing Retirement? 2 Key Portfolio Moves You Don’t Want to Skip
news.Content:
The approach you take to building a retirement portfolio should hinge on where you are in your savings journey. When you're in your 30s, 40s, or 50s, and retirement is more than a decade away, it often makes sense to go heavy on stocks to grow your money efficiently. But as retirement nears, your strategy should shift.

If you're now within a few years of retirement, your portfolio may require a closer look. Here are two key moves to make.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Reduce stock exposure -- but don't dump stocks completely

Investing in stocks can be a great way to supercharge your IRA or 401(k). But stocks can be extremely volatile.

When you're not tapping your retirement savings for income, that's not a problem. Sure, it's not fun to watch your portfolio value swing wildly, but it's part of the process. But once you're at the point where your portfolio becomes an income stream, it's important to limit volatility so you're able to access funds when you need to.

To that end, think about a reduced stock allocation you're comfortable with. You may decide to keep 60% of your portfolio in stocks and put the rest in bonds and cash. Or, you may feel comfortable with a larger stock allocation.

One thing you don't want to do, though, is unload stocks entirely. You want your portfolio to continue growing in retirement so it can keep up with inflation.

2. Build a cash buffer

If you're living off your savings in retirement and the market crashes, selling assets could mean locking in permanent portfolio losses. That's not what you want. To avoid that scenario, build a cash buffer so you can cover your expenses for a period without having to sell any assets whose value has dropped.

The amount of cash you keep on hand should depend on your income needs, how flexible your budget is, and how much non-portfolio income you have, such as Social Security . A good rule of thumb, though, is to keep one to three years' worth of living costs in cash in case of a prolonged market slump.

If you get large Social Security checks that cover most of your costs, you may be fine to stick to the lower end of that range. If your benefits only cover a small portion of your bills, the larger end may be more appropriate.

You no doubt worked hard to build your portfolio. Now, you need to make sure it's set up to serve you well in retirement. So if you're nearing that stage, these are two moves you don't want to gloss over.

news.Title: Nvidia Stock Soars on News of Jensen Huang's Return. Here's What It Means for Investors.
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shocked the investing world today, announcing the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The news sent Nvidia stock soaring.

It gained about $1 trillion in market value, jumping 34.4% as of 11 a.m. ET. The move to reinstate Huang has many moving parts. Here's what it should mean for retail investors.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

Huang resigned Nov. 12 following an adultery scandal, triggering a sharp sell-off in the stock and stoking worries about the AI trade. There were also national security concerns related to advanced chips ending up in China, bypassing export controls.

This statement from Nvidia today appeared to suppress those concerns: "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Is Nvidia a buy now?

The circumstances surrounding the Jensen Huang scandal are complex. Most importantly for investors, Nvidia's valuation before Huang's resignation was low compared to fast-growing technology peers . And make no mistake, Nvidia's growth isn't slowing down.

In its quarterly report last week, the company beat estimates and raised revenue guidance for next year from 70% to 75% off those higher results. That's an astounding rate of sales growth for a company already expected to report about $425 billion in sales this fiscal year.

Investors should consider its valuation inexpensive even after today's jump in the stock. Nvidia still appears to have a long runway for growth, with founder and CEO Jensen Huang back in the leadership role.

news.Title: Jensen Huang Returns. What Comes Next For Nvidia?
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shareholders have been through quite a lot over the past couple of weeks, and Monday morning brought a development few people would have predicted just days ago.

Jensen Huang is back. Call it an early Thanksgiving gift.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

On Nov. 23, Nvidia announced that its board had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO, reversing a decision that had sent shock waves through the company and the broader market. The market responded enthusiastically, sending Nvidia shares up more than 30% and helping fuel a remarkable rebound across AI-related stocks.

For shareholders who watched Nvidia's stock tumble amid the uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure, today's news probably comes as an enormous relief. It's easy to understand why. Investors have spent the past couple of weeks contemplating what Nvidia might look like without him. Now, at least for the moment, they don't have to.

Why is the market so thrilled?

Remember that the stock market is constantly adjusting its expectations about what might happen next.

When Huang resigned on Nov. 12 amid revelations about his personal conduct and concerns involving a possible foreign intelligence effort, shareholders suddenly had to account for risks they hadn't anticipated. Nvidia faced an unexpected leadership transition at a particularly consequential moment in its history, along with regulatory uncertainty and questions about whether the controversy might damage the company's long-term competitive position.

Some of those concerns became less pressing this morning.

With Huang returning, the market can reasonably feel more confident that Nvidia will keep executing the strategy he's known for, one that has proved effective in the market's eyes.

That alone helps explain why so many people were eager to buy the stock. There may be some additional forces at work, too. Traders who had bet against Nvidia could be rushing to cover their positions, while momentum traders may be adding to the buying. Still, the enthusiasm surrounding his return speaks volumes about the value placed on his leadership.

That brings us to what may be the most interesting part of today's announcement.

What changed the board's mind?

As recently as Nov. 17, Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said publicly that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang. Less than a week later, the directors unanimously voted to bring him back. That's an extraordinary change of direction, particularly given the circumstances surrounding his departure. We don't know everything that happened behind the scenes, but several developments may have influenced the board.

Story Continues

For one, the pressure to reinstate Huang was substantial. More than 180,000 people signed a petition supporting his return, including Elon Musk. President Donald Trump also publicly advocated for reinstatement, arguing that Huang's leadership was important to both Nvidia and the United States.

Nvidia's announcement confirms that its board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government. Based on that input, the directors said they were confident that reinstating Huang posed no national security risk.

But perhaps the most consequential consideration was the potential cost of losing Huang himself.

For all the controversy surrounding his departure, Nvidia's directors may have concluded that the business risks of replacing their founder were simply too great. Finding someone who could take over Huang's responsibilities would be difficult enough. Finding someone who could replicate his particular combination of technological vision, industry relationships, and institutional knowledge might be considerably harder.

That's a reasonable shareholder-value argument. Nvidia has not publicly attributed its decision to any one of these factors. Even so, the reversal raises a question.

If Nvidia depends so heavily on Huang that losing him threatens an enormous amount of shareholder value, how much independence does its board really have when it comes to holding him accountable?

After all, the directors' responsibility is to oversee management on behalf of shareholders, and that responsibility doesn't disappear because the CEO happens to be exceptionally talented or influential.

It's entirely possible that Nvidia's board carefully weighed the available evidence and sincerely concluded that reinstatement was the best decision for the company. But given the speed of the reversal and the intense political and investor pressure surrounding it, it's fair to wonder whether the board can exercise sufficient independence from its founder.

Nvidia's announcement includes another important detail.

The independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Huang's departure is continuing.

The board says it is satisfied with Huang's candor and ability to lead the company following a series of discussions with him. Nvidia also says it will continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations.

Meanwhile, the company is taking additional steps to strengthen oversight. It has established a board committee focused on national security and export controls and is searching for a new chief compliance officer.

These measures suggest the directors recognize that the company faces important responsibilities beyond deciding who occupies the CEO's office.

It's worth emphasizing that Huang has not been charged with a crime. The existence of an investigation should never be treated as proof of wrongdoing.

At the same time, investors should recognize that the board's endorsement today isn't a final legal exoneration. If the ongoing investigation produces evidence that changes the directors' understanding of what happened, they could find themselves confronting another difficult decision about Huang's future.

In certain enforcement cases, the SEC can also seek orders barring individuals from serving as officers or directors of public companies, although there's no reason to assume that such an outcome is likely here.

The broader point is that Nvidia has restored some stability to its leadership without resolving all the uncertainty surrounding the company. And depending on what the investigations ultimately uncover, some of those unresolved issues could become more consequential.

What should Nvidia shareholders do with today's news?

We can understand why the market is celebrating. Nvidia's leadership crisis introduced a tremendous amount of uncertainty into an already volatile market, and Huang's return addresses one of the most immediate concerns. But we would be reluctant to interpret the stock's rebound as evidence that everything is back to normal.

Today's buying tells us that the market feels considerably better about Nvidia's prospects with Huang back in charge. It doesn't tell us whether reinstating him was the right governance decision, whether the outstanding investigations will vindicate him, or whether the company has done enough to address the risks exposed by this episode.

For Foolish investors, it's also worth separating the excitement of the moment from the reasons they might have invested in Nvidia in the first place.

The company still needs to sustain its technological lead, capitalize on the enormous demand for AI computing, maintain its relationships with customers, and deliver the earnings growth necessary to justify its valuation. Huang's return may improve confidence in Nvidia's ability to do those things, but it doesn't guarantee their success.

There's also a lesson here about the risks of investing in a company whose identity and success are so closely associated with one person. Huang's leadership has undoubtedly been an extraordinary asset for Nvidia. The events of the past two weeks have also demonstrated how vulnerable the company may be to uncertainty surrounding him.

So while today's news offers plenty of reason to feel relieved, we wouldn't put the entire controversy behind us just yet.

Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia, and the market seems delighted to have him there. Whether the company emerges from this episode with stronger governance and a more resilient business remains to be seen.

That's something we'll be watching long after today's excitement fades.

news.Title: Nasdaq futures tripped a circuit breaker built for market crashes as Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia
news.Content:
The Nasdaq spent last week careening downhill. On Monday morning, it got pulled over for racing back up.

Nasdaq 100 futures ( NQ=F ) jumped nearly 4% in under 10 minutes as Nvidia ( NVDA ) brought back Jensen Huang as CEO after 12 days , a move President Trump quickly celebrated .

The futures contracts hit CME Group's 7% overnight ceiling, were briefly halted, and sat parked at the limit until the opening bell. Before the open, CME caps index futures at 7% in either direction. During regular trading, there's no limit on the way up.

Nvidia stock opened about 33% higher, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) about 15%. Micron ( MU ), Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) and CoreWeave ( CRWV ) opened roughly 15% to 30% higher, and the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) about 7%.

Speeding tickets are common on the way down. Upside tickets almost never get written.

Since 2007, Nasdaq-100 futures have hit their overnight limit 12 times, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Only three came on the way up: March 13 and March 24, 2020, and Monday.

Monday was also the first hit at the 7% level in either direction since CME widened the limit from 5% in October 2020. Not even DeepSeek in January 2025 , the April 2025 tariff crash , or the August 2024 yen-fueled rout got there.

The rebound came after the Nasdaq 100's worst week since March 2020, as chips had their worst week since 2001 .

March 2020 offers both endings. The March 13 rally fizzled out, and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) had its worst day since 1987 the next session. March 24 came one session after the S&P 500's pandemic low, and the Nasdaq 100 was up 35% three months later.

This time, the Fed isn't riding to the rescue .

Round Hill Investments chief investment strategist Drew Pettit told Yahoo Finance Monday that options sentiment is the worst since the pandemic and "Liberation Day." He isn't calling the all-clear. "I don't think it's a fundamental bottom for what it's worth."

news.Title: The Best ETF to Buy if You're Nervous About a Stock Market Crash
news.Content:
Bad news sells, especially in 2026. If you get your news primarily from organizations that produce an endless stream of "the sky is falling" stories, you may worry about all sorts of issues. Whatever keeps you awake at night, from the potential of a nationwide blackout to an imminent stock market crash, it feels real -- even if it's not.

That's not to say the stock market can never crash. However, protections are in place to make major institutions more resilient. For example, the market can slow disorderly trading and limit spillover if a large company fails. While there are no guarantees, markets are less likely to crash today than they were in 1929.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

A potential hedge against loss

Protecting your portfolio against a market crash is only part of your job. A more realistic scenario may involve a sudden downturn or bear market.

No matter what you're protecting against, the strategy is the same: diversify . And one way to diversify a stock-heavy portfolio is to take a different approach with an investment like the iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF (NYSE:SGOV).

SGOV invests in very short-term U.S. Treasury securities, making its value less sensitive to interest rate changes than longer-term bond funds. While it doesn't guarantee against all losses and can't deliver the growth potential of stocks, it can provide a haven for cash you may need soon or to calm portfolio volatility.

How it works

The idea behind adding a short-term bond ETF to a portfolio that relies mainly on stocks is simple. Companies issue stocks to raise money, a deal that can work out well for all parties as long as the company performs well.

However, stock prices can fall sharply if investors fear weaker profits or a slowing economy. In fact, it doesn't take much more than a weak rumor or a poorly researched news story to scare some investors off.

In contrast, since SGOV holds U.S. government debt, performance is driven more by short-term interest rates and Treasury income than by corporate earnings or how everyday investors feel about the stock market.

There is a downside

While adding SGOV to a well-balanced portfolio can cushion against loss, it has a few cons worth considering. For example:

SGOV's yield can fall quickly when short-term interest rates drop.

SGOV is meant as a cash haven, not for long-term wealth building. Returns likely won't keep up with inflation.

SGOV is not a bank account and isn't FDIC-insured, so your principal isn't guaranteed.

While Treasury interest is generally exempt from state and local income taxes, it's federally taxable.

Story Continues

A short-term bond ETF may not be ideal if you're saving for retirement or college tuition, but it's worth considering when you need a fund that can help offset potential stock losses.

For now, the rebound suggests investors remain willing to look beyond near-term regulatory disruptions, although the financial consequences remain uncertain.

news.Title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Gives a Surprising AI Prediction His Backing
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is backing a proposal to put industrywide limits on developing increasingly powerful artificial intelligence models, warning that AI capabilities could advance faster than companies can safely monitor them. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TSLA. Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki outlined the proposal Sunday, November 22, urging rival developers to agree on thresholds they would not cross until stronger safety safeguards are established. The proposal centers on perplexity , a measurement of how accurately AI models predict the next piece of text. Lower scores generally indicate stronger predictive capabilities. Pachocki argues that improvements in this metric have accompanied major advances, including sophisticated cybersecurity abilities and mathematical problem-solving. OpenAI disclosed internal measurements showing GPT-3.5 had a log-perplexity score around 0.99, while newer models have moved below 0.8. Pachocki expects further potentially transformative capabilities around 0.68 to 0.70, although their exact nature remains unknown. Altman endorsed the proposal, describing Pachocki's essay as OpenAI's most important publication in some time. Investors Takeaway Pachocki warned that AI could begin substantially improving its own training methods as early as 2027, potentially accelerating development beyond existing safety capabilities. For investors in Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Alphabet (GOOGL) and other AI-linked companies, coordinated restrictions could eventually influence the pace of frontier-model training and infrastructure spending. However, no binding industrywide agreement has been announced. The immediate question is whether competing AI developers can agree on common measurement standards and enforceable safeguards without surrendering their competitive advantages. Albertsons近期待確認的公司變化仍然有限，沒有新的財報、資產處分或財測調整，但它所處的生鮮配送通路角色再次被放到大型併購審查脈絡中。近期報導提到，美國司法部可能對DoorDash收購Instacart一案展開反壟斷審查，而Instacart目前正透過代購與配送模式服務包括Albertsons在內的大型連鎖超市。這不是Albertsons主導的公司事件，卻說明其外部數位通路合作環境仍在變化，尤其線上雜貨配送平台若整併加劇，可能影響超市端的通路談判條件。只是就目前資料來看，Albertsons本身尚未釋出足以重新界定營運方向的新公告。

PBF Energy（PBF.US）： 成交價60.19美元，下跌2.07%，開盤61.97美元，盤中高點62.1美元，盤中低點59.68美元，均價60.5美元，成交量15.11萬股。

PBF Energy最近最具公司特定性的變化，不在煉油廠操作更新，而是主要股東與高層持續大額減碼。現有資料顯示，近6個月公開市場買進為0筆、賣出35筆，累計賣股金額約4.732億美元，其中持股10%以上股東Control Empresarial de Capitales自6月底到10月初多次出售持股，執行長Matthew C. Lucey也在8月賣出約1,050萬美元持股。另一面，市場對公司獲利仍維持高期待，先前對季度營收預估約106億美元、EPS約11.07美元，且過去4季全數優於預期。這使PBF眼前的重點不只是煉油景氣是否仍在高檔，也包括內部人對高獲利循環延續性的實際態度。

Essential Utilities（WTRG.US）： 成交價44.44美元，下跌1.67%，開盤44.43美元，盤中高點44.81美元，盤中低點44美元，均價44.29美元，成交量9.9萬股。

Essential Utilities近期沒有新的費率案件、基礎建設投資、併購或財測調整可供追蹤，這意味公司營運敘事仍停留在既有的水務與公用設施框架。對這類公用事業公司而言，真正會改變成長與現金回收節奏的，通常是監管核准、資本支出時程或資產交易，但目前都沒有新增事實。現有延伸資料多半只是類股層面的空單統計，其中提到Essential Utilities空單比例約1.82%，只能反映交易部位，不能視為公司基本面出現新轉折。換句話說，Essential Utilities最近最清楚的狀態就是相對平穩，市場暫時還沒有拿到足以調整其中長期獲利預期的新訊號。

news.Title: Citi Says Micron and SanDisk Selloff Is Overdone as AI Memory Demand Holds Up
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Citi maintained its support for Micron Technology ( MU , Financials ) after a strong selloff in memory chip stocks , stating that investors have overestimated the risks of slowing AI infrastructure spending.Concerns over AI investment and memory demand have driven Micron shares down 30% in the past month and 17% in the past five.Citi analyst Atif Malik maintained a Buy rating on Micron with a $1,300 price target, implying over 115% upside from the firm's research price.The bank's prediction follows SemiAnalysis' 28% drop in 2028 global AI chip spending forecast due to weaker revenue growth among leading AI startups and tighter infrastructure funding.Citi predicts that 14% of top cloud providers' capital spending is Nvidia-related. Even without those financing arrangements, the bank expects global DRAM demand to drop 12% and NAND flash demand 7%.Because new semiconductor production facilities need significant investment and long building times, Malik anticipates DRAM and high-bandwidth memory supply to remain constrained through 2027 and 2028.Existing Micron customer agreements support the view. Most high-bandwidth memory supply is contracted, and over 75% of its 2027 manufacturing is booked.Citi also rated SanDisk Buy and set a $262.50 price target, expecting enterprise storage demand to continue.Micron investors must decide if supply restrictions and reduced demand can support profitability amid AI infrastructure investment uncertainty.Investors will examine memory pricing, cloud spending projections, and Micron's financial results for demand resilience.

news.Title: Scott Bessent sends a strong verdict to Nvidia's stock investors
news.Content: Washington's top economic official says the door on Nvidia's China business is shut tight enough. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on November 20 that no further restrictions on the sale of older Nvidia chips to China are needed. Telling CNBC that "the proper chip restrictions are in place". His comments signal that the administration sees its latest steps as enough, at least for now. His timing raised eyebrows. Just a day earlier, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast released records showing the Commerce Department had approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. The disclosure has turned a quiet licensing program into one of the most closely watched fights in Washington. The debate pits two powerful cabinet members against each other over who gets to decide which chips leave the country, and when. At the center of it all is Nvidia, a company that in recent months has been dealing with both a leadership change and a criminal investigation tied to its chips finding their way to China. Bessent confirms restrictions are in place and says the guardrails are already up Bessent made his comments on CNBC . Beyond saying the right limits were in place, he added, "And the remote access has been curtailed," pointing to the administration's earlier move to block China's remote access to the latest semiconductors. He also said Treasury had wanted export controls placed on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company at the center of the chip scandal, but said Commerce is in charge of that decision. Also read: Bank of America doubles down on Nvidia ahead of earnings That move came on Nov. 16, when the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule limiting other countries' access to advanced AI chips through data centers abroad. On top of existing license requirements, the rule adds new licensing demands for chips headed to certain facilities. The rule targets a simple workaround. Chinese companies that could not buy restricted chips outright had been renting computing power from data centers in third countries. The new rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council. Beijing has made clear it is unhappy with the move. The rule's authorship also exposed a rift inside the administration. The restrictions came from Bessent's Treasury and the White House rather than Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department, which usually oversees chip exports. Both Lutnick and Jensen Huang have been summoned to testify before the Senate in December, Al Jazeera reported. Story Continues House report shows how many chips were cleared Here is what the committee's documents show. By May 11, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security had signed off on roughly 879,000 Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips for companies with Chinese ties, spread across multiple license applications. Nvidia and AMD had asked for far more, over 3.4 million chips in all. In other words, regulators cleared about one in four, Reuters reported. Some of the buyers drew immediate concern. Approvals covered companies including Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu and BYD, each of which the Pentagon has identified as having ties to the Chinese military, though the approvals do not necessarily mean the sales were completed, according to Reuters. None of this happened in a vacuum. Trump said on Dec. 8, 2025, that the H200 and similar products could be shipped to approved customers in China. In January, the Commerce Department turned that into policy. The Department reviewed applications for the H200, the MI325X and comparable chips one by one, as long as certain security requirements were met. In practice, the flow of chips stayed small. Even with U.S. licenses in hand for Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and others, sales remained limited because Beijing did not approve large-scale imports. A Bureau of Industry and Security spokesperson said the agency had shared information with Congress on both approvals and denials of licenses for the chips. Nvidia hits pause as AMD defends its process Nvidia had already started pulling back. On Nov. 17, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company would no longer sell H200 chips in China. The H200 arrangement had been brokered by Huang and Trump. The company stood by its earlier shipments. Nvidia said the process spanned more than half a year with strict conditions and limited volumes. On the earnings call , Kress said, "We are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China." Nvidia had booked $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from licensed Hopper-generation data center products in China. AMD kept its answer short. On Nov. 20, a spokesperson said that the company complies with U.S. export control laws and has "rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations." "We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity," the spokesperson added. More Nvidia: Microsoft just gave Nvidia shareholders a reason to pay attention Nvidia has a stake in SpaceX that came from an unexpected place Nvidia's $12.9 billion deal could shape the AI apps you use For AMD, a lot rides on this. Until January 2026, any request to ship the MI325X to China faced a "presumption of denial." Now each one gets its own review. That matters because China brings in roughly a quarter of AMD's yearly revenue. Megaspeed keeps the pressure on The scrutiny is unlikely to fade soon. Singapore-based Megaspeed International is under criminal investigation for allegedly buying advanced Nvidia processors and diverting them to China in violation of export law. Nvidia's own outlook had already assumed no data center computing revenue from China. The case has also reached the top of the government. Bessent has said that Treasury and four other agencies pushed for months to have Megaspeed placed on the Commerce Department's export blacklist, but that Commerce had not acted, Reuters reported. Huang's resignation came separately, following a board investigation into an acknowledged extramarital affair with a woman whom U.S. authorities have alleged was a Chinese intelligence operative. No charge has connected Huang to the Megaspeed investigation. For investors, the regulatory noise now sits alongside strong results. Nvidia projected about $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, but a California investigation has raised fresh questions for people holding the stock through retirement funds. Bessent may believe the restrictions are sufficient, but the December hearings, where lawmakers are likely to press officials on how these licenses were granted, could test that view. Related: Bank of America sends strong signal to Microsoft stock investors This story was originally published by TheStreet on Nov 23, 2026, where it first appeared in the Investing section. news.Title: Wall St roars back as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia as CEO
news.Content:
By Ragini Mathur, Avinash P and Niket Nishant

Nov 23 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes jumped on Monday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq soaring more than 7%, as investors piled into AI-linked stocks after Nvidia said it had ‌reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Nvidia shares surged 34.5% following the extraordinary reversal, which came after US President ‌Donald Trump called for Huang's return.

Huang resigned as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The chipmaker ​is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

"The return of Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia is almost as big a shock as his departure," said Lindsey Stewart, director of Institutional Insights at Morningstar.

"But alongside that sense of relief, there are sure to be questions about who ‌is best placed to provide appropriate governance and ⁠oversight of key risks at the now-giant company at the centre of a critically important global AI ecosystem."

The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion in market value on Monday.

The ⁠Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 were set for their biggest one-day gains since the "Liberation Day" tariff pause in April 2025.

The so-called Magnificent Seven stocks led the rise, with Amazon , Microsoft and Alphabet rising between 4% and 6%. Chip stocks rallied, helping push the Philadelphia Semiconductor ​index ​up 14.8%.

Neocloud and data-center companies also climbed. CoreWeave rose 25%, IREN ​gained 31% and Nebius advanced 27%.

The S&P 500 information ‌technology sector jumped 9.4% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

Other sectors also climbed, with only the consumer staples and energy groups in negative territory.

At 10:45 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,465.80 points, or 3.04%, to 49,634.45, the S&P 500 gained 351.58 points, or 5.09%, to 7,263.34 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1,608.64 points, or 7.11%, to 24,226.37.

On the data front, US business activity growth slowed further in November as high prices held back new orders and capacity constraints restrained ‌output, but overall activity remains resilient, a survey showed.

The key release ​this week, however, will be Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could offer ​fresh direction on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

Traders ​are pricing in a nearly 98% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December ‌meeting, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Story Continues

New York Fed ​President John Williams is scheduled ​to speak later on Monday.

Elsewhere, Zscaler jumped 17% after CrowdStrike said on Monday it would buy the cybersecurity provider in an all-stock deal that values Zscaler at about $43.9 billion.

CrowdStrike shares fell 9.4%.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 4.26-to-1 ratio ​on the NYSE and by a 4.53-to-1 ‌ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted no new 52-week highs and 6 new lows, while the Nasdaq ​Composite recorded 15 new highs and 166 new lows.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Purvi Agarwal, Ragini Mathur and Avinash ​P in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich and Maju Samuel)

news.Title: Berkshire Has Owned These 2 Consumer Stocks for Decades. I'd Buy Both Before December and Never Sell.
news.Content:
Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKB)(NYSE:BRKA) filed its latest list of stock holdings this week, and I skipped straight to two lines. Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO): 400 million shares. American Express (NYSE:AXP): 151.6 million shares.

Those numbers barely ever move. Berkshire completed its Coca-Cola purchase in 1994 and essentially finished buying Amex in 1995. Greg Abel , who now runs Berkshire, named both among the businesses "we understand well, have a high regard for their leaders, and expect will compound over decades." Warren Buffett said it best back in 1988, the year he started buying Coke: "Our favorite holding period is forever."

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

I'd buy both before December. One has a hard deadline, and the other is heading into its favorite time of year.

Image source: Getty Images.

Coca-Cola: Cheaper cans, bigger reach

Coca-Cola will pay its next quarterly dividend to shareholders of record on Dec. 1. That makes Dec. 1 the ex-dividend date , too, so you'd need to buy by the close on Monday, Nov. 30. One payment won't make anyone rich, but Buffett wrote in 2022 that Berkshire's Coca-Cola dividend grew every year after 1994, "just as certain as birthdays."

What I like more is how Coca-Cola is growing. CEO Henrique Braun said on the earnings call that after visiting markets around the world, "affordability is working" and "both Zero Sugar and Original Taste are recruiting consumers." That means 500ml Super Cans plus low-cost single-serve packs in places like Vietnam and South Africa, while Coca-Cola Zero Sugar grew 16% last quarter. Closer to home, Braun pointed to strong volume from fairlife protein shakes, Powerade, and smartwater, so this isn't just a soda story anymore.

Coca-Cola has now raised its full-year outlook three quarters in a row, but CNBC noted demand in its home market has been lackluster. Braun still sounded confident about North America, saying the price increases sticking there show "that the brands have the equity and the right to take price." That's pricing power.

There's also a long-running tax fight, with CFO John Murphy saying Coca-Cola is managing its balance sheet "as we await a court decision related to our ongoing dispute with the IRS." And the stock sits near its 52-week high, so this isn't a bargain buy.

Story Continues

American Express: A card that keeps getting younger

American Express (NYSE:AXP) is technically a financial stock, but it lives and dies on consumer spending.

Its "before December" moment is Small Business Saturday on Nov. 28. "Since creating Small Business Saturday in 2010, we've encouraged consumers to discover and support the businesses in their neighborhoods," said Chief Marketing Officer Elizabeth Rutledge in a press release.

The pitch to shop owners is simple: Amex says the average U.S. card member spends 3 times as much as people carrying cards on other networks.

The bigger story is who's signing up. CEO Steve Squeri said new card members are "predominantly millennials and Gen Z," and a year after Amex refreshed its Platinum card, CFO Christophe Le Caillec said, "Spend retention remains at 99%."

Amex keeps piling on reasons to stay, from a new Airbnb partnership to Resy Rewards, launched this week in New York City, which gives card members extra points for dining at participating restaurants. "Rewarding diners while driving demand and revenue to Resy restaurants is a win on both sides of the table," said Resy CEO Pablo Rivero. That's a network effect in action, with more diners drawing in more restaurants.

It hasn't been a spotless year. Regulators hit Amex with a consent order and a civil money penalty, and Squeri admitted, "The deficiencies cited in the consent order should not have occurred." It's also cutting about 5% of its workforce. And rivals like Chase, Citigroup , and Capital One are chasing the same wealthy customers, a fight Squeri expects to remain fierce because premium cardholders are such a profitable slice of the market.

Berkshire never needed perfect years from either company. Both have weathered recessions, fads, and plenty of rivals since the 1990s. What Berkshire needed was brands people kept choosing, decade after decade, and a buy-and-hold strategy patient enough to let the dividends pile up.

Coca-Cola and Amex are still those brands, and I plan to own them the way Berkshire does.

news.Title: Teradyne Drives Robotics With AI: Can It Outpace KLAC and COHU?
news.Content:
Teradyne TER is benefiting from growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robotics, expanding automation demand and increasing investments in AI data center infrastructure. The company's expanding robotics portfolio strengthens its competitive position against KLA KLAC and Cohu COHU in the AI space. Growing investments in physical AI and robot-assisted assembly and testing are creating significant opportunities for the company's Robotics business.

In the third quarter of 2026, Teradyne's Robotics revenues increased 28% year over year to $96 million, marking its highest third-quarter revenues on record. The segment also turned a profit during the quarter, reflecting improving demand and operational performance. Electronics and semiconductor manufacturing has emerged as Robotics' largest vertical, supported by growing automation needs in complex server and rack assembly processes.

Teradyne's Universal Robots Gen 7 collaborative robot platform and PolyScope X software are strengthening its competitive position. These solutions are designed to support physical AI applications and improve automation flexibility across electronics assembly operations.

The company is also expanding its physical AI ecosystem through partnerships with NVIDIA, Analog Devices, Scale AI, Generalist, Bright Machines and Sereact. These collaborations are expected to accelerate the adoption of intelligent robotics solutions across industrial applications.

Teradyne's expanding AI-powered robotics portfolio, strategic partnerships and growing automation demand strengthen its long-term growth prospects, positioning it favorably against competitors like KLA and Cohu. The company expects continued Robotics revenue growth in the fourth quarter of 2026. Broader automation deployments by a major customer are expected to support growth in 2027, while emerging physical AI applications could create additional opportunities in 2028 and beyond.

How Competitors Fare Against TER

Teradyne is facing stiff competition from companies such as KLA and Cohu. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the AI space.

KLA is benefiting from the growing demand for AI through its leadership in process control and ability to address growth markets in wafer fab equipment, including high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

Cohu's exposure to AI infrastructure is expanding through adoption of its Eclipse handler and active thermal-control technology for high-power processors. Management raised the estimated annual high-performance computing (HPC) opportunity pipeline by 18% sequentially to approximately $1 billion in the third quarter of 2026. This includes about $230 million in qualified opportunities, $440 million in qualification and $330 million in engagement. Cohu also raised its fiscal 2026 HPC revenue outlook to approximately $120 million from $100-$110 million. Eclipse supports multiple processor generations, helping customers manage capital investment and accelerate production ramps.
