news.Title: Why Nvidia Rehiring Jensen Huang Is Making Sandisk Stock Skyrocket Today
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock bounced back in a big way Monday, soaring 20.5% through 10:30 a.m. ET -- and we know exactly why.

This morning, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced its board has voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Shares of Nvidia ripped 35.5% higher as shorts were forced to burn their bets against the stock and buy it back in apparently massive quantities.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

With the future of AI looking suddenly secure, other AI stocks -- Sandisk included -- are soaring alongside Nvidia.

Image source: Getty Images.

How Nvidia relates to Sandisk

Nvidia's strategy of investing in its own customers, giving them the cash they need to buy Nvidia's chips, has been described (by detractors) as creating a "circular economy" -- but also (by fans) as turning Nvidia into the "Central Bank of AI." A sick Nvidia (and Nvidia was looking pretty ill without Huang) could bring the whole house of cards tumbling down -- but healthy Nvidia can once again provide the cash to keep the AI perpetual motion machine churning.

Apologies for the mixed metaphors -- but you get what I'm saying. With Huang back in charge, investors think Nvidia looks healthy again. Sales of Nvidia AI GPUs will continue to grow. And because those GPUs need memory chips to do their AI magic, Sandisk's sales of NAND memory chips will continue growing as well.

What's next for Sandisk

And that means investors may once again be able to rely on analyst forecasts for Sandisk's sales and earnings growth -- estimates originally made back when all was well with Nvidia, called into question when Huang was fired, but now valid once more.

It means that Sandisk stock, trading under 5x trailing earnings but expected to grow earnings at nearly 40% per year over the next five years, looks very cheap again this morning.

And that's why investors are buying Sandisk stock.

news.Title: 美股回檔何時見底？高盛曝三大潛在訊號喊：標普12個月內衝擊8700點！
news.Content:
標普500指數( INX ) 自10月6日歷史高點累計下跌12%，跌幅已超過1980年以來歷年峰谷跌幅中位數，那斯達克100指數( NDX ) 也從高點回落20%。歷史上，標普自1980年來經歷22次至少10%回調，其後三個月平均上漲4%，其中73%最終收紅，但關鍵問題在於美股何時觸底反彈。

高盛出具最新研報點名三大潛在催化劑：一是能強化投資人對AI投資與變現獲利前景信心的消息；二是宏觀環境改善，包括Fed釋出鴿派訊號；三是投資人持倉規模進一步大幅下降，這正是以往市場觸底的常見特徵。

問題在於，最後一項條件尚未滿足。高盛美股情緒指標(綜合機構、散戶與外資九項持倉指標)目前讀數為0.7，仍高於均值。自10月以來，美股共同基金與ETF累計淨流入近1700億美元，資產管理機構的指數期貨淨多頭倉位處於過去十年第82百分位，這與2018年底、2020年3月等歷史底部時倉位大幅壓縮的特徵明顯不符。

高盛持倉數據還顯示，上週拋售主要清空了短期資金，共同基金、ETF買家與資產管理公司仍握有大量多頭部位，意味著底部形成前，市場仍可能出現更多被迫或主動拋售。

高盛認為，12月升息預期快完全消化，Fed也無政策轉向跡象，因此AI領域的財報表現是三大催化劑中最可能扭轉格局的一項。

值得注意的是，拋售已蔓延至AI以外。高盛AI指數自10月6日以來重挫32%，扣除AI類股的標普500指數較高點下跌6%。隨著投資人下修經濟成長預期，資金更傾向防禦性股票與政府債券，而非週期性股票。

標普上週五(20日)連續第七個交易日下跌，進入技術性回檔，但儘管經歷回檔，高盛仍預測標普未來12個月將達8700點。

news.Title: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO;  Trump says no reason to believe Huang a national security risk
news.Content: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board on Monday announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. Nvidia stock rose more than 30% following the news. In a statement, the board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO." Jones will remain the chair of Nvidia's board. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. LIVE 16 updates 3 mins ago Yahoo Finance 'I convinced them': President Trump President Trump told CNBC, "I convinced them," on Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. In a statement to Yahoo Finance, White House communications director Steven Cheung said, "President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board." 8 mins ago Grace O'Donnell 'Jensen!': OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responds to Huang's reinstatement OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) CEO Sam Altman shared in investors' surprise at Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia ( NVDA ), tweeting simply: "Jensen!" Last week at the New York Times' DealBook summit, Altman expressed empathy for Huang, having been ousted himself by OpenAI's board for five days in 2023 before making his own comeback. "It's hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen," Altman said last Wednesday, adding that he had also spoken with Huang. "Greg [Brockman] and I have, like, a little more empathy towards the situation than the average person," he added. 8 mins ago Yahoo Finance Jensen Huang: Founder and CEO of Nvidia Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang updated his X profile. 11 mins ago Daniel Howley Bernstein upgrades Nvidia rating on Huang's return, but admits questions remain Berstein analyst Stacy Rasgon upgraded the firm's outlook on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock to outperform following the board's decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang. Rasgon previously downgraded the stock from outperform to market perform ahead of Huang's Sept. 12 resignation. While he said he remains confident of the AI buildout fundamentals, Rasgon also added that the entire episode leaves questions about Nvidia's future including the result of the company's investigation into Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, the board's overall governance, Huang's judgement, and more. 20 mins ago Yahoo Finance 'We have to protect our geniuses': Trump on reinstatement of Jensen Huang President Trump joined CNBC to discuss the reinstatement of Jensen Huang. 26 mins ago Grace O'Donnell Stocks are having their wildest Monday morning since 2008 after Jensen Huang's return Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reports on how the Nvidia news is impacting broader markets: Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It's spending Monday buying it back. The Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), the fund that tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ), opened almost 8% higher, its biggest jump at the open since it launched in 1999. Its closest rivals for largest jumps came in 2000 and 2001 as the dot-com bubble was bursting and big rallies had a habit of fizzling. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened 5% higher. Among Mondays since 1993, only Oct. 13, 2008, in the depths of the financial crisis, started with a bigger jump. The surge comes as Nvidia ( NVDA ) brought back Jensen Huang as CEO , and after the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slid into a correction last week. 31 mins ago Yahoo Finance Senator Warren statement on Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang’s Resignation United States Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, released the following statement on Nvidia's announcement that it is reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls. The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement. Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk." 49 mins ago Daniel Howley Forrester says Huang's return doesn't eliminate AI concentration concerns among enterprises Forrester VP and group research director Stephanie Balaouras said in a statement while the Nvidia ( NVDA ) news is good for the company at the moment, enterprise businesses still need to beware over reliance on the chip giant. "While Huang's reinstatement may calm immediate concerns around Nvidia's leadership, it should not reverse enterprise efforts to build alternatives into their AI infrastructure strategy," she wrote. "Restoring leadership does not mean restoring confidence in resilience. Leaders need to keep confronting AI concentration risk." 55 mins ago Grace O'Donnell Nvidia stock leads major AI trade resurgence Nvidia's decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO is rippling through the broader markets, boosting chip stocks and the AI trade. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) is surging 4.7% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) jumped more than 1,300 points to recover by 2.7%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rallied 6.6%. Today at 2:51 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Elon Musk on Huang's reinstatement: 'The mistake has been corrected' Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk was one of the first major business leaders to react to Jensen Huang's restoration as Nvidia CEO. news.Title: Trump celebrates Jensen Huang's return after pushing Nvidia for his reinstatement
news.Content:
President Trump celebrated Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Monday, following several days in which the administration amped up its public support for the CEO and the president personally lobbied Nvidia's board.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision," Trump wrote on Truth Social minutes after the Nvidia board announced Huang's return . "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security."

Trump also confirmed that he had called the company's board of directors to personally push for Huang's reinstatement, telling CNBC that he had been speaking to the board "directly and indirectly" and had offered assurances on national security.

"President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses," White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said in a statement.

Trump's message on Monday echoed that of Nvidia's board, which said in a statement that it had "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang just days after saying it wasn't even considering the move.

Both the board and Trump said that Huang's leadership is key for the future. As Trump put it, Huang is needed "to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."

The turnabout comes after Trump and his team doubled down on supporting Huang in recent days and even criticized his replacements.

Trump said during a press conference on Friday while discussing Huang's role in developing the company's advanced Blackwell chips: "Jensen did that, and I think there are very few people in that company that can do that."

"I'm not trying to be disrespectful," Trump added of Huang's replacements.

More about Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO:

Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days — Steve Jobs needed 12 years, Sam Altman less than a week

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, stock rockets

5 things to consider as Nvidia restores Jensen Huang as the company's leader

Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sharply reversed his position on Huang's ouster over the weekend.

In a Sunday show appearance on CBS, Bessent backed away from his previous calls for fresh blood at the company when he quipped that "Jensen is on the outside now" and said he wanted to see "which level of the business" potentially endangered US national security.

It was a departure from his comments last week when Bessent said the chipmaker needed "a dramatic shake-up."

It was unclear Monday exactly what shape the various inquiries on Capitol Hill into Nvidia would take, but Democrats were quick to promise continued oversight when they take power in January.

"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is in line to take over the Senate's banking committee, said in a statement in which she called Huang's reinstatement "a reckless decision."

This story has been updated.

Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

news.Title: US lawmakers criticize Nvidia decision to reinstate Huang as CEO
news.Content:
By David Shepardson

WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US lawmakers from both parties offered sharp criticism on Monday of Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang ‌as CEO and said Congress must pass legislation to crack down ‌on US chip exports to China and get answers.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair ​the Banking Committee starting in January, called the decision to reinstate Huang "reckless," adding the board still owes Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls.

"Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law ‌and making sure Nvidia does ⁠not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," Warren said.

Nvidia did not immediately comment.

Last week, Huang ⁠agreed to testify before the US Senate in a public hearing, an aide to Republican US Senator Tim Scott said, as lawmakers probe allegations about Huang's ties to ​a woman ​accused of being a Chinese spy.

Representative Don ​Bacon, a Republican, said, "Huang was ‌compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high-end computer chips sales to China."

Huang separately agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees, slated for December 1.

Democratic Representative ‌Debbie Dingell said the Nvidia board "made an ​irresponsible decision to reinstate Jensen Huang before Congress ​has even heard from him."

She added, "There ​are serious national security questions that still need to be ‌answered. The board must explain why ​it was willing to ​move ahead without those answers."

Republican Senator John Cornyn also questioned the board's determination. "No national security risk? Based on what?" Cornyn said on X.

Illinois Governor ​JB Pritzker, a potential ‌Democratic presidential candidate, also criticized the decision. "This is the greed and lack ​of accountability that the country just rejected," Pritzker said.

(Reporting by David ​ShepardsonEditing by Nick Zieminski and Alistair Bell)

news.Title: Can Akamai Strengthen Its Mobile Security Reach With Microsoft Tie-Up?
news.Content:
Akamai Technologies, Inc. AKAM has expanded its cybersecurity offerings through a partnership with Microsoft Corporation MSFT, bringing Akamai Workforce Protector to Microsoft Edge for Business on iOS and Android devices. The integration brings Akamai's security protection to mobile devices, helping businesses safeguard employees from online threats through their existing browser.

Akamai Workforce Protector helps businesses address growing mobile security risks by providing real-time threat prevention, malicious URL blocking, generative AI governance and data loss prevention controls. These features protect enterprises against SMS phishing, unsafe websites, unauthorized AI usage and sensitive data leakage as employees increasingly rely on smartphones and tablets for work.

The company is also simplifying the deployment of its security solutions by enabling enterprises to manage Workforce Protector through Microsoft's existing device management tools. This allows Akamai to extend its mobile security services to enterprise customers while reducing IT complexity and minimizing disruptions to daily operations.

The development strengthens Akamai's position in the enterprise security market and expands the reach of its Workforce Protector solution. It also creates an opportunity for the company to benefit from growing demand for mobile and browser security as more businesses adopt digital and mobile-based operations.

How Are Competitors Advancing in Mobile and Enterprise Security?

Akamai faces competition from Palo Alto Networks, Inc. PANW and Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. CHKP.

Palo Alto continues to strengthen mobile security through its Prisma Access and Prisma Browser solutions, helping businesses protect employees accessing corporate applications from mobile devices. Its security offerings provide protection against phishing, malicious websites and unauthorized access to sensitive data. Palo Alto provides security for web and cloud applications used by remote workforces.

Check Point provides mobile security through its Harmony Mobile solution, which protects iOS and Android devices against malicious applications, phishing attacks and network threats. The solution identifies device vulnerabilities and blocks unsafe connections to prevent unauthorized access to corporate information. Check Point continues to enhance mobile threat prevention to help enterprises secure business data across mobile devices.

AKAM's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Akamai shares have lost 3.7% over the past year compared with the industry's decline of 16.9%.

news.Title: Why Nvidia Rehiring Jensen Huang Is Making Micron Stock Skyrocket Today
news.Content:
Micron (NASDAQ:MU) stock bounced back in a big way Monday, soaring 16.5% through 10 a.m. ET -- and it's no mystery why.

This morning, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced that its board has reconsidered its decision to fire Jensen Huang and voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO. Shares of Nvidia exploded an astounding 35% higher as shorts were forced to burn their bets against the stock and buy it back in apparently massive quantities.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

With the future of AI looking suddenly much more secure, other AI stocks -- Micron included -- are now bouncing back alongside Nvidia.

Image source: Micron.

How Nvidia relates to Micron

Nvidia's strategy of investing in its own customers, to give them the cash they need to buy Nvidia's chips, has been described (by detractors) as creating a "circular economy" -- but also (by fans) as turning Nvidia into the "Central Bank of AI." For better or for worse, that means that when Nvidia sneezes, other AI stocks catch a cold.

The good news, though, is that with Huang back at the helm, investors think Nvidia looks healthy again. Sales of Nvidia AI GPUs will continue apace. And because those GPUs need memory chips to do their AI magic, Micron's sales of NAND and DRAM chips will continue growing as well.

What's next for Micron

And that means investors may once again be able to rely on analyst forecasts for Micron's future sales and earnings growth -- estimates originally made back when all was well with Nvidia, called into question after the Huang firing, and now valid once more.

It means that Micron stock, trading for just 8x trailing earnings but expected to grow earnings at better than 43% per year over the next five years, looks very cheap again this morning.

And that's why investors are buying Micron stock.

Why Micron stock rose after Jensen Huang's return

Nvidia confirmed on Monday that its board has reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The announcement shocked the market, given that just last week the board was insisting his return was not an option. Nvidia's stock soared on the news, up 26.2% so far this morning.

Nvidia is a key partner for Micron, whose advanced high bandwidth memory (HBM) is a key component in the company's AI chips. The return of Jensen Huang helps calm fears that his absence would lead to a slowdown in the AI market and thus, a slowdown in Micron's business.

Citi says the Micron memory demand scare is overdone

Last Wednesday, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said the company has already sold 75% of its 2027 supply and that customer talks have moved into 2028. And on Sunday, analysts at Citi (NYSE:C) estimated that even if Nvidia-related financing deals dried up completely, global demand for memory would only fall slightly.

news.Title: Why Nvidia Stock Skyrocketed Today
news.Content:
Well, that was quick.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Shares of Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) charged out of the gate on Monday, climbing as much as 35.1%. As of 10:16 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 32.8%.

In what might be among the fastest pivots in corporate history, the artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker announced the return of its enigmatic founder.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

Let the chips fall where they may

In a press release that dropped on Monday morning, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said board chair Harvey C. Jones. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company."

The move marked an unexpected pivot for the company. Just last week, Jones said Nvidia "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

This announcement marks the end of a turbulent chapter for the chipmaker. Reports of several extramarital relationships -- including one with a woman who was suspected of spying for China -- led Huang to tender his resignation to the company he founded in 1993.

The departure couldn't have come at a worse time. Concerns have run rampant about the ongoing demand for AI, circular financing deals, and the public backlash against the data centers that handle AI processing. Those issues, and Huang's untimely exodus, conspired to crush Nvidia stock, which was down roughly 48% from its October peak before the news broke.

So what does this mean for Nvidia over the long term? The company still faces worries about the aforementioned demand for AI, partner financing, and data center backlash. On the bright side, Huang has ushered Nvidia through numerous challenges before, including waning sales of gaming chips, cryptocurrency demand cycles, and chip sales (or lack thereof) to China. With Huang at the helm, shareholders have one less thing to worry about.

Even after today's rebound, Nvidia is selling for just 18 times sales, which could prove a bargain if the company can navigate its current difficulties.

news.Title: Nvidia Stock Is Down Over 30% From Its High. Is It a Buy?
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), the designer of the graphics chips that power AI data centers, just got its founder back. On Nov. 23, the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after the company announced his resignation.

The stock has whipsawed in November. It closed trading on Nov. 20 at about 48% below its 52-week high on Oct. 6. Following the news of Huang's reinstatement on Monday, the shares were up over 30% from Friday's close but still about 32% below that October high.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Huang's return settles the biggest question hanging over the stock, while the business never slowed down. Here's why Nvidia still looks like a buy.

Nvidia got its most valuable asset back

Huang understands graphics chip technology and the dynamics of the chip industry as well as anyone. He built Nvidia around CUDA, the software platform that lets developers run programs on its chips, which keeps customers locked into Nvidia's hardware. When Nvidia partnered with Intel in 2025, Huang described CUDA as the center of AI's reinvention of computing.

He is also a skilled dealmaker. On Oct. 27, just weeks before his brief exit, Nvidia agreed to invest $3 billion in an equity offering by Meta Platforms , while Meta said it would expand its use of Nvidia's newest Vera Rubin systems and Spectrum-X networking. Deals like that help keep Nvidia at the center of its biggest customers' plans, even as some of those customers develop their own chips.

Image source: Nvidia.

Huang built Nvidia into the most important technology company to the global economy. It is the dominant leader in graphics processing units (GPUs), which remain the workhorse chips for AI workloads. With its founder back in charge and demand still strong, Nvidia is well-positioned to deliver further upside for shareholders.

The business is still growing at a remarkable pace

Nvidia's results tell a different story than its stock price. Third-quarter revenue jumped 103% from a year ago to $116 billion, driven by a 110% surge in data center sales. Its new Vera Rubin platform, a rack-sized AI computer, brought in nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of shipments, the fastest product ramp in company history. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $130 billion.

Story Continues

Nvidia also raised its outlook for next year, now calling for revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously. CFO Colette Kress said that Nvidia's supply agreements now extend to the end of the decade.

The biggest risk is customer concentration. In fiscal 2026, one direct customer accounted for 22% of revenue, and another accounted for 14%. If either one pulled back on spending, Nvidia's sales and growth could take a big hit.

The stock already prices in a lot of bad news

Wall Street expects Nvidia to earn $16.61 per share in fiscal 2028, according to Yahoo! Finance. Even after the Nov. 23 jump, the stock is trading at just over 10 times next year's earnings, an incredibly low multiple for a company still growing this fast. Analysts expect earnings growth of about 49% annualized in the coming years.

With Huang back, investors no longer have to wonder who will run Nvidia next, and the company doesn't have to replace a visionary founder.

The remaining watch item is the board's independent investigation, which will proceed to its conclusion. The board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee to oversee trade compliance. If the review turns up new problems, the stock could swing sharply again. Still, the board said it is confident, based on input from senior U.S. government officials, that Huang's return poses no national security risk.

I believe Nvidia stock is worth buying at this price, given its growth and low valuation. What Huang built over the last 30-plus years won't fade away anytime soon, and he's back to keep building it. Nvidia's momentum is strong, which should benefit the stock in 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: Michael Burry’s Latest Top 10 Stock Picks Amid AI Crash
news.Content:
Michael Burry, the investor who famously predicted the 2008 housing market crash, is back in the spotlight as a sharp selloff in artificial intelligence stocks draws renewed attention to his warnings about a potential AI bubble.

The investor has become increasingly vocal on X as major AI names, including Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius, have suffered steep declines. On November 19, Burry declared, "Coreweave, Nebius, NVIDIA, semis, I tried to warn you all." He said he had not necessarily recommended shorting those stocks but had provided investors with information that could justify selling them.

His warnings were not entirely new. In September, Burry raised concerns that expensive AI chips could lose economic value faster than companies recognize through depreciation. In October, he highlighted the financial pressure facing CoreWeave as borrowing costs increased. According to Business Insider, he also urged Nvidia shareholders to get out of the stock in a November 11 Substack post and warned about risks facing AI infrastructure providers the following day.

The selloff has been dramatic. As of November 19, CoreWeave and Nebius had fallen approximately 76% and 66%, respectively, from their earlier highs, while Nvidia was down about 39% from its October peak. Those declines have added credibility to Burry's concerns, although they do not establish that the broader AI bubble has burst. ChatGPT holds Nebius in a live trading experiment and disagreed with Burry on the stock in August. Read the argument .

But while Burry has been bearish on some of the biggest names in artificial intelligence, he has not abandoned the stock market. His latest reported trades reveal that he has been buying shares of companies across technology, e-commerce, healthcare, and other industries, even as markets struggle. In August, he was long a beaten-down healthcare stock , an animal health company that had dropped more than 70% from its 2021 peak.

So, if Michael Burry is betting against parts of the AI boom, what stocks is he buying instead?

Methodology

For this article, we reviewed Michael Burry's publicly accessible commentary on his Cassandra Unchained Substack, financial news reports covering his November 2026 trading disclosures, and portfolio information published by third-party tracking accounts.

Burry's former investment firm, Scion Asset Management, deregistered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in November 2025, as Reuters reported. Consequently, a current comprehensive 13F filing is not available to establish his exact portfolio composition, position sizes, or holdings rankings.

Story Continues

We selected ten companies for which Burry has expressed a bullish investment view or reportedly maintained or increased bullish exposure. Our Michael Burry portfolio list from last month covered his picks at that time, and he has made new trades since.

#10 Ero Copper Corp. (NYSE: ERO)

Ero Copper Corp. is a Canadian mining company operating copper and gold projects in Brazil.

Copper is essential for electrical infrastructure, industrial equipment, construction, and power transmission. Demand could benefit from investments in electricity grids, electrification, and data centers, although commodity prices remain sensitive to broader economic conditions.

Burry has reportedly been increasing his investment in Ero Copper as its share price has declined.

Burry disclosed buying additional shares on November 19 when Ero Copper was trading slightly above $20.

According to several media reports, Burry considered the company attractive based on the underlying value of its mining projects. His investment case was not limited to copper demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure, with broader demand and the economics of individual mining assets also playing a role.

Ero Copper ranks tenth in our list of the best copper stocks to buy for the AI and electrification boom. See the list for the nine stocks ahead of it.

#9 Adobe Inc. (NASDAQ: ADBE)

Adobe is an unusual stock pick of Burry that has surprised many investors.

The company has faced investor concerns that artificial intelligence could weaken demand for traditional creative software by making image editing, design, and content generation cheaper and more accessible.

Burry, however, has expressed confidence in Adobe's ability to adapt.

In his Substack post earlier this month, Burry reportedly disclosed purchasing additional Adobe shares at approximately $246, describing the investment as a full position.

He also stated that he continued to believe Adobe would successfully adapt to the changing artificial intelligence environment.

Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) is another one of Burry's investments that is losing money this year. The stock is down about 34% this year as investors fear AI design tools will slow its growth. Citi recently cut the stock to Sell, citing slower recurring revenue growth, AI competition, and the rising cost of running AI features. Bulls say the business is still growing. Subscriptions make up 97% of Adobe's revenue, and in its latest quarter revenue grew 13% from a year ago. Annualized recurring revenue from Adobe's AI-first products grew more than 150% year over year. Disney signed a multi-year deal with Adobe in November. The stock trades at 8.9 times forward earnings, compared with about 14.7 for Salesforce and 14.2 for Intuit.

Bears say AI turns design software into a cheap commodity. Image and video tools can now produce usable work from a single sentence, so companies may need fewer Creative Cloud seats, and Adobe may have to cut prices to keep customers. Canva already took much of the market below the professional level. Running AI features also costs real money, and Adobe lets millions of free users try them before they pay, so its gross margin has started to slip. Adobe's growth rate is already lower than it was a few years ago, and Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) has not yet shown that free AI users will become paying customers.

Some bulls say Adobe's own AI could strengthen its position because its Firefly model is trained on licensed content, and companies pay Adobe to avoid legal trouble. Click to read the full argument.

#8 PayPal Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: PYPL)

On November 11, some media reports said that Burry disclosed buying additional PayPal shares alongside purchases of Adobe, JD.com, MercadoLibre, and other stocks.

The investment reflects Burry's reported interest in established payment businesses whose valuations have declined substantially from previous levels.

PayPal continues to operate a large payments network with relationships across consumers, merchants, and financial institutions. However, the company must compete with digital wallets, card networks, and newer payment-processing platforms.

A central question for investors is whether PayPal can stabilize its branded checkout business while translating cost reductions, product improvements, and share repurchases into sustainable earnings growth.

The company's relatively depressed valuation could provide an opportunity if its competitive position stabilizes, but continued market-share pressure would complicate a recovery.

A private equity firm and Stripe ended their pursuit of PayPal in August after they could not agree on a price. Read what happened .

#7 BYD Company Limited (BYDDF)

On November 2, Benzinga reported that Burry had purchased additional BYD shares while increasing his bullish exposure to Chinese stocks.

He reportedly bought more shares on November 19.

Burry acknowledged that BYD's shares could decline further but maintained confidence in the company's long-term competitive advantages.

Burry reportedly considers BYD's manufacturing and competitive position attractive relative to other automobile companies, even as its share price approached multi-year lows.

The investment comes amid intense competition in China's automotive market, where price reductions and competition among domestic manufacturers have placed pressure on profitability.

BYD also faces international trade restrictions, changing government policies, and uncertainty surrounding global electric-vehicle adoption.

For the bullish investment case to succeed, the company must preserve its competitive strengths while managing pricing pressure and sustaining profitability.

Burry has also traded other Chinese stocks this year. In August, he sold his Alibaba stake and called the shares overvalued. Read why .

#6 Lululemon Athletica Inc. (NASDAQ: LULU)

Burry has been particularly interested in LULU's long-term potential despite the headwinds the company is facing. Burry has reportedly described Lululemon as one of his favorite investments before selling his shares in early October for tax-related reasons.

He reportedly purchased shares of Deckers Outdoor as a temporary substitute while planning to re-enter Lululemon.

That opportunity came on November 11, when Burry reportedly disclosed buying back Lululemon shares as the stock fell into the $106 range.

Lululemon (NASDAQ:LULU) shares are down about 50% so far this year, and the bear case centers on rising competition. Private brands like Alo, Vuori, and SKIMS are likely to keep Lululemon's comparable sales below analyst estimates into fiscal 2027, Cantor Fitzgerald analyst John Kernan said in a recent note. Kernan rates the stock neutral because he lacks confidence that margins will recover and expects private rivals to keep disrupting the company. He also said these rivals use AI-driven marketing to win customers quickly without copying Lululemon's whole business model.

Burry reportedly sees Lululemon as a value opportunity, and the company carries no debt. See why he is buying.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LULU as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. news.Title: Jensen Huang May Be Back as Nvidia's CEO, but the Stock Is Likely to Remain Volatile
news.Content:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO earlier this month as multiple extramarital affairs came to light. But seemingly almost right after it happened, there were calls for him to come back to lead the company again.

It's been reminiscent of when Sam Altman was ousted as CEO of OpenAI a few years ago, only to end up coming back shortly afterward. Coincidentally, that also took place in November. And just like with that situation, Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, with the company announcing the reinstatement in a press release on Monday.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The stock has been soaring in early trading since the news came out, and here's why the volatility is likely to continue.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

Political uncertainty may still weigh on the stock

Huang's extramarital affairs have weighed significantly on Nvidia's stock, which entered Monday at a valuation of around $3 trillion. That's still high, but prior to the scandal, the stock was comfortably above the $5 trillion mark. News of the reinstatement could, however, get it back to around those levels again.

The volatility , however, is likely to continue because while Huang is back, that doesn't mean the controversy is over. Investors shouldn't forget that Huang was reportedly involved with a potential Chinese spy, and there are national security issues to consider. Huang is going to appear in front of Congress next month, and there may be issues that arise from that which may weigh on the stock once more. And that's why there could still be uncertainty around the company's leadership moving forward. If, however, Huang is cleared of any wrongdoing, then the path may be clear for the stock to get back to its previous levels.

Nvidia's stock is roaring again, but investors should consider the risk

The market has a way of overreacting to news, and this volatility involving Nvidia is an excellent example. It overreacted to Huang's resignation, and it's overreacting once again to his reinstatement.

The company wasn't necessarily doomed without Huang, and it's certainly not smooth sailing now that he's back. There are still valid concerns around what happens with the business moving forward. While U.S. President Donald Trump has advocated for Huang's return, saying it would be in the best interests of the company, there may be more political pressure facing the business next year, especially with the Democrats controlling Congress and potentially taking a tougher stance on these issues.

Story Continues

Nvidia is still a top growth stock and can be an excellent long-term investment, but investors shouldn't be surprised to see more volatility ahead, and for those who aren't willing to take on the risk, a wait-and-see approach might be more appropriate.

news.Title: 5 things to consider as Nvidia restores Jensen Huang as the company's leader
news.Content:
Talk about another wow moment in the markets. Stunning news just hit: Nvidia ( NVDA ) founder Jensen Huang is being reinstated as CEO and as a board member. He was ousted after a series of affairs became public less than two weeks ago.

I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work."

Nvidia stock exploded 30%.

"Jensen will be on a mission," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Sozzi Unleashed .

Here are five thoughts on this now-developing news:

The Nvidia board could now be seen as a puppet to its founder. Basic corporate governance standards have been totally tossed in the trash.

This will not be the same Jensen Huang returning as CEO, and it can't be.

Ultimately, this puts the AI trade back on the map into year-end.

Now former interim CFO Colette Kress should resign as CFO. This is embarrassing to be a part of for such an accomplished leader.

Never underestimate the power of Washington in C-suites and boardrooms. President Trump demanded the reinstatement of Huang over the weekend.

news.Title: Why stocks are having their wildest Monday morning since 2008
news.Content:
Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It's spending Monday buying it back.

The Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), the fund that tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ), opened almost 8% higher, its biggest jump at the open since it launched in 1999. Its closest rivals for largest jumps came in 2000 and 2001 as the dot-com bubble was bursting and big rallies had a habit of fizzling.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF ( SPY ) opened 5% higher. Among Mondays since 1993, only Oct. 13, 2008, in the depths of the financial crisis, started with a bigger jump.

The surge comes as Nvidia ( NVDA ) brought back Jensen Huang as CEO , and after the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) slid into a correction last week.

Chip stocks are leading the charge

The iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) opened 15% higher, its biggest jump at the open since it launched in 2001 and well past its previous record of about 9% in October 2002.

Nvidia opened up 33% on Huang's return and is on track for one of the best days in its history, which tops out at a 42% gain in March 2000. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Micron ( MU ) and AMD ( AMD ) opened roughly 12% to 21% higher.

Not everyone thinks the panic has run its course. Options sentiment "screams" the worst levels since the pandemic and Liberation Day, Roundhill Investments chief investment strategist Drew Pettit told Yahoo Finance, "but it's not a washout."

History sides with the bulls, eventually. In the 20 times since 1993 that SPY opened Monday 2% or more higher, it was higher a year later in 17 of those, with a median gain of about 25%, roughly double that of a typical year, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

Creative Planning's Charlie Bilello found a similar pattern . Last week's nearly 9% drop was the S&P 500's 12th-worst week since 1950, he noted, and after the worst weeks, stocks averaged a 26% gain over the next year, compared with 11% otherwise.

Evercore ISI's Julian Emanuel is in that camp too, writing over the weekend, "Bull Market intact as double-digit EPS gains likely ahead."

The road higher is rarely smooth

In half of those 20 cases, SPY slipped back below the prior Friday's low within three months, most often within two weeks. Think of it as the morning after a big night out. The headache usually comes back before it goes away.

Even so, eight of those 10 were higher a year later. The two closest matches to this setup, October 2008 and May 2010, each paired a brutal week with a big Monday open, sank further over the next three months and were about 15% higher a year later.

Story Continues

That puts Friday's low, about 6,883 on the S&P 500, in focus. And the Fed isn't riding to the rescue , with Wall Street still pricing a December rate hike and every correction that hits with inflation speeding up this fast turning into a bear market .

BTIG's strategists aren't calling a bottom yet. "We don't think this is the final low, but we are looking for a short-term rally back towards 7250-7350 before likely turning lower again," they wrote over the weekend.

news.Title: Stock market today: Nvidia stock soars after company reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq surge
news.Content:
Stocks soared on Monday as investors cheered Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. It marked a major rebound on Monday as buyers stepped back in for the holiday-shortened week after a bruising sell-off.

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 5.3% following seven straight days of declines. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) jumped more than 1,500 points to recover by 3.1% following its worst week since the COVID-related sell-off in 2020. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) rallied 7.3%.

Nvidia stock soared more than 30% Monday morning after Nvidia announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said.

The move came after President Trump renewed his call to reinstate the chipmaker's founder, Jensen Huang, as CEO amid a series of controversies.

Sentiment was exuberant after a volatile week last week that saw the AI trade unravel and the S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory. Anthropic ( ANT ) shares slipped Monday after whipsawing earlier in the morning.

On the calendar for Monday: Investors will receive wholesale inflation data. Hewlett Packard Enterprise ( HPE ) and Zoom Communications ( ZM ) report results as the Q3 earnings season wraps up.

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said. "I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. … I can't wait to get back to work."

The board's independent investigation into Huang's ties to the Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, "will proceed to conclusion." The company said it also has assembled a National Security and Export Control Committee.

news.Title: Meta AI Chief Issues Stark Warning About Humanity's Future
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) chief AI officer Alexandr Wang warned Sunday that artificial intelligence could soon surpass human intelligence, raising concerns about whether people can maintain control over increasingly powerful systems. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META. Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. "Superintelligence is arriving," Wang wrote on X on November 22, arguing that decisions made over the next year could fundamentally shape humanity's future. His warning followed reports that an Anthropic researcher used Claude to solve the Riemann Hypothesis, a mathematical problem that has challenged researchers since 1859. Wang cited the reported breakthrough as evidence that AI capabilities are advancing beyond traditional human expertise. He argued that future systems could automate AI research, improve their own capabilities and accelerate discoveries in biology, economics and weapons development. The concern is recursive self-improvement , where AI systems become capable of developing increasingly powerful successors without requiring comparable human intervention. Wang questioned whether humanity could realistically control systems thousands of times more capable than people. However, he rejected the idea that society should automatically surrender decision-making to AI, urging developers to prioritize safety, security and human oversight. Investors Takeaway The warning highlights growing differences among technology leaders. While OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have supported slowing frontier-model development to improve safeguards, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has generally opposed coordinated restrictions. For investors in Meta, Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) and Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), the debate could influence future AI investment and regulation. The central question is whether companies can maintain rapid innovation while demonstrating that increasingly autonomous systems remain controllable. news.Title: Political and corporate leaders react to Huang's return as Nvidia CEO
news.Content:
Nov 23 (Reuters) - Nvidia on Monday said it is reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO after determining that he does ‌not pose a national security risk, sending the chipmaker's shares ‌surging, reviving the global AI trade, which has faltered this month.

Below are notable ​reactions on the announcement:

US PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP:

Trump on social media platform Truth Social said that Nvidia's board "made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO."

"The United States Government ‌has no reason to ⁠believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security."

"The Attorney General of the United States ⁠has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, ​I have ​gotten to know Jensen, and he ​is a Great Patriot ‌and National Treasure."

ELON MUSK, BILLIONAIRE CEO OF TESLA AND SPACEX:

Musk responded to the announcement with a post on X, saying: "the mistake has been corrected".

US DEMOCRATIC SENATOR ELIZABETH WARREN

Warren said the "reckless decision" to bring Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that he, ‌Nvidia's executives and its board still owe ​Congress answers about the company's compliance ​with US export controls.

"The Trump ​Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' ‌was given and by which senior ​officials in the ​United States government to support his reinstatement."

"Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into ​law and making ‌sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and ​put our national security at risk."

(Compiled by Manya Saini ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Diti Pujara)

news.Title: What Oppenheimer and William Blair See in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
news.Content:
We just published a list of the 10 Stocks Stanley Druckenmiller Just Dumped—and What His Big Exit Signals Next and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD ) ranked 7th on this list.

On November 16, 2026, Stanley Druckenmiller's family office filed its third-quarter 13F, and the numbers show a portfolio that shrank fast: 65 positions worth $4.47 billion at September 30, down from 95 at June 30. He explained his caution in an interview with Morgan Stanley's Iliana Bouzali, which we covered in our video on his new AI warning and top 5 stock picks and in our written recap of the interview .

Druckenmiller Plays Defense

Druckenmiller ran his hedge fund for 30 years without a single losing calendar year, as our video notes. He said he could barely recall a time when he had so little clarity about where markets would head over the next 12 months. His firm has largely stepped back from major directional bets, and its net equity exposure is roughly flat. "We're trying to not lose money as opposed to make money," he said.

His bigger prediction is about the AI labs themselves, which he thinks could stop selling access to their models and start selling finished work, such as software development and cybersecurity investigations. He thinks the next major AI opportunity may shift from companies building data centers and selling chips to companies that use AI to do real work for businesses. He singled out cybersecurity as the clearest example, asking, "Who's going to compete with these guys in cybersecurity?" The labs, he added, could field swarms of AI agents to defend businesses against attacks, which could threaten established security companies.

The filing shows where he still has money. He raised his stake in the online retail and cloud giant by about 43% and nearly tripled his position in a hard disk drive maker, even as he questioned the infrastructure trade. His largest holding is a maker of cancer-recurrence blood tests, worth $1.31 billion at September 30 and more than four times the next-largest position.

A Brutal Week for the AI Trade

In the week to November 20, the Dow fell 8%, the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq fell 10%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. The S&P 500's drop was its worst week since the April 2025 tariff sell-off, and the Nasdaq's was its worst since March 2020. The slide began earlier in the month: on November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell into a correction, and Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte attributed that selloff to a forced positioning unwind. For what he owned before the exits, see our list of the best AI stocks to buy according to Druckenmiller .

Story Continues

Watch the video below to see his new AI warning and his five biggest stock holdings, including the one that makes up close to 30% of his reported portfolio.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t4riDasPHkc

AMD made it to our list because Stanley Druckenmiller's family office fully exited a stake worth $42.35 million at June 30. Oppenheimer upgraded Advanced Micro Devices to Outperform from Perform on November 9 and set a $600 price target, and William Blair followed on November 12 with an upgrade to Outperform from Market Perform. William Blair said it expects data center AI revenue to pass server processor revenue in the fourth quarter. Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer pointed to strong server and data center demand. AMD is a semiconductor company whose products include processors, accelerators and graphics chips, and it also offers artificial intelligence and gaming solutions.

The case builds on the third quarter of 2026, released November 3. Revenue rose 45% to $13.4 billion, Data Center revenue rose 97%. The stock is not cheap, though, at 23.77 times forward earnings, and how much execution risk that premium valuation carries is the open question for skeptics weighing that premium.

Stanley Druckenmiller's family office reported 72,900 shares worth $42.35 million at June 30, and its September 30 filing listed none. Oppenheimer and William Blair both moved after the fund had already left the position, and the filing does not show when it sold or at what price.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of AMD as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Dollar jumps on hawkish Fed bets, AI rally
news.Content:
By Karen Brettell

NEW YORK, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The dollar hit a more than 19-month high against the euro on Monday as traders bet on a more hawkish Federal Reserve, ‌while Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO lifted optimism in the AI trade.

Strong US economic ‌data, stubbornly high inflation and hawkish Fed commentary have led traders to raise their bets on faster rate hikes, which has ​supported the greenback against peers.

Recent volatility in US stocks, however, has clouded the picture on how much more tightening the economy can withstand.

"We've had a pretty material moderation in expectations for Fed tightening and given that this happened at the same time as the deterioration in the market mood it's muddled things a ‌bit in terms of having the ⁠US dollar trading well above levels that we'd expect just given fundamentals," said Eric Theoret, currency strategist at Scotiabank.

Fed funds futures traders now fully price in a ⁠25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting, up from 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled. They have, however, priced out any chance of a larger 50-basis-point increase. They also see a 67% chance of another ​hike in ​January, up from 51% on Friday but down from ​71% a week ago, according to CME ‌Group's FedWatch Tool.

Huang's return was an extraordinary reversal that followed calls from US President Donald Trump for his return after he resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The news sent Nvidia's shares up 33% and helped to boost the dollar, which has been supported by capital inflows into the tech sector.

Meanwhile, US business activity growth slowed further in November as high prices ‌held back new orders and capacity constraints restrained output, but ​overall activity remains resilient, suggesting economic growth is continuing at ​an above-trend rate, a survey showed on ​Monday.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the ‌yen and the euro, rose 0.41% to ​104.27, with the euro down ​0.45% at $1.0918.

Data on Monday showed that euro zone growth momentum held up in November but was increasingly reliant on a surging Germany to make up for a weakening France, while fading ​business confidence cast a shadow ‌over the bloc's outlook.

Against the Japanese yen, the dollar strengthened 0.51% to 159.34. Sterling weakened ​0.34% to $1.3036.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin gained 3.57% to $63,041.66.

(Reporting by Karen Brettell; Additional reporting by Gregor ​Stuart Hunter and Sophie Kiderlin; Editing by Susan Fenton)

Our Methodology

5 Stocks Stanley Druckenmiller Just Dumped—and What His Big Exit Signals Next

5. Delta Air Lines (NYSE: DAL )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 78

Forward EV/Revenue: 0.91

Revenue Growth (Last 12 Months): 14.11%

Chief Executive Officer Ed Bastian said in Delta's October 9 results that "Demand remains strong, supported by consumers' growing preference for experiences and travel." Delta Air Lines provides scheduled air transportation for passengers and cargo, and it also runs a refinery that supplies jet fuel to its own airline.

The September quarter of 2026 brought record adjusted revenue of $17.6 billion, a rise of 16%, but adjusted fuel expense rose 62%, and earnings under generally accepted accounting principles fell sharply to $1.15 per diluted share from a year earlier. Delta guided to higher December-quarter revenue and gave a full-year 2026 earnings range. Bulls argue that falling oil prices could ease costs, which would help profits recover after record revenue , and that Delta's profitability, lower debt and loyalty business give it a stronger base than United's.

The shares trade at 10.70 times forward earnings. Stanley Druckenmiller's family office held 603,000 shares worth $56.48 million at June 30, and the September 30 filing listed none, so the fund was out before the airline reported these results in October, which means the filing says nothing about how it viewed them.

4. Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK )

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 122

Forward EV/Revenue: 1.67

Revenue Growth (Last 12 Months): 272.38%

Fox Advisors downgraded Sandisk to Equal-Weight from Overweight on November 2, days after the company reported its fiscal first quarter of 2027. Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani took the other side on November 11, keeping an Outperform rating and a $2,500 price target that predates the 8-for-1 stock split effective after the close on November 19. Evercore argued that investors focus too much on how long NAND pricing can stay elevated and not enough on structural changes to Sandisk's model, including multi-year supply contracts.

Sandisk develops, manufactures and sells data storage products built on NAND flash, including solid state drives for PCs and gaming consoles. In the fiscal first quarter of 2027, released October 29, revenue rose 378% to $11.03 billion and gross margin reached 85.0%. Bears warn that new factory capacity could eventually push memory supply past demand, creating a glut that would hit the profits behind those results.

The shares trade at 2.21 times forward earnings, which raises the question of whether a memory-cycle peak is already priced in . Stanley Druckenmiller's family office held 34,900 shares worth $79.35 million at June 30, and the September 30 filing listed none.

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 70

Forward EV/Revenue: 0.76

Revenue Growth (Last 12 Months): 12.31%

United Airlines reported record revenue for the third quarter of 2026 on October 20, and it still had to explain a fuel bill that grew faster than sales. Revenue rose 17% to $17.9 billion, fuel expense climbed 62%. United is a holding company that flies passengers on domestic, Atlantic, Pacific and Latin American routes and reports results across those four segments.

Bulls say falling oil prices could set up an airline comeback, and they note that United's recent revenue growth has been stronger than Delta's. news.Title: 3 Unstoppable AI Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist Before the End of 2026
news.Content:
Consistently investing in businesses that provide an essential service to the economy is a simple way to select winning investments that can power your retirement. This is what makes a stock truly unstoppable for a patient investor.

Big tech's artificial intelligence (AI) build-out depends on three components: software to design chips, machines to make them, and cloud platforms to put them to work. Here's why ASML Holding (NASDAQ:ASML), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Cadence Design Systems (NASDAQ:CDNS) are unstoppable stocks that can help you profit from this opportunity.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. ASML

ASML makes the machines that chipmakers use to print circuits onto silicon, and it's the only company that builds the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) systems needed for the most advanced chips. Without these tools, chipmakers couldn't expand production of the chips AI runs on.

Demand for the company's machines continues to exceed supply, but ASML also benefits from servicing these machines over their life. Revenue from servicing and upgrading them jumped 68% year over year in the third quarter. The current high demand for new machines could extend ASML's revenue opportunity for years to come.

The next generation, High-NA EUV, is catching on: Intel has run more than 1 million wafers on it, and Samsung and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing plan to use it in volume production in 2028 and 2030, respectively.

Down payments for future orders have grown this year. This is reflected in the growth of contract liabilities, which jumped from about 3.4 billion euros to about 9.3 billion euros since the end of 2025.

The biggest risk for ASML is customer concentration. ASML's largest customer accounted for about 24% of 2025 sales, and China accounted for about 29%. If a big customer paused orders or export rules tightened, sales could come under pressure. But this would be a temporary hurdle, as ASML remains the only provider of the machines required to make chips that power the global economy.

The stock trades at about 22 times 2027 earnings estimates, with earnings expected to grow about 33% next year. That's reasonable for an essential equipment supplier to the semiconductor industry.

2. Microsoft

Microsoft is the cloud provider behind Azure, where much of the world's AI is rented and run. Azure revenue grew 48% year over year in the September quarter, and management expects 49%-50% year-over-year growth in the December quarter.

Story Continues

While Wall Street is being more critical of companies spending aggressively on AI, Microsoft is squeezing more money out of every chip. Management credits efficiency gains across its GPU fleet for "higher revenue per token," and it found ways to rent out underused processor capacity.

Moreover, customer demand is there: Commercial remaining performance obligations hit $677 billion, up 73%.

The stock has pulled back over spending. Microsoft expects roughly $170 billion of capital spending in calendar 2026, according to The Motley Fool's research, while trailing free cash flow has fallen to about $60 billion. Most of that spending goes to short-lived chips, so if AI demand slows, they could lose value and squeeze margins.

Still, Microsoft is a highly profitable software giant. Enterprises and consumers rely on its services every day to get real work done, which makes it unstoppable for patient investors. At about 25 times this year's earnings estimates, Microsoft trades at a modest premium to the S&P 500 average multiple of about 19x -- a reasonable premium for a company expected to grow earnings about 16% a year.

3. Cadence Design Systems

Cadence sells the software that engineers use to design and verify chips, plus hardware that tests designs before they're manufactured. All the top AI companies are working with Cadence, and without them, chip designers couldn't catch costly flaws before production.

Recurring revenue accounted for 79% of third-quarter sales, and the backlog reached $8.2 billion. It expects more than half of that backlog to be converted to revenue in the next 12 months. Its emulation hardware posted another record quarter, and its AI design agents have more than 100 active customer engagements.

Revenue rose 22% year over year to about $1.6 billion in the third quarter, but that includes the Hexagon design and engineering business it acquired. Excluding it, management says growth was still in the mid-teens.

Integrating its acquisition is one headwind. GAAP operating margin fell to 26% from the low 30s over the last year. If integration costs linger, earnings growth could trail revenue growth, potentially weighing on the stock price.

Cadence is the priciest of the three stocks at about 36 times this year's earnings estimates, with expected earnings growth of about 17% a year. But it's worth paying up for the recurring revenue stream, which makes revenue more predictable and typically earns a higher premium from investors.

I believe all three are worth buying now and worth adding to on dips into 2027.

news.Title: Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang as CEO While Its Probe Goes On
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. Shares were up about 27% in early trading Monday. The board has settled who leads the company. It has not finished its probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and it is adding national security checks in the meantime.

Key Details

Board vote: Unanimous, to reinstate Huang as president, CEO, and director.

Board chair: Harvey C. Jones stays in the role.

Colette Kress: Steps back from interim CEO and stays on as CFO.

Independent investigation: Will proceed to its conclusion, with Huang's support.

What It Means

The board based its decision on its talks with Huang and on input from senior U.S. government officials. That input is why it says his return poses no national security risk. For a chipmaker whose top products fall under U.S. export rules, Washington's view carries more weight than any internal review could.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The weak spot is timing. Huang is back before the independent investigation ends, so the board is betting its findings won't change the picture. The release also says Nvidia is still cooperating with government investigations and inquiries, but it doesn't say what they cover.

The lasting change is oversight. A new committee of independent directors will watch trade compliance and national security risk. Nvidia is also searching for a chief compliance officer, a new role that will report to a board committee. That gives directors a direct line into compliance.

What to Watch Next

Watch whether Nvidia shares the investigation's findings when it ends. Then watch who fills the compliance job and what national security experience they bring.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »
