投資一定有風險，基金投資有賺有賠，申購前應詳閱公開說明書。

news.Title: ACMR Rides on Strong Operating Margin Growth: Will it Sustain?
news.Content:
ACM Research, Inc. ACMR is witnessing strong improvement in operating profitability, driven by robust revenue growth and better operating expense leverage. Non-GAAP operating income rose to $66.2 million from $36.5 million, with the corresponding operating margin expanding to 18% from 13.6%. The company reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with revenue growth outpacing expense increases. On a non-GAAP basis, operating expenses increased 12.7% to $86.7 million. Operating expenses as a percentage of revenues declined to 23.6% from 28.6% in the prior-year quarter.

Strong revenue growth is one of the driving factors. In the third quarter, revenues reached $367.7 million, up 36.6% year over year. Growth was primarily driven by higher sales of ECP, furnace and other technologies, alongside increased contributions from single-wafer cleaning, Tahoe and advanced packaging equipment. ACMR's expanding product portfolio and differentiated technologies could provide further support to profitability. The company's enhanced single-wafer hot SPM system, featuring a 70% sulfuric acid recycling rate, is another positive development. Its proprietary and patent-protected technologies could support strong margin growth in the long run.

Looking ahead, management expects continued growth momentum, supported by strong customer demand. ACM Research raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $1.24-$1.28 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 38-42% compared with its earlier forecast of $1.125-$1.175 billion. The company also expects fourth-quarter shipments to increase from third-quarter levels. However, despite strong top-line growth, forex volatility and product mix may lead uneven margin expansion across quarters.

How Are Competitors Faring?

Lam Research LRCX is a major supplier of wafer fabrication equipment and services to the semiconductor industry. Lam Research benefits from AI-driven investment in memory, advanced foundry processes and packaging. During the first quarter, the company's non-GAAP operating margin reached 40.2%, rising 520 basis points year over year and 180 basis points sequentially. Non-GAAP operating expenses increased to $1 billion from $916 million in the previous quarter, primarily on higher incentive compensation tied to profitability. Lam Research had also stepped up investment in product programs, with research and development comprising roughly two-thirds of total operating expenses.

Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT is a leading supplier of equipment used to manufacture semiconductor devices, flat panel displays and solar photovoltaic products. During the fourth quarter, AMAT's operating expenses rose 20% to $1.59 billion, but declined as a share of revenues by 430 basis points to 15.2%. Non-GAAP operating income reached $3.68 billion compared with $1.95 billion in the prior-year quarter. Differentiated equipment and value-based pricing are translating into wider margins and operating leverage for AMAT.

news.Title: What's Wrong With Alphabet Stock?
news.Content:
Shares of Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG)(NASDAQ:GOOGL) have been nosediving in recent months. The sell-off has gotten so extreme in recent months that the tech stock hit a new 52-week low last week. In just the past six months, it has declined by more than 30%.

Given the company's persistently strong results and dominance in Google Search and its solid ad business, it could make for a compelling long-term buy at this point. But before investors consider buying the stock, it's important to understand what's behind the recent free fall, and whether this is just due to the recent pullback in the tech sector as a whole, or if there are significant problems with Alphabet's business that could weigh on the stock's future performance.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's take a closer look at its performance and valuation to determine whether the tech stock is a good buy right now.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The stock nosedived after earnings

Although there's been weakness in tech of late, there was a big sell-off of Alphabet stock that took place after it reported its latest earnings numbers in late October. In fact, the decline of around 12% the day after earnings came out was its worst ever single-day performance.

While the company reported 25% growth on the top line during the September quarter, its results fell short of expectations on its search advertising revenue, which rose at a slower pace of 12%. While the company has leaned heavily into artificial intelligence (AI) and its Gemini chatbot, it's unclear how that strategy will play out as AI competition from other chatbots appears to be impacting its overall search business.

Perhaps more concerning, however, was the negative $9.1 billion free cash flow it reported during the period, a result of its high capital spend on AI. That's a significant change from the three quarters earlier when its free cash flow was a positive $24.6 billion.

Alphabet's stock looks cheap right now

Due to the sizable decline in its value, Alphabet is looking like an enticing AI stock to buy today. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple , which is based on analyst expectations, is just under 18. That's right in line with the S&P 500 average.

That's an attractive multiple to be paying for the stock, as in the past the forward P/E has easily been over 20. While there are question marks about Alphabet's business, at a reduced valuation, investors are getting some decent margin of safety here. For long-term investors, now may be an opportune time to load up on Alphabet's stock.

news.Title: Billionaire Investor Stanley Druckenmiller Just Issued a Sobering Warning to Wall Street
news.Content: Stanley Druckenmiller is truly one of the best investors of all time, and he's got the track record to back it up. Druckenmiller launched his own hedge fund, Duquesne Capital, around 1981, with just $900,000. By 2010, Druckenmiller and his team had turned that start-up capital into $12 billion, generating mouth-watering average annual returns over 30% and never experiencing a full down year (although it was down about 5% in 2010, the partial year it shut down), which very few investors can say. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Today, Druckenmiller still invests his personal wealth through the Duquesne Family Office. While Druckenmiller doesn't speak all that often, he appears on television or at conferences a few times a year. The legendary investor just issued a sobering warning to Wall Street. Stanley Druckenmiller. Image source: Getty Images. 'Taking a break' At the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, Druckenmiller answered questions about his current views on the economy and stock market, and I'm sure it had investors on Wall Street perking up. While Druckenmiller may not be outright bearish on stocks or the market, he told the audience that he is "taking a break," which could last anywhere from two days to six months. "So, we are not long equities. We're not short equities . I like to go short. I admit it," he said. "But for all the reasons I think most people came to this conference, I wouldn't dare go short the innovation and everything going on here. Also, a lot of that stuff is oversold and washed out. And I think positions are down tactically." Overall, Druckenmiller is simply unsure right now. In fact, the George Soros protégé said that in the five decades he's been doing this, he can't recall a time when he's had less clarity on what will happen in the economy and stock market over the next year. This should serve as a sobering warning for Wall Street, as Druckenmiller is arguably best known as a macro-driven investor focused on central bank policy, market liquidity, interest rates, and other economic trends. What's arguably even more fascinating about this statement is that Druckenmiller knows Kevin Warsh, the chair of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, as well as anyone. Warsh worked as a partner at his family office. "We've had regime change at the Fed. A gentleman I know ... sat next to me for 15 years. Um, he is not happy that we had free money for 15 years while the deficit and everything else went through the roof," Druckenmiller said. "He's even less happy that inflation's been above target for five years. So, we have monetary tightening going on." Story Continues As mentioned earlier, Druckenmiller is not short equities because he still believes in much of the innovation happening in artificial intelligence. Druckenmiller has been a board member of the Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and he thinks they will solve cancer, potentially as soon as 10 years from now. Furthermore, he thinks there will eventually be data centers in space, a hotly debated topic, particularly regarding feasibility. The fact that Druckenmiller can't find clarity should be concerning Druckenmiller is not a traditional long-term buy-and-hold investor, so as he said, he may change his views next week. However, I think the big takeaway and warning here is that Druckenmiller is as uncertain as he's been in five decades of investing. If he doesn't know, then who possibly could? One reason I suspect Druckenmiller is so uncertain is that the AI trade could take so many unforeseen turns. Some people believe it will be a tremendous success, significantly increasing productivity and benefiting others. The bears think people may be overestimating its capabilities and that all the capital investment will yield mediocre returns. But what if it works so well that a tremendous amount of human labor is replaced and consumer spending, which accounts for the majority of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP), declines sharply? Or what if AI eliminates many of the inefficiencies in the world that enable many of today's jobs? These are all things investors need to be thinking about. Now, long-term investors can certainly stay invested in the market. But it's likely a good idea to make sure that the valuations on stocks you own are driven by reasonable assumptions, and that your portfolio has at least some exposure to sectors or stocks less impacted by AI. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook. Continue » The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy . news.Title: Ciena vs. Cisco: Which Optical Networking Stock is the Better Buy?
news.Content:
Ciena Corporation CIEN and Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO are benefiting from rising investments in AI, data center expansion and growing demand for high-speed networking solutions. Ciena is capitalizing on strong demand for optical networking and data center interconnect solutions, while Cisco is leveraging its broad networking, security and AI infrastructure portfolio to address evolving customer needs.

Both companies are witnessing strong momentum as hyperscalers and enterprises increase investments in next-generation networking infrastructure. Ciena's WaveLogic 6 and Hyper-Rail solutions, alongside Cisco's Silicon One platforms and Acacia optics, are strengthening their positions in the AI-driven networking market. With demand expected to remain robust, both companies are well-positioned to capitalize on multiyear growth opportunities.

Let's analyze their fundamentals, growth opportunities, market challenges and valuation to assess which one presents a stronger investment opportunity.

The Case for CIEN

Ciena is gaining from robust demand for high-speed optical connectivity, fueled by rising AI investments and expanding data center infrastructure. Increasing bandwidth requirements, network traffic and the adoption of AI-driven applications are creating significant growth opportunities across traditional wide area networks, AI networks and data centers. Management expects its total addressable market to double from approximately $25 billion to $50 billion by 2029. The company's strong technological capabilities and expanding optical networking portfolio position it well to capitalize on these opportunities and capture additional market share.

The company is benefiting from strong adoption of its advanced optical networking solutions, particularly WaveLogic 6 Extreme, RLS and Waveserver platforms. WaveLogic 6 Extreme continues to witness faster adoption than its predecessor, WaveLogic 5e, while RLS maintains a leading position with approximately 70% market share. Ciena is also making progress with its next-generation Hyper-Rail platform, which is expected to generate several hundred million dollars in revenues in fiscal 2027. Growing demand for WaveLogic 5 Nano pluggable optics and emerging interconnect solutions, including Nitro and Vesta, further strengthens its long-term growth prospects.

Ciena's impressive financial performance reflects strong customer demand and improving operational efficiency. In third-quarter fiscal 2026, revenues increased 37% year over year to a record $1.67 billion, supported by more than 80% growth in direct cloud provider revenues. Adjusted operating margin reached a record 22.5%, while adjusted earnings per share surged 215% to $2.11. The company's backlog increased $800 million sequentially to $8.5 billion, with management anticipating more than $10 billion by fiscal year-end, providing substantial revenue visibility.

Story Continues

The company's outlook remains encouraging, supported by sustained demand and expanding customer commitments. For fiscal 2027, management anticipates revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3-$8.4 billion, alongside adjusted operating margins of 25-27%. Long-term supply agreements extending through 2029 and ongoing capacity investments should help Ciena meet rising demand, strengthen customer relationships and improve profitability.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, Ciena is grappling with significant supply-chain constraints amid unprecedented demand for optical networking equipment. Limited availability of critical components continues to restrict production capacity, preventing the company from fully capitalizing on its substantial order backlog. Management expects the supply-demand imbalance to persist through fiscal 2027 and potentially into fiscal 2028. These constraints could delay product deliveries and revenue recognition, particularly for high-growth offerings such as Hyper-Rail.

Additionally, Ciena faces growing working-capital requirements and potential cash-flow pressure as it expands manufacturing capacity and secures critical components. Despite generating $116 million in free cash flow during the third quarter, cash conversion weakened sequentially due to higher inventory investments. Management expects operating cash flow to decline in the fourth quarter as payments related to long-term supply agreements increase. Moreover, potential Canadian tariff-related costs of approximately $10 million per quarter and continued investments in product development could add pressure to financial performance.

The Case for CSCO

Cisco is gaining from robust demand for its networking infrastructure as enterprises and cloud providers accelerate investments in AI. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, networking revenues surged 43% year over year, supported by triple-digit growth in AI infrastructure and double-digit growth in data center switching and campus networking. Networking product orders increased 28%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Cisco believes it is in the early stages of a multiyear networking upgrade cycle, positioning the company for sustained growth.

The company is benefiting from expanding AI infrastructure investments by hyperscale customers. Cisco raised its fiscal 2027 AI infrastructure revenue forecast to $9 billion from $7.5 billion, representing more than twice the fiscal 2026 level. It secured three new AI design wins during the first quarter, bringing the total to 18 over the past five quarters. Its Silicon One P200 systems and Acacia optical technologies are strengthening its position in AI networking. Moreover, orders for Nexus data center switches associated with AI deployments increased 47%, reflecting growing demand beyond hyperscalers.

Cisco is witnessing healthy demand across customer segments and geographies, supported by enterprise modernization and sovereign infrastructure investments. First-quarter product orders increased 21% year over year, including 15% growth in enterprise orders and 13% growth in public-sector orders. Service provider and cloud orders surged 47%, while orders from telecommunications customers rose approximately 20%. Campus networking orders increased 14%, and industrial IoT orders climbed approximately 50%. Management believes the campus refresh cycle remains in its early stages, providing additional growth opportunities.

The company is gaining traction in cybersecurity through its expanding security portfolio and AI-driven offerings. Security revenues increased 7% year over year in the first quarter, while core security orders, excluding Splunk, grew 15%. Firewall orders advanced more than 30% for the third consecutive quarter. Cisco's Zero Trust secure access platform has attracted 5,400 customers, including nearly 800 additions during the quarter. Its AI Defense solution now protects more than 2 trillion tokens monthly, highlighting increasing adoption of AI security capabilities.

Cisco's solid financial performance and disciplined cost management are strengthening its profitability and shareholder returns. First-quarter revenues increased 24% year over year to a record $18.5 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share surged 40% to $1.40. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 37.8%, reflecting operating leverage. Operating cash flow rose 36% to $4.4 billion, enabling shareholder returns of $3.7 billion. Encouraged by strong execution, Cisco raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8-$75.8 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share outlook to $5.47-$5.53.

However, Cisco is grappling with gross margin pressure stemming from an increasing hardware revenue mix and elevated component costs, particularly memory. First-quarter non-GAAP gross margin contracted 250 basis points (bps) year over year to 65.6%, while product gross margin declined 350 bps to 63.7%. Hardware revenues are growing substantially faster than software and services revenues, creating an unfavorable mix. With hyperscale AI revenue expected to account for 12% of total fiscal 2027 revenues compared with 6% in fiscal 2026, this shift could continue weighing on gross margins despite productivity improvements and pricing initiatives.

CIEN Shares vs. CSCO

Over the past six months, CIEN's shares have plunged 59.9%, and CSCO stock has lost 24.8%.

Valuation for CIEN & CSCO

In terms of Price/Book, CIEN shares are trading at 10.87X, higher than CSCO's 6.92X.

How the Zacks Consensus Estimate Compares for CIEN & CSCO

Analysts have not changed their earnings estimates for CIEN's bottom line for the current year.

For CSCO, there have been marginal upward revisions for the current year.

CIEN or CSCO: Which Stock to Bet on?

Cisco appears to be a better investment choice, supported by its diversified business portfolio, strong AI infrastructure momentum, expanding customer base and robust cash-flow generation. Its improving earnings outlook, attractive valuation relative to Ciena and favorable estimate revisions further strengthen its investment appeal.

CSCO has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present, while CIEN has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Consequently, in terms of Zacks Rank, CSCO seems to be a better pick at the moment.

news.Title: Tesla's autonomy ambitions just got a Wall Street vote of confidence
news.Content:
Wall Street is taking an early bullish stance on Tesla's ( TSLA ) new v15 software.

"With Rivian preparing to showcase its autonomy roadmap at its December 9 Autonomy & AI Day, Ford advancing toward the 2027 Fathom launch, and GM navigating CEO succession discussions ahead of its 2028 launch of 'eyes-off' highway on Cadillac Escalade IQ, we see the breadth of the v15 release as another illustration of TSLA's head start in consumer autonomy, raising the (already high) bar another notch," JPMorgan analyst Rajat Gupta wrote on Monday.

Tesla said this past weekend it has begun rolling out its highly anticipated Full Self-Driving (FSD) v15 software.

The centerpiece of the release is "Tesla Reality View." It's being described as an interactive, real-time AI visualization that re-renders the surrounding street like a video game while using less total compute.

Under the hood, a new vision encoder shared with Tesla's Robotaxi and Optimus programs is trained on millions of internet videos. It reportedly delivers a 25x improvement in handling safety-critical interventions.

The update also targets longtime driving weak spots with sharper detection of potholes, road signs, and standing water, as well as automatic slowdowns at speed cameras and a dedicated Bike Rack Mode.

Tesla stock rose 4% in premarket trading today on the news.

"Moreover, TSLA indicated that compute efficiency improvements need not mandate a near-term upgrade to AI5 hardware (~10-12x more compute), reducing the complexities associated with moving the consumer fleet to a next-gen hardware and limiting hardware upgrade complexities to pre-HW4 vehicles," Gupta added.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

12 Month EPS

Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Micron. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Arm locks in CEO Rene Haas through 2033, ending Nvidia succession speculation
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Arm Holdings announced today that Chief Executive Officer Rene Haas has signed a new long-term agreement committing to lead the British chip designer through 2033, effectively taking one of the semiconductor industry's top executives out of contention for the vacant chief executive role at Nvidia.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

In a coordinated move announced alongside majority owner SoftBank Group, Arm also confirmed that Haas will assume the newly expanded role of Vice Chairman of SoftBank Group effective December 1, 2026. The dual announcement serves as an unmistakable signal from both Arm and SoftBank Chairman Masayoshi Son to quell intense market speculation that Nvidia might poach Haas to replace ousted co-founder Jensen Huang.

"I've never been more confident about Arm's future," Haas said in a statement accompanying the release. "I believe deeply in our people, our strategy and the opportunity ahead. I'm incredibly proud of what we're building and wholly committed to realizing Arm's full potential for many years to come."

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

The commitment comes just eleven days after Huang abruptly resigned from Nvidia on November 12 following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman under U.S. counterintelligence scrutiny over alleged Chinese intelligence ties and suspected AI chip diversion. In the days following Huang's departure, major financial outlets reported that Nvidia's board and executive search firm had sounded out Haas as a potential successor.

For Nvidia's board, led by newly appointed Chairman Harvey Jones, Haas represented a rare hybrid candidate capable of bridging the gap between an external turnaround hire and an internal culture fit. Before joining Arm in 2013 and taking its helm in February 2022, Haas spent seven years at Nvidia rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business. During his tenure at Arm, he steered the company through its 2023 Nasdaq initial public offering and positioned its processor architecture at the center of the global artificial intelligence boom, including supplying the designs behind Nvidia's own Grace data-center CPUs.

Story Continues

Reports that Nvidia was courting Haas had briefly rattled Arm investors, sending Arm shares tumbling earlier this month amid fears of a sudden leadership vacuum just as the company expands from licensing mobile designs into selling its own custom data-center chips. By locking Haas into a seven-year runway—which will keep the 64-year-old executive at the helm until age 71—and elevating him to Vice Chairman at SoftBank, the Japanese conglomerate has moved decisively to protect its most valuable asset and preserve stability across the broader chip ecosystem.

With Haas formally off the table, Nvidia's board faces a narrowed field as it navigates ongoing Securities and Exchange Commission inquiries, investor lawsuits, and internal employee petitions calling for Huang's return. The company's 10 independent directors must now weigh internal continuity options—such as interim CEO and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress or longtime CUDA software architect Ian Buck—against external semiconductor executives.

news.Title: Rocket Lab Just Raised Prices on a Rocket It Hasn't Launched Yet. Here's What That Means for SpaceX.
news.Content:
Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) reported earnings earlier this month, with $0.12 per share in losses, missing analyst targets -- but its positive GAAP operating cash flow , $268 million in revenue, and a big $1.2 billion boost to its backlog all exceeded expectations.

However, for space investors in general (if perhaps not Rocket Lab investors in particular), none of that was the biggest news.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Rocket Lab.

There's a launch crisis in space

For months we've been hearing that Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), the 800-lb. gorilla of rocket launch, is planning to retire its Falcon 9 rocket. For weeks, analysts have worried over what this means for space companies that depend on SpaceX (as the company is known for short) for its launch services:

If the Falcon 9 stops flying, how will AST SpaceMobile put its BlueBird satellites into orbit?

If the rocket stops flying, what will replenish Planet Labs ' Dove satellites when they fall out of service?

And how will NASA send astronauts to the International Space Station?

Not all hope is lost. Across the globe, rocket providers from Blue Origin to United Launch Alliance -- jointly owned by Boeing (NYSE:BA) and Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) -- to Arianespace are working frantically to get their own rockets, which are almost all currently grounded, but theoretically capable of duplicating the Falcon 9's performance, flying again. And not only these, but newer space companies are developing bigger rockets of their own that may be able to take on some of the missions previously flown by the Falcon 9.

In fact, Rocket Lab has one such rocket in the works itself: the Neutron.

Rocket Lab's Neutron: A solution to the launch problem?

As part of its earnings release on Nov. 9, Rocket Lab announced it won $515 million in Neutron rocket launch contracts in the third quarter from customers including SAR radar satellite operator Iceye, space data-center company Starcloud, and even the U.S. Space Force.

CEO Peter Beck said that Rocket Lab inked "nearly $1 billion of ... new launch contracts, signed in Q3 2026 alone," which means that more than half of the launch contracts his company signed in the quarter (by value) were Neutron contracts.

Neutron hasn't launched yet -- but its price is already rocketing higher

Story Continues

And even that's not the best news for the Neutron. More than a year after it was supposed to have its inaugural launch out of Wallops Island, Virginia, it still hasn't flown a single test flight. (Rocket Lab's latest estimate for a first flight date isn't until sometime next year). But no matter.

Demand for Neutron launches in particular is "huge," says Rocket Lab, with 16 missions booked already, and no new launch slots available for purchase until the 2030s.

And with launch capacity in such short supply, it seems satellite companies are now bidding up launch prices, even for rockets like the Neutron, which haven't yet proved they can fly. Rocket Lab originally intended to price Neutron launches around $55 million, significantly undercutting SpaceX's Falcon 9 on price. With Falcon 9 going away, however, there's no need to keep a lid on prices anymore.

And so Rocket Lab has raised the price on the Neutron by 27%, to $70 million per launch.

What it means for Rocket Lab, for SpaceX, and for everyone else

This is amazing news for Rocket Lab, assuming, of course, that it can get the Neutron off the launch pad and into orbit, generating revenue. But it's also potentially good news for other space companies.

Consider that if SpaceX rethinks retiring the Falcon 9 -- which, with a 22.8-ton payload to Low Earth Orbit, is nearly twice as capable as the Neutron will be -- it's likely the company could double its current launch price from $74 million to $140 million or even $150 million -- and the market would gladly pay that price. United Launch Alliance, Blue Origin, and Arianespace, too, all have a huge incentive to quickly resolve their technical issues and get their rockets flying again to cash in on the rich launch prices on offer.

Turns out, there's still a lot of money to be made in space.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

news.Title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Has Incredible News for Investors. Is This the Much-Needed Catalyst for the Stock?
news.Content:
Shares of Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) have fallen off a cliff in the second half of 2026, losing 60% of their value since the beginning of July following a tremendous start to the year.

The broader decline in the semiconductor sector is partially responsible for Intel's decline. However, it is worth noting that the pullback was exacerbated by the company's third-quarter results last month. Though Intel's revenue and earnings exceeded expectations, its Q4 guidance was well below what Wall Street was looking for.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, Intel stock showed signs of breaking out on Nov. 19 following remarks from CEO Lip-Bu Tan. Let's see what Tan said and check whether this development can bring Intel out of the rut it is in.

Image source: Intel.

Intel has won its first 18A foundry customer

CNBC reports that Intel's foundry division has won the first outside customer for chips manufactured on the 18A process node. Speaking at a business summit in Austin, Texas, Tan noted that the company has "just signed the first customer" for 18A. This could be a big deal for Intel, especially considering that the foundry market has been growing at an incredible pace due to artificial intelligence (AI)-fueled demand.

Foundry giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) has been winning big in the foundry market, driven by strong demand for its advanced process nodes used by leading chip designers to manufacture AI chips. TSMC has built a strong customer base that includes Nvidia , AMD , Qualcomm , Apple , Broadcom , Marvell Technology , and others.

This explains why TSMC's revenue has increased by 44% in the first 10 months of 2026. However, TSMC isn't able to meet the massive demand for AI chips, which explains why the company has been ramping up its capital expenditure. The Taiwan-based foundry giant is on track to spend $60 billion to $64 billion on capex this year, up from $40.9 billion in 2025. What's more, management notes that TSMC's capex between 2026 and 2028 will be significantly higher than in the past three years.

TSMC's forecast suggests a supply gap in the foundry space that needs to be filled. So, Intel's first external customer for the 18A process node is indeed a big deal, as it indicates the chipmaker can fill that gap. Wall Street analysts estimate that this new customer could be anyone, including Microsoft , Amazon , or Alphabet 's Google, cloud computing giants that are struggling to secure sufficient chip supply to meet demand.

Story Continues

Tom's Hardware reported last year that Intel's 18A could give TSMC's latest 2-nanometer (nm) process node serious competition. That won't be surprising, as the 18A process is essentially a 1.8nm node, which explains why it is anticipated to deliver stronger performance and compete with TSMC's 2nm node.

As such, Intel could gain more customers for 18A in the future, potentially setting the company up for stronger growth.

Why opportunistic investors can consider buying Intel right now

The sharp slide in Intel stock has made it attractive from a valuation perspective. It trades at 30 times forward earnings. Though that's a premium to the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's forward earnings multiple of 20, investors will do well to note that Intel's earnings are expected to jump by a whopping 254% in 2026.

Though analysts have reduced their earnings per share (EPS) growth expectations over the next couple of years, they still anticipate a significant acceleration in Intel's bottom line in 2028.

INTC EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

The company's foray into the foundry market and the potential addition of new external customers should pave the way for Intel to beat analysts' earnings growth expectations, providing the stock with a much-needed catalyst. But even if Intel's EPS reaches $2.99 in 2028 and it continues to trade at 30 times earnings, the stock price could jump to $90.

That signifies a potential 76% upside in just over two years, which is why savvy investors looking for a beaten-down growth stock that could go on a bull run may consider buying Intel following its recent slide.

news.Title: McDonald's (MCD) Has Raised Its Dividend 50 Straight Years. I'd Buy It in November and Never Sell.
news.Content:
On Nov. 4, McDonald's (NYSE: MCD) released its third-quarter earnings report, featuring global systemwide sales rising 4% year over year to more than $38 billion and adjusted operating income rising 8%. Many people pay close attention to companies' quarterly reports, but some might have missed another noteworthy announcement from McDonald's in September. It declared an upcoming 4% dividend increase, from $1.86 per share per quarter to $1.93.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

That dividend increase was an especially big deal because it marked McDonald's 50th consecutive annual dividend increase. That's quite impressive, as it means that throughout all kinds of economic ups and downs and all kinds of market crashes and recoveries, McDonald's just kept paying -- and increasing -- its dividend.

Companies that hike their payouts for 50 years in a row are dubbed " Dividend Kings ," and they're in elite company. As of Nov. 3, there were only about 59 such companies, including Procter & Gamble (with 70 consecutive years of increases), Coca-Cola (64), and Lowe's (64).

Should you invest in McDonald's?

When I'm looking for investments, any company that qualifies as a Dividend King would get extra consideration. In order to become a Dividend King, a company must have been around for decades, and must have been doing well enough to be able to sustain (and raise) a dividend for a long time. Much can change in a society over 50 years, too -- just think back to 1976, if you can. A Dividend King must have successfully implemented its strategies and pivoted when necessary, adapting to changing circumstances.

That said, each company is different. So here are some reasons why I'd consider investing in McDonald's -- either now or within the coming months:

Its business model is attractive -- and unusual. You might think that, with its 45,000-plus locations dishing out burgers and nuggets and fries, it's essentially a fast-food operation. It is that, but it's also a real estate titan. About 95% of its restaurants are franchisee-owned and operated, but McDonald's owns most of the land and buildings, charging its franchisees rent.

It's focused on growth, aiming to reach 50,000 restaurants by the end of 2028.

It's also rolling out a new value menu, offering customers a "clear and compelling" value proposition.

That dividend recently yielded 2.83% -- and when you add in the effect of stock repurchases, the total yield for shareholders rises to nearly 4%.

The stock's valuation is reasonable, with a price-to-sales ratio of 7, well below the five-year average of 8, and a forward-looking price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 19.9, below the five-year average of 23.5.

Story Continues

So give McDonald's some consideration for your long-term portfolio. You might buy a few shares now, wait for an even more attractive entry point, or simply pass. It's working on beefing up its performance, and it will pay you to wait for it to happen. The company may very well be rewarding shareholders 50 years from now, too.

news.Title: Premarket movers: Chip stocks lead AI rebound; CrowdStrike falls
news.Content:
nvesting.com - U.S. stock index futures rallied on Monday, as investors stepped in to buy beaten-down technology shares following a bruising week on Wall Street that pushed all three major equity benchmarks into correction territory. A sharp rebound in semiconductor and artificial intelligence-related stocks helped lift sentiment, while a major cybersecurity acquisition added to the premarket activity.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

By 05:23 ET (10:23 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures had surged 882 points, or 3.5%, while S&P 500 futures climbed 190 points, or 2.1%. Dow Jones futures advanced 929 points, or 1.9%.

Chipmakers led the recovery, with Nvidia shares jumping 8.7% in premarket trading, rebounding from their longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Advanced Micro Devices gained 5.8%, Broadcom rose 5.7%, and Micron Technology advanced 7%.

The rally extended across the semiconductor supply chain. Lam Research and Marvell Technology each climbed more than 7%, while SK Hynix's U.S.-listed shares gained nearly 10%. Intel, Applied Materials and AMD rose more than 6% at one point, while SanDisk and Seagate Technology advanced 7.8% and 6.8%, respectively.

AI infrastructure and data center stocks also staged a strong recovery. Nvidia-backed neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius Group jumped 10.1% and 11.1%, respectively, while IREN gained 10.2%. Applied Digital advanced 9.8% and Core Scientific rose 8%.

The gains followed a difficult stretch for technology stocks, with investors reassessing valuations and the scale of spending required to sustain the AI boom. Nvidia's recent leadership turmoil had added to uncertainty surrounding the chipmaker, but Monday's rebound suggested investors were looking to capitalize on the sector's steep losses.

Newly listed AI developer Anthropic also rose 4.5%, recovering after its shares fell 8.5% on Friday amid the broader market selloff. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its initial public offering, alongside another $26 billion from technology companies that purchased shares at the offering price. Its market debut has given investors a closely watched public-market gauge of sentiment toward the AI industry.

In a major development for the cybersecurity sector, CrowdStrike announced an agreement to acquire rival Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valuing the company at approximately $43.9 billion.

Story Continues

Zscaler shares jumped more than 13% in premarket trading, while CrowdStrike fell over 8% as investors assessed the terms and strategic implications of the deal.

Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share held, implying a value of $260.41 per Zscaler share, a premium of approximately 34% to its previous closing price.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

The combination would bring CrowdStrike's endpoint security capabilities together with Zscaler's network security platform, expanding the range of protection businesses can obtain from a single provider.

The deal comes as companies face growing cybersecurity risks from the rapid adoption of AI, which can help attackers identify software vulnerabilities and exploit weaknesses more quickly. Recent technology outages and vulnerabilities affecting widely used Java and PHP software have further heightened concerns about corporate network security.

Elsewhere, Capricor Therapeutics shares plunged 69.5% in premarket trading to $2.32 after the FDA rejected the company's investigational cell therapy, deramiocel, for Duchenne muscular dystrophy for a second time in less than two years.

The agency issued a Complete Response Letter on Friday, saying the data submitted in support of the application were insufficient to establish the treatment's effectiveness. The FDA also identified serious data-integrity concerns in the HOPE-3 trial, including unauthorized changes to statistical analyses and breaches of trial blinding, which it said could not be corrected retrospectively.

VNET Group shares gained 8.7% after the China-based data center operator reported third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted EBITDA beating analyst expectations.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 21.7% year over year to RMB923.1 million, exceeding the RMB890.9 million consensus. Its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 31.1% from 29.4% a year earlier, while its net loss attributable to shareholders narrowed 73% to RMB83.1 million.

The company also authorized up to $50 million in American depositary share repurchases, providing another boost to investor sentiment.

Enphase Energy shares rose 4.9% to $20.60, recovering from a 52-week low of $19.47 reached last Thursday. The move came without a fresh company-specific catalyst, with the broader market rebound providing the main support.

Investors were also weighing the company's recently announced restructuring plan, which calls for reducing its workforce by approximately 12%, or around 320 employees, and relocating certain functions to lower-cost regions. The changes are aimed at aligning its cost structure with current market conditions while preserving investment in future growth.

Texas Instruments shares advanced 4.5% after Cantor Fitzgerald upgraded the semiconductor maker to Overweight from Neutral and raised its price target to $385 from $340.

The upgrade followed a period of weakness for the stock, which fell more than 5% on Nov. 20 amid concerns about demand in the analog semiconductor market and margin pressure from elevated capital expenditure. Cantor's more positive stance provided a fresh catalyst for the shares as chipmakers broadly rebounded.

Monday's gains offered some relief after a difficult week for Wall Street, with technology and AI-related stocks leading the recovery. However, the sharp divergence between Zscaler and CrowdStrike, alongside Capricor's steep decline, highlighted how company-specific developments continued to drive substantial moves beneath the broader market rebound.

news.Title: ETFs to Benefit as U.S. Approves AI Chip Exports to China
news.Content:
The U.S. decision to permit the export of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips to selected Chinese companies has reopened an important growth opportunity for American semiconductor manufacturers. However, the move also raises questions about national security, technological competition and the future direction of U.S.-China trade relations.

The latest disclosure of export licenses by the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee highlights the scale of potential demand from China. On Nov. 19, 2026, the committee revealed that the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) had approved more than 879,000 AI chip export requests between December 2025 and May 2026, out of applications covering approximately 3.4 million chips.

The approvals involved advanced processors from NVIDIA NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices AMD, including NVIDIA's H200 and AMD's MI325X. Some licenses covered Chinese companies such as Alibaba BABA and Tencent TCEHY, which have been designated by the U.S. Department of Defense as Chinese Military Companies. However, the approval does not necessarily mean that the chips were shipped or delivered.

Background of U.S. Chip Export Restrictions

The United States has restricted China's access to advanced semiconductor technology since October 2022, when the Biden administration introduced export controls on high-performance computing chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The objective was to prevent China from using advanced American technology to strengthen its military capabilities and accelerate the development of sophisticated AI systems.

These restrictions created a significant challenge for U.S. chipmakers, particularly NVIDIA and AMD, which had historically viewed China as an important market for their data center processors. In response, manufacturers developed modified versions of their processors that could comply with U.S. export requirements.

What Is the New AI Chip Export Policy?

The Trump administration adopted a more flexible approach in December 2025, allowing NVIDIA to sell H200 chips to approved Chinese customers under strict conditions. In January 2026, the Commerce Department shifted to case-by-case reviews for NVIDIA's H200, AMD's MI325X and comparable processors.

Exporters must ensure adequate security checks, protect U.S. chip supplies and submit chips for independent testing. The policy aims to balance national security with revenue opportunities for U.S. chipmakers, although it is facing growing congressional opposition.

Story Continues

Why is the Latest Approval Attracting Attention?

The approval of more than 879,000 AI chips has intensified congressional scrutiny because some licenses involved Chinese companies that Washington considers to have potential military connections.

According to the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the applications included 75,000 chips for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent and 43,000 for Baidu BIDU, per Business Standard.

The administration has also introduced fresh restrictions on overseas data centers. An interim rule published requires additional licensing and due diligence when advanced U.S. computing technology is exported to certain overseas facilities that provide substantial computing capacity to Chinese entities. It also expands licensing requirements for advanced semiconductor exports to selected countries, including Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

This suggests that the United States is not necessarily abandoning its export-control strategy. Instead, it is attempting to allow selected commercial transactions while tightening oversight of the ultimate users of American AI technology.

ETFs in Focus

NVDA and AMD-Heavy ETFs

Since NVDA and AMD are prominent chip exporters, they are likely to benefit from the move. This will impact their corresponding ETFs that have a high weightage of the respective stocks.

Investors might look at Strive U.S. Semiconductor ETF SHOC, with 19.30% exposure to NVDA, and AOT Growth and Innovation ETF AOTG, with 15.47% exposure to AMD in its portfolio.

ETFs Associated With Chinese Technology

Chinese companies like Alibaba and Tencent receiving export approvals could also benefit if they obtain access to advanced AI processors. These companies are investing in large language models, AI-powered applications and cloud computing services.

Investors might watch KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF KWEB, which provides exposure to Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu. Alibaba and Tencent represented approximately 8% and 9.62% of its portfolio, respectively. Invesco China Technology ETF CQQQ offers exposure to Tencent (10.31%) and Baidu (6.16%).

news.Title: Black Friday Stock Deals: 4 Great Stocks Down 30% or More
news.Content:
Black Friday is the one time of year when most people get excited about buying things on sale. Oddly enough, that excitement rarely extends to the stock market, where investors tend to get nervous when prices fall.

This year, there are plenty of discounts to choose from. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% on Nov. 5 alone and briefly closed nearly 12% below its October record. It has been choppy since, and many individual stocks are still well below their highs. Here are four great businesses on sale for 30% or more below their recent highs.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

1. SoFi Technologies

As a SoFi Technologies (NASDAQ:SOFI) shareholder, I've watched the stock fall nearly 40% this year and roughly half from its late-2025 peak. But you'd never know it was under so much pressure by how the business is performing. In the third quarter, adjusted net revenue rose 44% to a record $1.37 billion, members grew 35% to 17.1 million, and management introduced a 2027 outlook calling for $0.90 of earnings per share. SoFi has been doing an excellent job of increasing its cross-selling rate, getting members to deepen their relationships, and this strategy could pay off nicely in the long run.

2. Zscaler

Zscaler (NASDAQ:ZS) got caught up in a sell-off of cybersecurity stocks that began with Fortinet's report in late October. It currently trades roughly 35% below its 52-week high. Meanwhile, its most recent quarter showed 25% growth in both revenue and annual recurring revenue (ARR). At around 40 times forward earnings, it isn't cheap, but that's well below its usual valuation . I own Zscaler, and its Dec. 2 report is the next test. But cybersecurity is an increasing need as agentic AI evolves, and this trend isn't likely to reverse anytime soon.

3. MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI), Latin America's leading e-commerce and fintech company, hit a new 52-week low on Nov. 5 after its third-quarter profit missed estimates. It recently traded at about $1,420, roughly 40% below its 52-week high. The miss came from spending on shipping, warehouses, and marketing, with the stock selling off even though revenue grew 45% to $10.75 billion. After the drop, the stock trades for less than 35 times forward earnings, well below its five-year average of about 63. I own MercadoLibre, and I think this spending will pay off in a bigger, stickier customer base.

Story Continues

4. Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) has been one of the most volatile space stocks this year. It recently traded around $53, about 65% below its 52-week high. That's hard to square with its latest quarter, which looked extremely strong overall. Revenue rose 73% to a record $268 million, and backlog jumped 52% in a single quarter to $3.57 billion, including more than $515 million of orders for its Neutron rocket before it has even flown. Neutron's first launch has slipped to 2027, and the stock still carries a premium valuation, so this is a higher-risk pick. But if Rocket Lab can execute on its long-term strategy, it could be a massive winner for patient investors.

To be sure, there's a reason each of these stocks is down. SoFi and Robinhood depend on consumer credit and trading activity; Zscaler faces tough competition; MercadoLibre's heavy spending is squeezing its margins; and Rocket Lab still has to prove that Neutron can fly on schedule.

Having said all that, I'd much rather shop for great businesses when they're 30% off than when they're priced for perfection. I'm adding to the three I own this holiday season, and I'd keep the other two on a watch list for a smaller, longer-term position.

news.Title: Texas Instruments vs. Lam Research: Which Chip Stock Is a Better Buy?
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two prominent U.S. semiconductor companies benefiting from the growing demand for chips. While Texas Instruments specializes in analog and embedded processing chips used across industrial, automotive and data center markets, Lam Research supplies wafer fabrication equipment that helps chipmakers manufacture advanced semiconductors.

Both companies are benefiting from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom and improving semiconductor demand. However, their growth drivers and business models are different. Lam Research is gaining from rising investments in semiconductor manufacturing capacity, while Texas Instruments is benefiting from stronger demand across several end markets and its expanding manufacturing capabilities.

With both companies reporting strong September-quarter results, investors may wonder which stock offers a better investment opportunity at present. Let's compare their latest financial performance, growth prospects and valuations to determine which semiconductor stock makes for a better investment option.

Broad-Based Recovery and Data Center Support TXN Prospects

Texas Instruments delivered a strong third-quarter 2026 performance, reflecting improving demand across its major end markets. Revenues increased 28% year over year to $6.06 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) surged 77% to $2.62. Operating profit jumped 73% to $2.87 billion, highlighting the benefits of higher sales and improved operating leverage.

Texas Instruments Incorporated Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Texas Instruments Incorporated price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Texas Instruments Incorporated Quote

A major growth driver was the recovery in industrial and automotive markets, alongside strong demand from data centers. Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year, while automotive revenues grew in the mid-teens. The data center business was another standout performer, with revenues surging approximately 95% year over year and 20% sequentially.

Data centers are becoming increasingly important for Texas Instruments. The company's analog and embedded chips support power management, connectivity and other essential functions in AI infrastructure. As data centers expand and require more power-efficient systems, demand for these chips is likely to increase.

Texas Instruments is also benefiting from its long-term manufacturing investments. Its 300-millimeter wafer production strategy is expected to support lower manufacturing costs and improve profitability as production volumes increase. During the last earnings call, management highlighted that the company's manufacturing capacity, broad product portfolio and customer relationships position it well to capture rising demand.

Story Continues

The company's cash generation is another positive. Operating cash flow reached $9.9 billion over the trailing 12 months, up 43% year over year. Free cash flow climbed to $8.42 billion from $2.42 billion a year ago. The company also returned $5.8 billion to shareholders over the past 12 months.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Texas Instruments expects revenues of $5.80-$6.30 billion and EPS of $2.45-$2.79. Management also indicated that demand remains strong across industrial, automotive and data center markets. The company is investing in manufacturing capacity to support future growth. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates year-over-year growth of 26.4% and 65%, respectively. These estimates reflect expectations of sustained recovery across its major markets and increasing contributions from data center demand.

AI-Driven Equipment Demand Fuels Strong Growth for LRCX

Lam Research is benefiting directly from increasing investments in semiconductor manufacturing equipment as chipmakers expand capacity to meet AI-related demand. Its deposition and etch technologies are essential for manufacturing advanced chips, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and increasingly complex semiconductor devices.

The company delivered an exceptional first-quarter fiscal 2027 performance. Revenues surged 54.4% year over year to $8.22 billion compared with $5.32 billion in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP EPS increased approximately 75% to $2.20 from $1.26. Profitability also improved significantly. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.4% from 50.6% a year ago, while non-GAAP operating margin increased to 40.2% from 35%. These results reflect strong demand, favorable product mix and operational execution.

Lam Research's Systems business remains a key growth driver. Systems revenues increased to $5.73 billion from $3.55 billion in the year-ago quarter. Customer Support Business Group (CSBG) revenues rose to $2.49 billion from $1.78 billion. The CSBG business provides a relatively stable revenue stream through services, spare parts and equipment upgrades.

Lam Research Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote

AI is creating significant opportunities for Lam Research across DRAM, NAND and advanced foundry markets. Increasing demand for HBM and advanced packaging requires more sophisticated manufacturing processes, boosting the need for deposition and etch equipment.

During its latest earnings call, management highlighted that wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending is expected to reach the mid-$150 billion range in calendar 2026. The company's preliminary outlook projects wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027. DRAM is expected to lead growth, followed by leading-edge foundry logic and NAND.

Lam Research expects its calendar 2026 systems revenues to grow well over 40% year over year. Management also believes that increasing device complexity, greater deposition and etch intensity, and market-share gains will help the company outperform the broader WFE market.

For the December 2026 quarter, Lam Research expects revenues of $8.60 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, operating margin of 40.5% and EPS of $2.33. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 revenues and non-GAAP EPS indicates year-over-year growth of 49.9% and 65.2%, respectively. These projections highlight Lam Research's stronger near-term growth potential compared with Texas Instruments.

However, Lam Research faces certain risks. Semiconductor equipment spending can be cyclical, and changes in customer investment plans can affect revenue growth. Its business is also exposed to export controls, geopolitical developments and supply-chain constraints. During the first-quarter earnings call, management specifically acknowledged that clean-room availability and component supply constraints could limit the industry's ability to meet end demand.

TXN vs. LRCX: Valuation and Stock Performance Comparison

Both stocks have strong growth prospects, but their valuations and recent share-price performances tell a different story.

Texas Instruments currently trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 23.86 compared with 17.44 for Lam Research. Thus, Lam Research is cheaper on this particular valuation measure despite having a higher revenue growth expectation.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, the valuation difference should be considered alongside the companies' business models and earnings visibility. Lam Research's higher expected growth is closely tied to the current semiconductor equipment investment cycle. Any slowdown in customer spending could affect its financial performance.

Texas Instruments, meanwhile, has exposure to several end markets, including industrial, automotive and data centers. Its manufacturing investments and strong cash generation also provide support for long-term growth.

Stock performance is another important consideration. Texas Instruments has gained 52% year to date, significantly outperforming Lam Research's 7.1% growth. Despite its stronger share-price performance, TXN's forward P/E multiple remains relatively moderate.

Conclusion: Texas Instruments Seems a Better Buy Right Now

Both Texas Instruments and Lam Research are well positioned to benefit from the long-term growth of the semiconductor industry and rising AI infrastructure investments. Lam Research offers stronger near-term revenue growth and benefits directly from increasing investments in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its lower forward P/E multiple also makes its valuation attractive relative to Texas Instruments.

However, Texas Instruments appears to offer a more balanced investment proposition. Its strong recovery across industrial and automotive markets, rapidly growing data center business and improving cash generation provide multiple avenues for growth. Its manufacturing investments should also support long-term cost efficiency and profitability.

Texas Instruments has significantly outperformed Lam Research in 2026, demonstrating stronger share price momentum. Although TXN trades at a higher forward P/E multiple, its diversified end-market exposure, strong free cash flow and manufacturing advantages offer investors a compelling combination of growth and business stability.

Texas Instruments appears to be the stronger choice for investors seeking exposure to the semiconductor industry's long-term growth through a more diversified revenue base.

Currently, Texas Instruments carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), making it a must-pick compared with Lam Research, which has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Content:
面對台股交易結構年輕化、小額投資日益普及，加上網路與人工智慧（AI）投資訊息真偽難辨，台灣證券交易所今（23）日正式啟用「證好學 TWSE Academy」投資人教育平台（網址： academy.twse.com.tw ）。

平台取「正好學」諧音，象徵「現在開始學習，正好」，將原本每年觸及逾2,500萬人次的宣導資源全面整合升級，針對校園、職場、家庭與樂齡四大人生階段量身規劃課程，並結合短影音、時事解析與專家對談，協助民眾在資訊爆炸時代建立正確的風險評估能力。

零股與ETF交易比重雙雙攀升　李愛玲：別被AI幻覺誤導

台股散戶參與度持續提高，讓投資人識讀教育更顯迫切。證交所總經理李愛玲在發表會上引用最新市場數據指出，零股交易占大盤成交值比重已從去年全年平均的2.08%，大幅躍升至今年10月單月的4.6%；同期ETF成交值占比也由去年平均的7.2%走高至今年10月的8.5%，顯示越來越多國人以小額、被動式商品切入資本市場。

李愛玲坦言，自己平時遇有疑問也會使用AI查詢，但AI雖然便利卻可能產生幻覺與資訊混淆，投資人必須具備辨識資訊真偽的能力。她強調，證交所推出「證好學」平台肩負重要的企業社會責任，目的是提供單一、權威且值得信賴的學習管道，協助民眾釐清商品風險，落實「投資而非投機」。

高晶萍盼建立財務防禦力　短影音取代生硬公開說明書

金管會證期局局長高晶萍致詞時指出，金融教育的第一步「不是教大家一夜致富，而是幫大家建立財務防禦力」，讓民眾深刻理解風險與報酬的對價關係，以及天下沒有白吃的午餐。

她透露，數月前與證交所高層開會時，便針對股市熱絡下詐騙頻傳的現象交換意見，促使周邊單位積極強化投資人教育，讓新平台在不到一季內火速上線，這也是響應金管會「金融大回饋」政策的具體行動。

考量傳統公開說明書內容較為枯燥生硬，「證好學」集結產官學界及中華民國證券商業同業公會、中華民國證券投資信託暨顧問商業同業公會兩大公會的專業資源，改以短影音、圖文與專業主持人深度對談的形式宣導，並延續保留前身「宅在家學習網」的圖文精華，讓正確知識跑在錯誤訊息前面，隨時幫助投資人線上學習、內化知識並識破詐騙陷阱。

news.Title: US futures rally as AI selloff pauses, Asian authorities support stocks
news.Content:
(Refiles to change story tag, no changes to text)

By Danilo Masoni and Tom Westbrook

MILAN/SINGAPORE, Nov 23 (Reuters) - US stock futures rose sharply on Monday as authorities in Asia moved to support markets after last week's AI-linked stock wipeout sparked a global selloff in riskier assets.

Nasdaq 100 ‌futures bounced 3.5% by 1200 GMT and S&P 500 futures added 2.8%, while Europe's region-wide STOXX 600 gained 0.8%, led by semiconductor and other technology stocks.

Investors ‌are questioning whether the vast sums of money being spent on AI data centres will generate enough profit to justify the investments.

Concerns over tighter US Federal Reserve policy, a leadership crisis at Nvidia ​and a potential slowdown in AI-related spending after the US midterms added to the pressure.

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its biggest decline since the March 2020 pandemic-driven selloff, while volatility pushed Wall Street's so-called fear gauge above 40 for the first time since April 2025.

Deutsche Bank strategist Jim Reid said fears surrounding the AI trade had spread into a broader risk-off, prompting investors globally to seek liquidity.

"This was no longer simply a tech selloff," he wrote.

The fall in Taiwan's chipmaker-heavy benchmark last week was ‌the biggest since 1990, while European shares, which are less ⁠exposed to tech stocks, posted their worst weekly performance in almost eight months.

Taiwan stocks rose 2.4% on Monday, with government support helping to stabilise the market, and although the rout deepened for South Korea's KOSPI, the index came off 10-month lows to trade ⁠down by about 3.3%.

The KOSPI was global equities' leading light in the first half of this year, as bets on chip demand more than doubled the index's value in six months.

Following the selloff, the index has halved from its peak, and South Korea's finance minister reiterated on Monday plans to stabilise the market if necessary.

Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of ​short-selling ​rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such ​as easing requirements for margin financing.

Japanese markets were closed for a ‌holiday on Monday but futures indicated selling pressure, while markets in Hong Kong and mainland China sank to new multi-month lows.

Safe-haven demand, meanwhile, eased after Friday's surge into bonds and the dollar.

US 10-year Treasury yields added 4.6 basis points to 4.95% and their German equivalents, the benchmark for the euro zone, were steady at 3.30%.

Story Continues

AI TRADE TURNS

For about four years since the launch of chatbot ChatGPT, the "AI trade" has lifted a wide range of stocks, from chipmakers to switch and cable makers to electricity generators, on the assumption of explosive growth in computing demand.

According to analysts, AI spending is staying solid, with Morgan Stanley forecasting a rise next year in hyperscaler ‌capital expenditure of more than 70% to top $1.6 trillion.

But the mood in the market has shifted ​drastically.

The exit of Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO nicknamed the "godfather of AI", has called the chipmaker's ​strategy of financing some of its customers into question.

The faltering debut of AI ​leader Anthropic, which on Friday closed 8.5% lower on its first full day of trading, showed traders turning fickle.

The next test, besides ‌the price performance of US markets this week, will be ​the results and outlook from computer maker Dell ​on Tuesday and, next month, whether the Fed raises interest rates as investors expect.

The US dollar stayed below Friday's 19-month highs against a basket of currencies as last week's selloff prompted traders to scale back expectations for an aggressive US rate hike next month. The dollar index was broadly unchanged ​at 103.9.

That also helped gold regain some ground and ‌trade up 2.5% at $3,620 per ounce. Bitcoin was up 0.7%.

Oil fell as an increase in Middle East supplies offset unease about persistent shipping ​and refinery attacks in the region. Brent was down 1.3% to $91.3 a barrel.

(Reporting by Tom Westbrook and Danilo Masoni; Additional reporting by Liang-sa ​Loh in Taipei; Editing by Jacqueline Wong, Jamie Freed, Xevi Fontdegloria and Alexander Smith)

news.Title: Anthropic Just Rewrote Wall Street's IPO Record Books. Here's Where History Says Its Shares Will Head Next.
news.Content:
On June 12, Elon Musk's Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), better known as SpaceX, shattered Wall Street's record books with a $75 billion capital raise from its initial public offering (IPO) . A little over five months later, on Nov. 19, the developer of the Claude large language model, Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), booted SpaceX from its pedestal.

Anthropic sold approximately 980 million shares at $83, raising a record $81.3 billion, which may soar to as much as $107 billion once the underwriters' overallotment is accounted for.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

It's not hard to understand why investors are so excited for Anthropic's debut. The company's sales soared to roughly $17 billion in the third quarter, with annual run rate revenue reaching about $81 billion. It's one of the fastest-growing artificial intelligence (AI) companies and is central to the AI build-out.

But it's also far from a slam-dunk investment . According to history, it's pretty clear where shares of Anthropic will head next.

History offers a disappointing outlook for Wall Street's hottest IPO

While past events can't concretely predict the future, history has, more often than not, accurately foreshadowed what's to come on Wall Street. When it comes to Wall Street's most hyped IPOs, history says that piling in early is rarely, if ever, a good idea.

In the weeks leading up to SpaceX's IPO, the analysts at Truist Financial (NYSE:TFC) published a data set to X (formerly Twitter) that examined the performance of 30 of the most hyped tech-driven IPOs since the debut of Facebook (now Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META)) in May 2012.

On the surface, the data isn't terrifying, with 43% of the 30 IPOs higher at the six- and 12-month marks. However, the column on maximum year-one drawdowns points to trouble ahead for Anthropic.

According to Truist, the average year-one drawdown for the hottest tech-focused IPOs is 55% over 14 years. This indicates that retail investor hype for game-changing IPOs quickly fades, leaving those investors with potentially steep peak-to-trough losses within the first year of a company going public.

Interestingly enough, SpaceX's maximum drawdown thus far is 54%, which is more or less in line with the historical average.

Story Continues

If Anthropic were to align with this average year-one maximum drawdown, its share price would be expected to drop from an intraday high of $115.10 on Nov. 19 to just below $52.

But wait -- there's more

In addition to Wall Street's most anticipated IPOs stumbling out of the starting gate, the stock market's two record-breaking debuts of 2026 are also, arguably, fleecing retail investors.

SpaceX's prospectus outlined a staggered and accelerated share-unlock schedule for its insiders (high-ranking executives, board members, and early investors), allowing them to cash out at the expense of retail investors.

Anthropic revealed a similar insider lockup schedule, but took things a step further. Amid the 23 separate events in which select insiders are eligible to sell some of their shares, Anthropic allowed some of its insiders to cash out on its debut day !

Given Truist's data set and the expectation of weak early returns for hyped IPOs, an accelerated share-unlock schedule that repeatedly balloons Anthropic's float is a disaster in the making for retail investors.

news.Title: 台股跌完了嗎？ 法人曝還有這兩個關卡要過
news.Content:
台股在金管會祭出第三波限空、一連串的穩定股市方案抒緩市場恐慌情緒、美國總統川普力挺黃仁勳回任輝達（NVIDIA）執行長、及美國財政部長貝森特的態度也出現偏向中性的轉折，諸多因素推升大盤指數反彈收高，為台股重挫以來第1根帶量長紅，市場關心，台股跌完了嗎？法人則是強調，不會以第1根大紅K當底部，後續還要看12月上旬的兩道關卡能不能平安度過。

台股23日強力反彈，盤中最低下探35,442.41點，隨後買盤進場推升指數，最高衝上37,108.2點，盤中高低震盪逾1,600點，終場以36,811.89點收盤，上漲778.6點，漲幅2.16%；上市、上櫃合計上漲家數1,300家、下跌634家，漲停68家、跌停16家。

台股這波下跌，指數急挫9,082.83點，23日的反彈， 到底是不是底部？台股跌完了嗎？第一金投顧董事長黃詣庭表示，台股反彈的因素有兩點，一是金管會第三波限空令，及穩定股市方案的實施，抒解市場上的恐慌情緒；二是美國總統川普力挺黃仁勳回任， 呼籲輝達董事會應重新聘任黃仁勳。

美國財政部長貝森特對中國大陸的態度也有轉折，先前強調攻擊美國商務部的態度轉偏中性；另外，他曾公開說過，輝達的執行長需從外部尋找，近期更在接受訪問時表示，「黃仁勳現在已是外部人士」；兩人的態度激勵美股NASDAQ期貨反彈，台股也隨著走升。

黃詣庭指出，不會以第1根大紅K當成底部，後續仍需觀察，在基本面的部分，首先今日低點不能跌破，其次是若出現連續下影線，代表下檔有支撐，另外則是有帶量紅K或是帶量跳空，都是觀察的重點。

黃詣庭強調， 面對5日線反壓，若能帶量攻上，大盤可望再往年線39,451點前進，若能站上年線，後市將會更穩固，以現階段到年底來觀察，季線將 比較大的壓力帶；另外， 12月初黃仁勳的國會聽證會及12/9的FED升息及對之後的看法，則是兩個重要的關卡。

黃詣庭認為，這兩個時間點若能平安度過，可視為底部出現；至於最近1~2個交易日如果未破今日盤中低點，可採反彈操作，第一階段鎖 大型權值股及市值ETF；另外，嚴重超跌的個股，則要考慮其基本面， 若沒有疑慮，可適度承接。

The S&P 500 fell 8.6% last week, its worst week since the April 2025 tariff turmoil. The PHLX Semiconductor Index lost about 17% over the week, and Nvidia shares sank nearly 23%.

news.Title: 台股反彈是逃命波！陳嘉偉喊「初跌段都沒走完」 預言明年OpenAI倒閉
news.Content:
台股23日迎來止跌反彈，市場盛傳美國財政部長貝森特受訪言論暗示黃仁勳有望重返輝達，激勵多頭士氣。然而證券分析師陳嘉偉在節目直言，此波反彈僅是「假利多」帶動的逃命波，指數翻紅反而提供平盤上放空的切入點；他並對照2008年金融海嘯走勢，預警台股連大循環「初跌段」都尚未走完，更點出AI新雲端算力中心正面臨「以債養債」斷鏈危機，預言明年全球將爆發資料中心倒閉潮，甚至連OpenAI也難逃倒閉命運。

駁斥黃仁勳回歸傳聞 喻如「63歲喬丹重返公牛」權力已遭架空

針對早盤傳出美媒專訪貝森特提及「黃仁勳現在也是外部人士」、引發黃仁勳可能重返輝達的聯想，陳嘉偉駁斥這是完全不可能的假消息，並認為此舉與10月5日傳出「台積電攜手馬斯克德州設廠」拉高出貨的手法如出一轍。他以與黃仁勳同日出生的籃球巨星Michael Jordan為例，指出即便黃仁勳真的回歸，過去一人決策的權力也早已被董事會剝奪，如同找現年63歲的喬丹重返公牛隊打球般根本無法扭轉局勢；在金管會「限空令3.0」平盤下禁空規範下，指數反彈翻紅反而是絕佳放空時機。

對照2008海嘯走勢拒絕翻多 點名櫃買五年線反彈後恐再破底

回顧11月2日台積電季線正式下彎後，陳嘉偉曾參考過去川普關稅戰與俄烏戰爭跌幅，推算加權指數對應低點為33,678點與26,882點，而上週五夜盤期貨最低已殺至33,719點，距離首波目標僅差約40點。面對市場詢問是否已達滿足點，他將當前盤勢對照民國97年（2008年）大盤自9,859點跌至7,384點的歷史軌跡，指出33,719點僅相當於當年的中繼低點7,664點，當年櫃買指數同樣回測五年線後再度破底；以波浪理論位階來看，目前台股甚至連「初跌段」都尚未走完，後續還將迎來跌勢更劇烈的「主跌段」與「末跌段」。

原物料重挫定價經濟衰退 揭新雲端算力「以債養債」斷鏈危機

陳嘉偉形容本波修正是結合亞洲金融風暴、網路泡沫、金融海嘯與歐債危機的「完美風暴」，指出近期布蘭特原油、銅、黃金、白銀與比特幣同步走跌，反映市場已提前定價明年的經濟衰退。他進一步點出日本算力業者Datasection大幅下修明年財測九成的警訊，直言許多新雲端算力中心過去仰賴輝達資金與借貸「以債養債」採購台廠設備，如今受中國AI禁令衝擊導致客戶流失、營收斷鏈，連馬斯克舉債利率都逼近9%，高風險算力中心已難再取得銀行融資，預言明年全球將掀起資料中心倒閉潮，最終甚至連OpenAI也將走向倒閉。
